182273

Job Level:
Mid Level

Home District/Group:

Department:
Environmental

Market:
Transportation

Full Time

Position Overview

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers (KIE) has an immediate opening for an experienced Environmental Manager for either our Lone Tree, CO; Bellevue or Federal Way, WA; Lenexa, KS or Woodcliff Lake, NJ location. In this role, you will lead the environmental permitting for complex infrastructure projects across North America including very large design-build, progressive design-build (PDB), public-private partnerships (P3), and construction manager/general contractor (CM/GC) contracts. We seek a technical expert—someone with in-depth environmental planning experience that can be drawn upon to deliver pursuits and construction projects across North America. Experience coordinating with agencies such as State DOTs, FHWA, FRA, FTA, FAA, USACE, FERC, etc. is an integral part of this role.

District Overview

2025 ENR National Contractor Rankings #1 for Transportation and #3 Top 100 design build firms

Kiewit Infrastructure Engineers seamlessly transitions solutions from design to construction through the collaborative efforts of Design Engineering, Design Management, Proposals, Estimating, and Integrated Project Controls. Our construction-focused engineering approach involves a multidisciplinary team working together to maximize value for clients by improving schedules, controlling costs, and minimizing risk on infrastructure projects. This integrated strategy emphasizes collaboration and constructability throughout the project lifecycle, enabling us to identify and implement quality solutions with a strong safety focus.

Clients benefit from Kiewit’s proven processes and tools, which minimize project risk. As an in-house resource, we support projects across the company, in all major markets, sharing experiences, innovative concepts, and best practices. Kiewit’s management and implementation of this process results in safe, cost-effective, and innovative designs that exceed client expectations and uphold Kiewit’s legacy of excellence.

At Kiewit, we believe in building more than just structures – we build relationships, strengthen communities, and expand workforce capacity. We don't just build projects; we build careers. With top-notch health benefits, a wealth-building 401k plan (RRSP), and unbeatable growth opportunities, we are deeply invested in the future of our employees. Join us at Kiewit, where we go beyond construction to develop the ultimate road to success.

Location

This position can be based out of our Lone Tree, CO / Bellevue, WA / Federal Way, WA / Woodcliff Lake, NJ location.

Responsibilities

You will be responsible for overseeing and coordinating environmental permitting, reports, and technical documentation, as well as managing tasks and mentoring/leading others in the delivery of environmental products. You can expect to oversee junior staff working on multiple large-scale projects.

Tasks may include, but not limited to the following:

Technical

Collaboratively develop and implement strategy for delivering environmental components of our projects.
Review environmental documents, RFPs, and other documents to identify risk and scope.
Lead environmental planning and permitting processes and document preparation for transportation, transit, and infrastructure clients.
Serve as technical lead for a variety of infrastructure projects during conceptual planning and design through environmental approvals and permitting.
Develop documents that meet the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Section 4 (f) of the Department of Transportation Act , Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act , Section 401 and 404 of the Clean Water Act, and Sections 7 and 10 of the Endangered Species Act, and other applicable laws. This includes knowledge or ability to learn requirements and processes pursuant to state codes and municipal ordinance.
Create and/or perform quality reviews of environmental deliverables that meet client requirements and regulatory standards to ensure high-quality products are produced on time and within budget.
Perform quality reviews of other discipline’s engineering designs and plans to identify environmental constraints.

Management

Prepare and manage scope, schedule, and hours for a variety of environmental tasks for infrastructure projects.
Work with schedulers and estimators to incorporate environmental permit requirements into the project master schedule and budget.
Collaborate with transportation planning, engineering, urban design/landscape design, and other disciplines to determine compatibility of designs with environmentally sensitive areas.
Coordinate with clients, sub-consultants, and in-house personnel on a regular basis.
Establish and maintain professional relationships with all levels of internal and external agency personnel.
Support project communications and technical meetings, provide coordination to resolve design issues.
Lead environmental task force meetings to advance the pursuits and active design projects.
Provide guidance and support to less experienced staff on technical and professional matters.
This position may manage a junior-level direct report.

Qualifications

Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Planning, Environmental Planning, Life Sciences, Cultural Resources, Urban Design, Architecture, Landscape Architecture or another related field.
Minimum of 8 years of environmental planning experience in either transportation, land development or related projects.
Project Management and technical experience with design/planning projects on U.S. projects.
Ability to think strategically, adapt and innovate in accordance with project requirements and regulations.
Highly motivated, with a demonstrated passion for excellence and taking initiative and ownership.
Demonstrated commitment to ethics and integrity.
Strong work ethic, willing to put in the effort to get the job done right the first time.
Must have excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with individuals across teams and disciplines.
Team player with the ability to work independently to meet deadlines, goals and objectives.
Must have excellent organizational skills and data integrity/file management/version control experience.
Passion for safety – no one gets hurt.
Proficiency in Microsoft 365, exposure to or experience in utilizing AI to optimize tasks/workflows.
Regular, reliable attendance.

Preferred

Experience with U.S. infrastructure projects.
Design-Build project experience.
Experience developing construction plans for transportation projects.
This position includes occasional travel to project offices and work sites.

Other Requirements:

Regular, reliable attendance.
Work productively and meet deadlines
Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment.
Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.
Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.
May work at different locations, including active construction sites and conditions may vary.

Other Requirements:

Regular, reliable attendance
Work productively and meet deadlines timely
Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment
Perform work safely and effectively. Understand and follow oral and written instructions, including warning signs, equipment use, and other policies.
Work during normal operating hours to organize and complete work within given deadlines. Work overtime and weekends as required.
May work at various different locations and conditions may vary.

Base Compensation: $110,000/yr - $130,000/yr

(Actual compensation is subject to variation due to such factors as education, experience, skillset, and/or location)

This posting will be active from: 09/10/2026 - 12/31/2026

We offer our fulltime staff employees a comprehensive benefits package that’s among the best in our industry, including top-tier medical, dental and vision plans covering eligible employees and dependents, voluntary wellness and employee assistance programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with matching, and generous paid time off.

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Environmental Mine Closure Engineer, Specialist
jobs.description:
Responsabilidades Principales

Liderar el desarrollo y coordinación de estudios, planes e ingenierías de cierre de minas desde una etapa conceptual hasta la implementación.
Definir y evaluar estrategias, alternativas y medidas de cierre, y rehabilitación ambiental mediante una evaluación de riesgos.
Gestionar proyectos multidisciplinarios, asegurando el cumplimiento de los objetivos de seguridad, calidad, alcance, cronograma y presupuesto.
Actuar como referente técnico en temas de cierre de minas, proporcionando asesoría especializada a nuestros clientes, equipos internos y partes interesadas.
Liderar talleres técnicos, reuniones de coordinación y presentaciones ante clientes, autoridades regulatorias y otros actores relevantes.
Participar activamente en la preparación de propuestas técnicas y comerciales, desarrollar oportunidades de negocio y fortalecer relaciones con clientes.
Revisar y aprobar entregables técnicos, asegurando el cumplimiento de estándares corporativos, regulatorios y de calidad.
Guiar, supervisar y desarrollar técnicamente a profesionales junior e intermedios, promoviendo la transferencia de conocimiento y el crecimiento del equipo.
Colaborar con especialistas y equipos regionales y globales para impulsar la innovación y el desarrollo de la práctica de cierre de minas.

Requisitos

Título profesional en Ingeniería Ambiental, Ingeniería Civil, Ingeniería de Minas o disciplina afín.
Más de 10 años de experiencia profesional, incluyendo experiencia relevante en minería y cierre de minas.
Experiencia comprobada en planificación, diseño y desarrollo de planes de cierre de minas e ingenierías de cierre.
Experiencia en estudios de cierre a nivel conceptual, prefactibilidad, factibilidad y/o ingeniería de detalle.
Experiencia en gestión de proyectos y coordinación de equipos multidisciplinarios.
Conocimiento sólido de la normativa minera y ambiental en Chile, así como de estándares y buenas prácticas internacionales aplicables al cierre de minas.
Deseable experiencia en proyectos de cierre en distintos países de Latinoamérica.
Experiencia en evaluación y gestión de riesgos asociados al cierre y post-cierre de faenas mineras.
Experiencia en relacionamiento con clientes y participación en procesos de desarrollo de negocio y preparación de propuestas.
Inglés intermedio avanzado o superior, con capacidad para participar en proyectos y equipos internacionales.

Competencias Clave

Visión estratégica e integral del ciclo de vida minero.
Excelentes capacidades de liderazgo y gestión de proyectos con orientación a resultados.
Pensamiento analítico y resolución de problemas complejos.
Comunicación efectiva y habilidades de presentación.
Capacidad de construir relaciones sólidas con clientes y equipos multidisciplinarios.
Alta autonomía, criterio profesional y capacidad de toma de decisiones.
Compromiso con la sostenibilidad, la gestión de riesgos y la excelencia técnica.
Capacidad para desarrollar, orientar y potenciar el desempeño de profesionales junior e intermedios hacia la excelencia técnica.

jobs.description:
Forming Our Future together

FormFactor, Inc. (NASDAQ: FORM), is a leading provider of essential test and measurement technologies along the full semiconductor product life cycle — from characterization, modeling, reliability, and design de-bug, to qualification and production test. Semiconductor companies rely upon FormFactor’s products and services to accelerate profitability by optimizing device performance and advancing yield knowledge. The company serves customers through its network of facilities in Asia, Europe, and North America.

Rooted in our core values — Focus on the Customer, Ownership & Accountability, Respectfully & Effectively Communicate, and Motivate & Develop People — we foster an environment where diverse perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated. Everyone can make an impact here. Whether it's improving products, supporting customers, or positively influencing peers and the community, the contributions of our people matter.

Shift

The regular hours for this position are day shift.

Job Description

The Environmental Health and Safety Engineer
supports day-to-day implementation of environmental, health and safety (EHS) programs within a semiconductor manufacturing environment. Working under the guidance of more senior EHS team members, this role helps maintain compliance with applicable environmental, health and safety requirements and internal standards, supports routine monitoring and documentation, and assists with projects that reduce EHS risk and improve sustainable manufacturing operations.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance & Programs

Support site compliance activities for federal, state, and local environmental requirements (e.g., air, water, wastewater, hazardous waste, chemical management) through routine inspections, tracking, and documentation.
Support hazardous waste management, including container labeling/accumulation requirements, satellite accumulation areas, waste determinations/profiles, vendor pickups, and documentation; respond to spills/releases by following site procedures, assisting with containment/cleanup coordination, and completing required reporting and follow-up.
Assist with maintaining environmental programs relevant to semiconductor manufacturing, including Hazardous waste management, Air permitting, Wastewater and industrial pretreatment programs, and Stormwater pollution prevention.
Support environmental audits, inspections, and routine reporting activities; help prepare information for submittals and participate in agency interactions with guidance as needed.
Support site sustainability initiatives by assisting with data tracking and documentation and participating in projects across energy, water, waste, recycling, and emissions in alignment with corporate sustainability and ESG goals.

Semiconductor Manufacturing Support

Provide environmental support to fab operations, process engineering, facilities, and equipment teams by answering routine questions and escalating complex issues to senior staff.
Assist with reviewing new processes, chemical introductions, and equipment installations for environmental considerations and compliance requirements, with oversight as needed.
Support management of hazardous materials and specialty gases common to semiconductor manufacturing (e.g., acids, solvents, dopant gases) by helping maintain inventories, waste profiles, and operational controls.

Risk Assessment & Problem Solving

Identify routine environmental risks and recommend practical mitigation measures; partner with senior staff on higher-risk or complex issues.
Support environmental reviews and incident/non-compliance investigations by gathering facts, completing documentation, and helping track corrective actions.
Assist with collecting and analyzing environmental performance data and participate in continuous improvement initiatives.

Documentation & Training

Develop and update environmental procedures, work instructions, and documentation for assigned areas, using established templates and guidance.
Support delivery of environmental training to operations, engineering, and facilities teams (e.g., onboarding and annual refreshers).
Support internal EHS management systems activities (e.g., ISO 14001 or equivalent), including recordkeeping and internal audit preparation.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

Collaborate with Facilities, Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Supply Chain, and Corporate EHS to complete assigned environmental tasks and projects.
Participate in site sustainability goals and waste reduction initiatives.
Contribute environmental input to projects and operational changes, coordinating with senior team members as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with ISO 14001 or other Environmental Management Systems (EMS) concepts.
Exposure to air permitting, wastewater systems, or hazardous waste programs in manufacturing (semiconductor experience a plus).
HAZWOPER training (e.g., 24-hour or 40-hour) or ability to obtain; familiarity with spill response, hazardous waste handling, and contaminated materials management.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CHMM) are a plus.
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
Experience in manufacturing, electronics, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, or other regulated industrial environments; demonstrated ability to follow procedures and work collaboratively on environmental issues.

Work Environment

Manufacturing and cleanroom environment with required use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Exposure to chemicals and industrial systems consistent with semiconductor fabrication operations.
On-site presence required to support fab and facilities operations.

Skills

Air Permitting, Air Permitting, Chemical Safety, Collaboration, Communication, DOT Hazardous Materials, Environmental Management, Environmental Permitting, Environmental Regulations, Environmental Reporting, Environmental Stewardship, Environmental Sustainability, Hazardous Chemical Management, Hazardous Materials, Hazardous Material Safety, Hazardous Materials Management, Hazardous Materials Response, Hazardous Materials Training, Hazardous Waste Disposal, Hazardous Waste Management, Hazardous Wastes, Health and Safety, Internal Auditing, Investigative Skills, ISO 14001 {+ 11 more}

Education & Experience

No previous professional experience | Required

$60,600.00 - $79,590.00

This role in Beaverton, Oregon pays between $60,600.00 and $79,590.00 per year, depending on your experience, skills, and background. Pay may vary in other locations. We offer a full benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability coverage, a 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase plan (ESPP), and paid time off. jobs.description:
Perdue Foods has a goal of becoming the most trusted name in premium proteins by creating products for consumers and for retail and foodservice customers around the globe while changing the way animals are raised for food. It is part of Perdue Farms, a fourth-generation, family-owned food and agricultural business deeply rooted in tradition yet with a forward-thinking mindset. We believe that success starts with our people, and our culture is built on a foundation of teamwork, integrity, and respect, where every voice matters and everyone is encouraged to contribute to our shared goals. We are dedicated to creating a supportive, inclusive environment where associates feel valued and inspired to make an impact, both within the company and in the communities we serve. From promoting growth and development to prioritizing work-life balance, we’re committed to helping our team members thrive. That's Perdue.

Summary

Lead environmental compliance and sustainability initiatives that protect our people, operations, and the environment. As an Environmental Manager II, you will provide strategic leadership for environmental programs across a harvest processing facility and multiple supporting operations, including feed mills, hatcheries, and other locations. You will ensure compliance with environmental permits and regulatory requirements while driving programs related to air quality, water and wastewater treatment, stormwater management, waste reduction, recycling, hazardous materials, chemical compliance, and emergency planning. Partnering with site leadership and cross-functional teams, you will champion corporate sustainability initiatives, support environmental audits, and lead efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve energy efficiency, conserve water, and strengthen environmental performance. This role is ideal for an experienced, results-driven environmental leader who is passionate about regulatory excellence, operational sustainability, and deliver meaningful environmental impact across a complex manufacturing network.

Principal Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Provide a safe work environment for all associates by eliminating unsafe acts and conditions while adhering to all company safety policies.
Observe all safety requirements and actively prevent and report unsafe acts and conditions for all safety programs, including personal protective equipment (PPE), lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, confined space entry, process safety management, and machine guarding.
Ensure compliance with wastewater operations, air quality compliance, biosolids programs, hazardous waste, recycling, solid waste, potable water, and oil-handling programs for designated plant operations.
Supervise and manage associates, including hiring, training, and development, to ensure production requirements, environmental regulatory requirements, and sustainability goals are met cost effectively.
Provide timely, accurate, and consistent reports to internal and external customers.
Lead public education and community relations efforts related to environmental programs.
Order all parts, supplies, chemicals, and other materials required by the department.
Monitor all activities related to environmental programs, including wastewater operations.
Control costs and assets to manage within established goals.
Maintain a dotted-line reporting relationship with the Director of Operations at the assigned location and supporting facility managers.
Provide timely notification of activities, spill releases, and noncompliance events.
Conduct environmental audits of other facilities as part of the internal audit program.
Attend and conduct regular meetings to communicate department activities, plant activities, and safety information to associates and management.
Perform additional duties as directed by Environmental Operations leadership.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Biological Science, or a related field.
6+ years of related work experience.
Alternatively, a combination of relevant education and experience demonstrating progressive responsibility in environmental management may be considered.
Demonstrate strong reading, mathematics, writing, communication, analytical, and organizational skills.
Demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively in verbal and written form.
Possess a wastewater license at the level required to operate the largest wastewater treatment facility within the areas of responsibility. Multiple license requirements may apply.
Meet company safety handbook requirements.
Demonstrate knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Travel to remote facilities and offices for meetings as needed.

Preferred Education And Experience

Master of Science degree in Environmental Management, Environmental Health, Environmental Engineering, Biology, Chemistry, or another natural science discipline.

Physical Requirements And Environmental Factors

Position is primarily sedentary but may require occasional movement to other offices or buildings.
Move light equipment or supplies weighing up to 50 lbs.
Access files, supplies, and equipment as needed.
Work in an office, open-partitioned, cubicle environment.
Perform activities involving bending, twisting, lifting, reaching, sitting, and grasping with varying repetitions, distances, angles, weights, heights, time intervals, objects handled, and body positions depending on assigned tasks.
Experience exposure to wet and moist floors, including metal and plastic grating surfaces when in a plant environment.
Experience exposure to temperatures ranging from 28°F to 100°F, including conditions with ambient and 100% humidity.
Handle products in environments ranging from 25°F to 50°F.
Experience exposure to noise levels ranging from 50 dB to 110 dB.
Experience exposure to chemicals commonly found in poultry, food processing, and wastewater treatment facilities.
Wear and use all protective and safety equipment required for the job as directed by the company.

Project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously

Requirements

jobs.title: Senior Director, Environmental Compliance
jobs.description:
Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

The Senior Director of Environmental Compliance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of Veolia Water New Jersey's (VWNJ) environmental compliance programs, ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, in alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities, while advancing public health protection, environmental stewardship, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. This position provides executive oversight of all environmental compliance activities related to air, drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, waste management, hazardous materials, spill prevention and response, environmental permitting, emergency preparedness, and environmental auditing.

This position leads the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Company's environmental compliance management systems, environmental governance framework, and regulatory compliance programs across all VWNJ operations. The Senior Director provides oversight of all laboratory analysis required to demonstrate compliance, including outside laboratory services and the Haworth WTP laboratory.

The Senior Director serves as the organization's subject matter expert for environmental compliance, environmental permitting, drinking water quality, wastewater treatment compliance, environmental management systems, and environmental regulatory relations. The role partners closely with other functional areas including, operations, engineering, legal, finance, strategic relations, etc., to identify environmental risks, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure consistent compliance across all operations.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities

Lead, empower, and mentor a direct team of environmental professionals, driving cohesive collaboration and operational alignment across all functional disciplines within the position's scope (including Operations, Engineering, Legal, and Finance).
Serve as a strategic leader with external regulatory agencies, effectively interpreting complex regulations and guidelines to advocate for approaches that balance strict regulatory compliance with exceptional customer service and operational/business realities.
Provide environmental compliance leadership for VWNJ. Ensure alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities.
Provide strategic oversight of compliance programs related to all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including requirements administered by the EPA and applicable state environmental agencies.
Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and communicate impacts to business leadership. Lead development of comments for submission during public comment period for draft regulatory requirements. Interpret emerging regulatory requirements and develop implementation strategies to ensure organizational readiness.
Support development of policies related to water treatment operations, laboratory quality assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Lead the design, implementation, and continual improvement of VWNJ's environmental compliance management systems.
Lead environmental due diligence activities supporting capital projects and new business initiatives.
Evaluate environmental impacts associated with operational activities and infrastructure investments.
Direct internal environmental assessments and support external regulatory inspections. Oversee development, implementation, and closure of corrective action plans.
Lead VWNJ environmental auditing and compliance assurance programs.
Monitor environmental performance trends and ensure timely resolution of compliance issues.
Oversee environmental permitting activities across all operations.
Ensure timely submission of required regulatory reports and environmental compliance documentation.
Ensure maintenance of systems supporting environmental permits, compliance obligations, inspections, reporting, and regulatory commitments.
Provide oversight of environmental emergency preparedness and response programs.
Direct environmental incident investigations, including spill response and root cause analyses.
Serve as liaison with environmental regulatory agencies.
Build productive relationships with regulators, industry associations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the organization during inspections, audits, enforcement actions, and compliance negotiations.
Establish departmental goals, performance expectations, succession planning, and employee development initiatives.
Allocate resources to support business priorities and regulatory obligations.
Foster collaboration across Operations, Engineering, Legal,Finance, and Corporate leadership.
Develop departmental strategic plans, budgets, and resource forecasts.
Establish and monitor environmental performance objectives, key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting metrics.
Recommend process improvements that enhance compliance, operational reliability, sustainability, and financial performance.
Support corporate sustainability and environmental stewardship initiatives.

Work Environment

Participation in environmental emergency response activities and on-call leadership, as required.
Combination of office and field environments, including visits to treatment facilities, construction sites, laboratories, and industrial operations.
Ability to conduct field inspections and work in varying environmental conditions while utilizing appropriate personal protective equipment.

Qualifications

Education/Experience/Background:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, or a related technical discipline.
Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 12 years of progressively responsible environmental compliance experience within a regulated utility, environmental services, industrial, manufacturing, or infrastructure organization.
Minimum of 7 years of leadership experience managing environmental professionals and cross-functional teams.
Demonstrated experience leading environmental compliance programs across multiple operating locations.
Experience interacting with federal and state regulatory agencies.
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance management systems.
Experience supporting environmental due diligence, capital projects, and business development preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Safe Drinking Water Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Clean Air Act, and related environmental permitting requirements.
Knowledge of drinking water treatment, water chemistry, wastewater operations, hazardous materials management, and environmental risk management.
Strong understanding of environmental auditing, compliance assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance management systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience developing environmental compliance strategies, policies, and governance frameworks.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and build effective relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
Strong project management and organizational leadership capabilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Google applications and environmental compliance management systems.

Additional Information

Pay Range:
$180000 to $200000 Per Year.

Benefits:
Veolia's comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement. Pay and benefits for employees represented by a union are outlined in their collective bargaining agreement.

Sick leave - 56 hours; Observed Holidays - 11 days; Vacation - Flexible Time Off

Eligible for up to 20% Annual Performance Bonus

Join us for an extraordinary opportunity

Be part of a major aviation project in the Greater London area, that will redefine the future of air travel and delivery excellence. We're building a dynamic team to plan and deliver complex, high-impact work, at the heart of one of the region's most innovative and fast-moving developments.

In this role, you will conduct field investigations and client interviews to determine work scope and cost estimates for a project's civil/structural aspects. You will lead design, development, modification, evaluation, and constructability reviews of civil/structural components and processes. Your technical expertise will ensure the unique and complex requirements of a project's civil/structural aspects are met.

"This position is designated as part-time telework per our global telework policy and may require at least three days of in-person attendance per week at the assigned office or project. Weekly in-person schedules will be determined by the individual and their supervisor, in consultation with functional or project leadership".

Major Responsibilities

Deliver design management on projects, ensuring environmental risks and requirements are effectively managed across archaeology, landscape, ecology, water, soil, materials, waste and resources.
Develop project scope that meets business needs and supports the business case.
Prepare design briefs for external consultants and manage design contracts through the design process.
Develop safe, cost-effective design solutions that meet environmental requirements and align with GAL Engineering Standards or agreed concessions.
Define asset information requirements for design and construction contracts.
Develop sustainable design solutions that reduce construction carbon through energy efficiency, material selection, waste reduction and transport optimisation.
Coordinate design changes during construction and handover.
Assess environmental impacts on programme, cost and efficiencies.
Support Principal Designer duties with the CDM Advisor.
Support contractor and consultant technical evaluations.
Manage site environmental constraints and quality requirements.
Review as-built information for commissioning and handover.
Ensure legal, statutory and standards compliance.

Education And Experience Requirements

Degree or equivalent in civil, environmental engineering or environmental management.
Chartered membership of an engineering or environmental institution desirable.
UK design/design management experience on environmental projects.
Experience managing concurrent design projects desirable.

Required Knowledge And Skills

UK environmental legislation, consents and regulator engagement.
Manage external design consultants, ensuring that design outputs are reviewed, co-ordinated and meet quality

Construction health, safety and environmental awareness.
Practical problem-solving skills.
Construction techniques and constructability.
Quality management monitoring.
MS Office and Project proficiency.
NEC contracts, PMIs and claims experience desirable.

Total Rewards/Benefits

A distinguished researcher in environmental science, water or a related field

jobs.description:
**Overview**

Vernadero Group Inc. (Vernadero) is a Veteran\-Owned Small Business founded in 1999 to provide infrastructure and environmental program support to Federal agency projects and activities throughout the United States and its territories. Vernadero is seeking a GIS Analyst to provide geospatial support for the Army National Guard (ARNG).

The successful candidate will join a team of other highly skilled analysts and will be responsible for performing geodatabase maintenance, quality control, and tool development on Common Installation Picture (CIP) layers. Typical responsibilities extend to web\-GIS, including maintenance and development of various ArcGIS Enterprise items including dashboards, hosted feature services, and scripting using the ArcGIS API for Python. The candidate must have some experience with nearly the entire ArcGIS suite of software because the position also requires leading training sessions and providing ad\-hoc support to ARNG staff and State/Territory GIS teams. This is a full\-time, permanent position that allows for remote teleworking.

Candidates who reside in the Washington, D.C., metropolitan region and are willing to work at least one day a week at the Army National Guard’s Readiness Center (TARC) facility in Arlington, Virginia, will be given precedence. The position also requires a Tier 1 Department of Defense background check and the ability to obtain a government issued Common Access Card.

**General Qualifications**

Candidates should possess the following minimum qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree in geography, geospatial science, computer science, or related field
* Minimum of 4 years of professional geospatial and geodatabase experience
* Extensive experience with ESRI ArcGIS Pro and utilizing extensions including data reviewer, spatial analyst, and network analyst
* Experience with ArcGIS Enterprise and manipulating/creating various types of items including dashboards, hosted feature services, and experience builder applications
* Experience with scripting using both ArcGIS Arcade, the ArcGIS arcpy module, and the ArcGIS API for Python
* Knowledge of Microsoft Office software, to include Excel, PowerBI, PowerAutomate, SharePoint, and Forms
* Excellent written and oral communications skills including leading training sessions and public speaking on occasion
* Customer service\-oriented skills to help with training sessions for entry\-level GIS users on how to pre\-process geodatabase submissions and use published map templates
* Organizational skills and the ability to work in a complex environment
* U.S. citizenship and ability to intermittently travel nationwide
* Valid U.S. driver’s license

**Preferred Qualifications**

Preference will be given to candidates that possess:

* Graduate degree in geography, geospatial science, computer science, or related field
* GISP Certification
* Experience leading GIS and geospatial support training classes
* Knowledge of Microsoft Access databases and how to update and maintain them
* Experience with Army and ARNG geospatial databases, infrastructure, and real property data and terminology
* Demonstrated experience with Python scripting using any ESRI\-published module
* Experience with SDSFIE version 4\.0
* Experience with the Department of the Army databases and software packages
* Experience administering an ArcGIS Enterprise Portal and PostgreSQL database

**Responsibilities** 

Specific responsibilities for the GIS Analyst may include the following:

* Develop content and teach GIS workshops to ARNG stakeholders
* Generate maps and other content to support funding requests for military construction projects to Congress via the DD 1391 process
* Communicate directly with ARNG stakeholders in multiple states
* Work with a team of GIS Analyst in the development of Common Installation Picture (CIP) data layers, metadata, and SDSFIE migration of several terabytes of data
* Maintain ArcGIS Enterprise dashboards, that include complex data sources involving Arcade scripting.
* Continued maintenance on a suite of ArcGIS Toolbox features including models, and published geoprocessing tools (Python arcpy module)
* Track stakeholder requests using various Microsoft SharePoint Lists and Excel files.
* Geodatabase quality control and post\-processing of ARNG stakeholder\-submitted data. This involves both manual and automated QA/QC procedures.

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $80,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off

jobs.title: PhD: Modelling Impacts of Agricultural Practices on Soil Ecosystem Services
jobs.description:
Your job

The Earth Systems and Global Change Group at Wageningen University and Research invites applications for a PhD position (4 years) in a challenging project titled: “Modelling impacts of agricultural practices on soil ecosystem services across Europe”.

Preserving and restoring agricultural sustainability in Europe requires a monitoring framework quantifying how single and combined agricultural management practices affect European soil ecosystem services. The project aims to develop site specific recommendations for the implementation of agricultural practices in arable farming systems that enhance their contribution to a sustainable environment. The project is part of an ongoing European research project with 17 research partners. By finetuning and extending existing regional soil health assessment frameworks to assess the integrative contribution of crop, soil, nutrient and water management practices, this project will deliver new knowledge to enable farmers and policy makers to improve the ecosystem services the soil supplies, and to enable decision-makers to explore scenario outcomes, assess impacts and incorporate the results into soil quality related policy recommendations at national and EU level.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

As a PhD researcher, you will expand and improve an existing modelling framework to assess carbon and nutrient flows, and soil functions contributing to multiple ecosystem services, and the impact of management measures on regional level, assembling empirical and process-based algorithms considering agronomic and environmental impacts. You contribute to the following activities:

Develop a model to simulate and upscale impact of the combinations of farming practices on soil ecosystem services for regional / EU level
Perform an integrated spatial assessment of soil ecosystem services and adoption of farming practices, identifying synergies and trade off among arable farming practices in view of multiple ecosystem services
Assess the impact of co-created adoption policies / measurement packages at farm system level

You will work here

The research is embedded within the chair Earth Systems and Global Change Group (https://www.wur.nl/en/research-results/chair-groups/environmental-sciences/earth-systems-and-global-change-group.htm), which is led by Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-hhe-hannah-van-zanten) and Prof. dr. Nynke Hofstra (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-n-nynke-hofstra). You will be supervised by Dr. Gerard Ros (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/drir-gh-gerard-ros), Dr. Mengru Wang (https://www.wur.nl/nl/personen/dr-m-mengru-wang) and Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-hhe-hannah-van-zanten) from Wageningen University, and Prof Dr. Erik Meers from Ghent University.

Your qualities

You Are/have The Following

knowledge of soil health, nutrient and/or agrochemical cycles in agriculture;
experience in quantitative modeling and programming (e.g., R, python);
excellent scientific writing skills in English;
experience with publishing peer-reviewed academic journals is appreciated;
good organizational and intercultural communication skills;
willingness to travel across Europe.

You also possess:

a successfully completed MSc degree in environmental sciences, agricultural studies, or similar with a strong quantitative background;
enthusiasm for collaborating with an interdisciplinary team of researchers with diverse backgrounds and disciplines.
the entry requirements of the WUR PhD programme;
enthusiasm to do a PhD project at Wageningen University for four years.

For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale). Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here (https://www.wur.nl/en/education/phd-programme/admission-requirements).

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

Partially paid parental leave;
working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team.

The gross salary for the first year is € 3,204,- per month rising to € 4,051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (https://www.universiteitenvannederland.nl/en/collective-labour-agreement-of-dutch-universities) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well.

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment.

Coming from abroad

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/) can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account, dual career programs or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact Dr Gerard Ros via email: gerard.ros@wur.nl (mailto:gerard.ros@wur.nl)

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Jessa Rozema, Corporate Recruiter, via jessa.rozema-stol@wur.nl

Ready to apply?

You can apply directly using the apply button on the vacancy page on our website which will allow us to process your personal information with your approval. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered.

To apply, please send the following documents ( max. 3 pages in total
):

Complete and up-to-date curriculum vitae (max. 2 pages);
Motivation letter (max. 1 page).

The maximum length of the documents must not exceed 3 pages. If it exceeds, applications will not be considered. Additional files such as grades and transcripts are not required during this stage and will not be considered.

You can apply up to and including 2 October 2026.

Additional information form

Qualifications

For this position, you must fill in a mandatory form which will allow us to have a comprehensive view of your qualifications and better assess your fit for it. You can access the form using the link below:

PhD: Modelling Impacts of Agricultural Practices on Soil Ecosystem Services – Fill out form (https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/kGP2ELdVnL)

Your prompt response will ensure that your application continues to move forward in the evaluation process. We assure you that the information provided will be kept confidential and used solely for this application process.

Welcome, safe, and valued

Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization.

We are

The mission of Wageningen University & Research is “To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life”. Under the banner Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen University and the specialised research institutes of the Wageningen Research Foundation have joined forces in contributing to finding solutions to important questions in the domain of healthy food and living environment. With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. The unique Wageningen approach lies in its integrated approach to issues and the collaboration between different disciplines.

Read the 5 reasons (https://www.wur.nl/en/Jobs/Why-choose-WUR.htm) why your future colleagues enjoy working at WUR and watch the video below to get an idea of our green campus!

Avy pioneers unmanned aviation technology for emergency services, healthcare logistics, and security and intelligence. We partner with innovative organizations that are among the first in the world to integrate long-range drone operations into their daily workflows.

Avy’s Flight Operations Team plays a central role in our mission. We lead both the technical and operational side of drone flight: carrying out test missions that drive the development of our flagship drone, Aera, and performing exciting demonstration flights and proof of concept operations, while also flying real-world operations with real-world impact.

We are looking for a passionate new team member to bring these missions to life: ensuring smooth, safe, and efficient flights that serve a variety of important sectors, including Emergency Response, Monitoring and Inspections, Healthcare and Logistics, and Security and Intelligence.

We’re not necessarily looking for someone with drone flight experience (although that's a nice to have), but someone who brings the aviation mindset: a structured, safety-driven, and situationally aware approach to flying and operating aircraft.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Earth Observation
jobs.description:
About The Role

Muon seeks a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead earth observation programs for U.S. Government customers. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development. These programs span the full mission lifecycle — concept development and design through integration, launch, and on-orbit operations — and are executed under formal government contract structures with defined deliverables and milestones. The Senior TPM runs the program end to end: executing every contractual commitment and positioning Muon to win the work that follows.

The Senior TPM holds single-point accountability for delivering the program on schedule, within budget, and to technical performance standards. Operating with high autonomy on an accelerated contractual schedule, you will drive key milestones and lead cross-functional technical exchanges spanning systems engineering, payload, flight software, ground segment, and mission operations.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Responsibilities

Program Execution

Serve as the single accountable owner for the program's cost, schedule, and technical baselines
Own the integrated master schedule, cost baseline, and risk register; track and report progress against contract milestones
Plan and run formal program events — internal readiness reviews, and customer-facing milestone deliverable reviews
Maintain tight cost and schedule discipline; surface deviations to the customer promptly and with a recovery plan

Customer Interface

Act as the primary programmatic interface to the Government customer, including contracting and technical representatives
Lead technical exchange meetings and convert customer input into actionable program direction
Own the delivery and quality of all contract data deliverables

Cross-Functional Leadership

Direct a cross-functional team spanning systems engineering, payload, flight software, ground processing, and mission operations
Partner with mission operations when program activities involve Muon's operational systems — without disrupting existing missions
Drive design trades and study conclusions to closure on schedule, escalating crisply when decisions stall

Security, Compliance, and Growth

Execute the program in full compliance with its government security requirements, including handling of controlled information and strict public-release restrictions
Ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR export controls and U.S.-only performance requirements
Support program growth: convert program artifacts into proposal-ready material and support capture of follow-on opportunities

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering or a technical field, or equivalent experience.
8+ years of program management experience on complex aerospace or defense development programs, including direct ownership of cost, schedule, and technical baselines
Experience executing U.S. Government contracts: statement-of-work and CDRL deliverables, milestone-based structures, and day-to-day work with government contracting and technical representatives
Experience leading engineering teams through concept development, trade studies, and preliminary design
Exceptional written communication skills — you will author and own the quality of customer-facing reports, design artifacts, and contract deliverables

Preferred Qualifications

Satellite or instrument program leadership across the full lifecycle (design, build,
integrate, test, operate)
Domain experience with remote sensing systems — EO/IR, RF, or both — at the payload or mission level
Direct experience working with USSF Space Systems Command or JPL
PMP certification or equivalent program management credentials
Ability to obtain a security clearance

Salary

The salary range for this role is $206,000 - $232,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position requires access to export controlled information. To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C.

1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C.
1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. The Company may, for legitimate business reasons, decline to pursue any export licensing process.

jobs.title: Wildlife Repair/Exclusion Technician
jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re ready for more than a job, Critter Control offers a career with purpose.

Are you looking for a hands-on career, not just a job? Do you have experience in construction, roofing, insulation, or home improvement and want to put those skills to work in a stable, recession-resistant industry?

Critter Control Operations specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. We help customers resolve wildlife-related concerns in safe, effective, and environmentally responsible ways while protecting homes, businesses, and communities.

This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. You’ll play a critical role in preventing future wildlife intrusions by performing exclusion work, repairs, and remediation while maintaining high safety and quality standards.

Critter Control is a brand that invests in its people. If you are a driven professional who embraces our values and upholds our standards of excellence, you’ll find opportunities to succeed, grow, and advance within our organization.

Responsibilities

As a Wildlife Exclusion/Repair Service Technician
at Critter Control, you perform hands-on exclusion, repair, and remediation services for residential and commercial properties. You identify entry points, complete structural repairs, and implement humane wildlife prevention solutions while following safety, technical, and quality guidelines.

What Does a Day in the Life Look Like?

Perform interior and exterior property inspections, including roofs, attics, crawlspaces, and other confined spaces, to identify wildlife entry points and potential vulnerabilities.
Install preventative exclusion materials such as screens, chimney caps, vent covers, and other barriers to prevent wildlife access.
Complete minor repairs to roofs, siding, foundations, and other structural areas where wildlife may gain entry.
Safely remove wildlife using humane trapping and relocation techniques in accordance with company standards and regulations.
Maintain accurate documentation of services performed, materials used, and customer interactions.
Provide clear, detailed reports and review completed scopes of work with customers.
Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to ensure seamless and positive customer experience.
Follow up with customers to confirm satisfaction and address any additional concerns or recommendations.

What type of benefits will you receive?

Competitive hourly rate: $20-$20/Hour
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401k with generous match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
6 Paid Holidays Annually!
PTO accrual based on tenure - 3 weeks beginning first full year!
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year (federal max!) OR free tuition on approved programs through Purdue Global!!!
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities!
Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Qualifications

What do you need to be successful?

High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is a plus
Valid driver’s license
Proven experience in construction, carpentry, roofing, or other related fields
Ability to work in the field independently
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Proficiency in using several types of software and applications

What does the work environment look like?

We go where the wildlife goes! Candidates must be physically capable of safely performing the following job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Must be able to drive to various locations, often covering large territories.
Frequent walking, standing, and moving through diverse types of terrain, including uneven ground, stairs, roofs, and sometimes slippery or muddy areas.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions (extreme heat, extreme cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must have the ability to climb stairs and ladders safely.
Must be able to crouch, kneel, bend, and stretch frequently.
Capability to carry and use equipment necessary for inspections and minor control measures (Traps, ladders, inspection tools, etc).
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Clear verbal communication skills to interact effectively with clients and team members.

Join us in making a positive impact on nuisance wildlife management and become a part of our dedicated team today!

Critter Control Operations is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Performing due diligence and permitting for new manufacturing faculties.

Manage and oversee compliance with environmental regulations and Amazon policy;
Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization;

Prioritize and manage multiple technically complex assignments concurrently;

Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately;
Assist in time-critical report submission to various governmental agencies;
Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and associated regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective action.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds

jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!

At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

Parsons has been a leader in the planning, design and delivery of transportation infrastructure for more than 75 years. We are seeking an experienced Environmental Planner with strong Ontario Ministry of Transportation (MTO) experience to join our Infrastructure team in the Greater Toronto Region.

The successful candidate may be based in our Toronto, Markham, Oakville or London office, with flexibility for hybrid work. You will help deliver provincial highway projects while strengthening Parsons’ environmental planning capabilities and relationships with MTO and other transportation clients.

Position Overview

The Senior Environmental Planner will lead the environmental planning and assessment components of MTO highway assignments through planning and preliminary design and support the implementation of environmental commitments during detail design and construction.

The position will coordinate multidisciplinary environmental studies, consultation, environmental documentation, permits and approvals, and the integration of environmental requirements into project design and contract documentation.

The successful candidate will also contribute to proposals, client development, technical quality, and the mentoring of junior and intermediate planners.

Responsibilities

Lead environmental planning and assessment for MTO highway projects in accordance with the current Class Environmental Assessment for Provincial Transportation Facilities and Municipal Expressways (2024).
Serve as Environmental Lead on planning, preliminary design and detail design assignments, coordinating environmental specialists, engineers, subconsultants and project managers.
Establish environmental work plans, study requirements, schedules, budgets and deliverables appropriate to the applicable Class EA requirements, project classification and potential environmental effects.
Apply the MTO Environmental Reference for Highway Design (ERD) and applicable MTO environmental guides, policies, directives, standards, forms and technical guidance.
Prepare and review Transportation Environmental Study Reports, environmental assessment documentation, consultation records, environmental commitment records and design-phase environmental reports.
Lead the identification and evaluation of environmental effects, avoidance opportunities, mitigation measures, monitoring requirements and environmental commitments.
Coordinate public, stakeholder, agency and municipal consultation, including notices, Public Information Centres, presentations, comment-response tracking and issue resolution.
Support MTO-led consultation with Indigenous communities and organizations, including consultation planning, documentation, comment tracking and the consideration of potential impacts on Aboriginal or treaty rights.
Support issue resolution under the Class EA and assist MTO in responding to Section 16 Order requests, where applicable.
Develop and coordinate environmental permitting and approvals strategies with technical specialists, project teams and regulatory agencies.
Ensure environmental commitments and approval requirements are carried forward into detail design, drawings, specifications, contract documents and construction requirements.
Provide technical review and quality assurance for environmental planning deliverables.
Build and maintain productive working relationships with MTO, municipal clients, regulatory agencies and project partners.
Lead or support proposal preparation, including methodologies, work plans, schedules, staffing plans, budgets and level-of-effort estimates.
Mentor junior and intermediate environmental planners and support consistent environmental planning practices across the team.
Monitor changes to environmental legislation, MTO processes, policies and industry practices that may affect project delivery.

Requirements

University degree in environmental planning, urban or regional planning, environmental studies, geography, environmental science or a related discipline. A relevant graduate degree is an asset.
Minimum of 10 years of environmental planning or environmental assessment experience, including substantial recent experience delivering MTO highway assignments in a consulting environment.
Demonstrated experience acting as an Environmental Lead or senior environmental planner on MTO planning, preliminary design or detail design projects.
Strong working knowledge of the Class Environmental Assessment for Provincial Transportation Facilities and Municipal Expressways (2024), including project classification, consultation, evaluation, documentation, issues resolution and transition requirements.
Familiarity with the previous MTO Class EA process and the transition of projects from the 2000 Class EA to the 2024 Class EA is an asset.
Knowledge and practical application of the MTO ERD and associated environmental guides, policies, standards, procedures and technical requirements.
Experience preparing or reviewing MTO Transportation Environmental Study Reports, consultation materials, environmental commitments and multidisciplinary environmental reports.
Experience coordinating environmental specialists covering areas such as natural heritage, fisheries, archaeology, cultural heritage, noise, contaminated property, excess soil, groundwater, drainage and stormwater management.
Experience supporting public, agency, stakeholder and Indigenous consultation for provincial transportation projects.
Strong understanding of applicable provincial and federal environmental legislation and associated permitting and approval requirements.
Demonstrated project-management experience, including managing scope, schedule, budget, risk, subconsultants and multidisciplinary teams.
Strong technical writing, presentation, consultation and issue-resolution skills.
Demonstrated ability to build client relationships and contribute to proposals and business development.
Membership or eligibility for membership with the Ontario Professional Planners Institute or Canadian Institute of Planners is an asset. An RPP or MCIP designation is also considered an asset.
Experience with the Transit and Rail Project Assessment Process under O. Reg. 231/08, federal impact assessment processes, and municipal environmental assessment processes—including the transition from the Municipal Class EA to the Municipal Project Assessment Process—is considered an asset.
Valid Ontario Class G driver’s licence and ability to travel to project sites and client meetings when required.

This position is part of our Critical Infrastructure team.

For more than 80 years, our experts have designed and delivered the critical infrastructure that connects and protects communities around the world. We work in collaborative teams, both within the company and with our partners and customers, to plan, design, build, and modernize infrastructure. We take special pride in projects and solutions that improve communities as well as people’s quality of life by promoting economic growth, enhancing mobility, and increasing sustainability and resiliency. Powered by our people, we provide the imagination necessary to support our customers’ visions—and to help them see what's next!

Salary Range: $85,000 - $135,000

This job posting is for a current addition or replacement opportunity within Parsons.

We value our employees and want our employees to take care of their overall wellbeing, which is why we offer best-in-class benefits such as health, vision, dental, employer paid provincial care premiums, Defined Contribution Pension Plan (DCPP), Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA), Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP), life insurance, paid time off, sick leave, all province observed holidays off, and gym membership discounts to fit your busy lifestyle!

Parsons is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility in the workplace. Parsons equally employs representation at all job levels for indigenous peoples, women, individuals with disabilities, and visible minorities.

We truly invest and care about our employee’s wellbeing and provide endless growth opportunities as the sky is the limit, so aim for the stars! Imagine next and join the Parsons quest—APPLY TODAY!

Job Overview

APTIM has an immediate need for an Environmental Scientist on a full-time basis to participate in a variety of environmental, health, and safety compliance support tasks, such as, diversified industry hygiene sampling, asbestos consulting services, mold assessments, and lead assessment surveys. Other work could include industrial hygiene air sampling, and soil and groundwater sampling. This individual will be performing field duties but will also directly work with clients. The successful candidate MUST be willing to travel and work in industrial facilities. Travel is expected to average 5 days a month, though some projects may require longer extended stays of 1 or 2 months.

This position will consist of a mix of field and office work, where the applicant will be required to write final reports. The candidate must have good writing skills and skills in working in Excel, WORD and some sale’s software application. This position will include the ability to work remotely, when work allows, but the candidate may be required to work at APTIM’s Office located in Lawrenceville, New Jersey on a limited basis.

The candidate must have valid asbestos certifications or state licenses as an USEPA AHERA Asbestos Building Inspector and Asbestos Abatement Project Monitor (or Project Designer). APTIM will provide some site-specific technical training when needed.

Executing various work scopes, while meeting project schedules and budgets.
Working independently and as part of a project team and be able to adjust to changing conditions.
Working as a team member and/or team lead to assist in preparation of reports
Interfacing with client facility personnel (with eventual interaction directly with client management).
Site sampling (asbestos, lead, mold, air, water, soil, noise, and other industrial hygiene services).
Perform site assessments/inspections for environmental, health, and safety, up to and including job safety assessments (JSA).
Future progress into becoming a Project Manager and managing client contracts and business development.
Eventually learning APTIM management requirements including financial cost build-up, multipliers, margins and business procedures.
Individual should be aware that the field work can be physically challenging and involve working in industrial settings.
Working at heights, and areas of high temperatures are a possibility.

Bachelor's degree in science or related area required.
Related work experience between 5+ years.
Strong written and oral communication skills.
Strong computer skills required. Must have a demonstrated strength and proficiency in Microsoft applications such as MS Excel, MS Word, SharePoint Online, etc. and the ability to learn other software applications.
