Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

HDR is seeking a strategic, client-focused Technology, Media & Telecommunications (TMT) Environmental Lead
to provide leadership, technical excellence, and market growth for environmental sciences, planning, permitting, and regulatory services across the global TMT market sector. This role will partner closely with TMT Market Sector Leadership, Environmental Cross Sector Leadership, Regional Environmental Leaders, and Client Development Leaders to drive HDR’s environmental services strategy and support the delivery of complex mission-critical infrastructure projects. This position can be based out of any of our HDR offices.

Position Summary

The TMT Environmental Lead
will serve as the primary environmental point of contact and subject matter expert for the TMT sector, helping clients navigate environmental, land use, permitting, and regulatory challenges associated with data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, digital campuses, fiber networks, and related technology developments. The role will support business development, project delivery, professional development, quality management, and strategic growth initiatives across HDR’s global TMT portfolio.

This position reports directly to the TMT Market Sector Director with additional indirect relationships with the TMT Business Development, TMT Practice, and Environmental Cross Sector Leadership teams and will collaborate extensively across Business Groups and regions to align environmental strategy with market objectives and client needs. The individual is expected to maintain strong client relationships and remain actively engaged in industry leadership and key project pursuits.

About HDR's TMT Market Sector

HDR is a global leader in architecture, engineering, environmental, and consulting services with a long-standing track record of successfully delivering mission-critical projects, including data centers around the world.

Our TMT teams provide comprehensive, end-to-end services ranging from site selection and due diligence through design, permitting, construction support, commissioning, retrofits, and operational optimization. We understand the unique requirements associated with mission-critical facilities and bring deep expertise in developing high-performing, future-ready campuses designed for reliability, performance, scalability, and operational resilience.

What sets HDR apart is the breadth and integration of our services. In addition to architecture and engineering, HDR provides stakeholder engagement, environmental planning and permitting, regulatory compliance, real estate services, utility coordination, acoustics, air quality, emissions consulting, and specialized technical advisory services. With global reach and multidisciplinary depth, HDR is uniquely positioned to help clients deliver rapidly expanding digital infrastructure programs while meeting environmental, regulatory, community, and operational objectives.

Primary Responsibilities

Market Leadership and Strategy

Develop and implement HDR's environmental strategy for the TMT Market Sector.
Support TMT market sector annual and long-range strategic planning initiatives.
Identify emerging market trends, permitting challenges, and regulatory developments affecting data center and telecommunications clients.
Help define HDR's market positioning and growth strategy for environmental permitting, planning, and compliance services within the TMT sector.
Partner with Client Development Leaders and Market Sector Leadership to expand HDR's environmental services footprint globally.
Serve as HDR's environmental ambassador within industry organizations, conferences, and client forums.

Environmental Permitting and Regulatory Leadership

Serve as HDR's primary point of contact and technical resource for environmental and land use permitting associated with data centers, telecommunications facilities, fiber infrastructure, network operations centers, and related technology developments.
Provide technical oversight and strategic guidance for permitting programs supporting greenfield and brownfield development projects.
Lead development of permitting strategies that support accelerated project delivery schedules while maintaining compliance with applicable regulations.
Support clients in obtaining approvals from federal, state, provincial, county, municipal, and other regulatory agencies.
Advise project teams regarding environmental review processes, permitting risks, mitigation strategies, and regulatory compliance requirements.
Monitor evolving environmental and land development regulations and communicate impacts to clients and HDR leadership.

Land Use and Development

Lead and support environmental planning and permitting efforts involving:

Land use approvals and entitlement strategies.
State, provincial, county, municipal, and local government permits and approvals.
Site access authorizations for construction and development activities.
Zoning reviews, zoning variances, rezoning applications, and zoning board approvals.
Conditional use permits and special use permits.
Easements, right-of-way approvals, and property access agreements.
Utility connection approvals and infrastructure coordination.
Building occupancy permits and certificates of occupancy.
Construction permits and development approvals for improved and unimproved lands.
Stakeholder engagement and public agency coordination.
Environmental due diligence and site feasibility assessments.

Business Development and Client Engagement

Build and maintain senior-level relationships with key TMT clients.
Support strategic pursuits, capture planning efforts, and major proposal activities.
Actively identify opportunities for environmental, planning, permitting, and regulatory services.
Collaborate with business development and technical leaders to develop integrated client solutions.
Participate in client meetings, executive presentations, and pursuit strategy workshops.
Serve as Project Principal, Technical Lead, or Strategic Advisor on select key projects.

Project Delivery and Technical Excellence

Promote best-in-class project delivery practices across the TMT environmental practice.
Support project teams in developing innovative approaches to complex permitting and entitlement challenges.
Provide quality oversight and participate in HDR's project review processes.
Foster consistency, technical excellence, and knowledge sharing across offices and regions.
Develop and implement best practices, tools, and guidance documents for environmental services delivery.

Team Development and Leadership

Mentor and develop environmental professionals supporting the TMT sector.
Assist with strategic recruitment and succession planning initiatives.
Foster collaboration between environmental practitioners, planners, engineers, architects, and market sector teams.
Support career development, technical training, and leadership development.
Help build a connected, high-performing practice across regions and business groups.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in environmental planning, environmental science, urban planning, engineering, public policy, or related discipline.
Minimum 10+ years of experience leading environmental planning, permitting, and regulatory programs for major infrastructure, industrial, technology, telecommunications, or mission-critical projects.
Demonstrated expertise in land use planning, development entitlements, and construction permitting.
Extensive experience obtaining approvals from state, provincial, county, municipal, and local regulatory agencies.
Demonstrated experience leading permitting programs for large, complex development projects with aggressive schedules.
Strong knowledge of permitting requirements associated with site development, utility infrastructure, zoning, occupancy approvals, and construction activities.
Proven ability to build and maintain executive-level client relationships.
Demonstrated success supporting business development, project pursuits, and strategic growth initiatives.
Experience supporting data center campus development projects.
Experience with telecommunications, fiber, wireless, or digital infrastructure development.
Established industry reputation within the technology, telecommunications, mission-critical, or land development sectors.
Experience presenting at industry conferences and participating in professional organizations.
Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary teams across multiple geographic regions.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed.

Success Measures

The successful TMT Environmental Lead will:

Establish HDR as the premier environmental and permitting advisor for data center and digital infrastructure development.
Build a cohesive, high-performing environmental practice aligned with TMT market growth objectives.
Expand client relationships and increase HDR's market share in mission-critical and digital infrastructure services.
Deliver innovative permitting and entitlement solutions that accelerate project delivery while maintaining regulatory compliance.
Advance technical excellence, professional development, and collaboration across HDR's environmental practice.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a Professional, Architecture, Engineering or closely related field
A minimum of 10 years of experience in related field
For Business Class leadership roles for which the core service being overseen is technical design, the role must maintain a professional or Architecture/Engineering registration and has related technical experience
Experienced in development and management of diverse teams
Works cooperatively with other business class directors, operations managers, technical directors and marketing managers on business class efforts
Committed to quality, improvement and HDR values
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. HDR is seeking a strategic, client-focused Technology, Media & Telecommunications (TMT) Environmental Lead
to provide leadership, technical excellence, and market growth for environmental sciences, planning, permitting, and regulatory services across the global TMT market sector. This role will partner closely with TMT Market Sector Leadership, Environmental Cross Sector Leadership, Regional Environmental Leaders, and Client Development Leaders to drive HDR’s environmental services strategy and support the delivery of complex mission-critical infrastructure projects. This position can be based out of any of our HDR offices.

Position Summary

The TMT Environmental Lead
will serve as the primary environmental point of contact and subject matter expert for the TMT sector, helping clients navigate environmental, land use, permitting, and regulatory challenges associated with data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, digital campuses, fiber networks, and related technology developments. The role will support business development, project delivery, professional development, quality management, and strategic growth initiatives across HDR’s global TMT portfolio.

This position reports directly to the TMT Market Sector Director with additional indirect relationships with the TMT Business Development, TMT Practice, and Environmental Cross Sector Leadership teams and will collaborate extensively across Business Groups and regions to align environmental strategy with market objectives and client needs. The individual is expected to maintain strong client relationships and remain actively engaged in industry leadership and key project pursuits.

About HDR's TMT Market Sector

HDR is a global leader in architecture, engineering, environmental, and consulting services with a long-standing track record of successfully delivering mission-critical projects, including data centers around the world.

Our TMT teams provide comprehensive, end-to-end services ranging from site selection and due diligence through design, permitting, construction support, commissioning, retrofits, and operational optimization. We understand the unique requirements associated with mission-critical facilities and bring deep expertise in developing high-performing, future-ready campuses designed for reliability, performance, scalability, and operational resilience.

What sets HDR apart is the breadth and integration of our services. In addition to architecture and engineering, HDR provides stakeholder engagement, environmental planning and permitting, regulatory compliance, real estate services, utility coordination, acoustics, air quality, emissions consulting, and specialized technical advisory services. With global reach and multidisciplinary depth, HDR is uniquely positioned to help clients deliver rapidly expanding digital infrastructure programs while meeting environmental, regulatory, community, and operational objectives.

Primary Responsibilities

Market Leadership and Strategy

Develop and implement HDR's environmental strategy for the TMT Market Sector.
Support TMT market sector annual and long-range strategic planning initiatives.
Identify emerging market trends, permitting challenges, and regulatory developments affecting data center and telecommunications clients.
Help define HDR's market positioning and growth strategy for environmental permitting, planning, and compliance services within the TMT sector.
Partner with Client Development Leaders and Market Sector Leadership to expand HDR's environmental services footprint globally.
Serve as HDR's environmental ambassador within industry organizations, conferences, and client forums.

Environmental Permitting and Regulatory Leadership

Serve as HDR's primary point of contact and technical resource for environmental and land use permitting associated with data centers, telecommunications facilities, fiber infrastructure, network operations centers, and related technology developments.
Provide technical oversight and strategic guidance for permitting programs supporting greenfield and brownfield development projects.
Lead development of permitting strategies that support accelerated project delivery schedules while maintaining compliance with applicable regulations.
Support clients in obtaining approvals from federal, state, provincial, county, municipal, and other regulatory agencies.
Advise project teams regarding environmental review processes, permitting risks, mitigation strategies, and regulatory compliance requirements.
Monitor evolving environmental and land development regulations and communicate impacts to clients and HDR leadership.

Land Use and Development

Lead and support environmental planning and permitting efforts involving:

Land use approvals and entitlement strategies.
State, provincial, county, municipal, and local government permits and approvals.
Site access authorizations for construction and development activities.
Zoning reviews, zoning variances, rezoning applications, and zoning board approvals.
Conditional use permits and special use permits.
Easements, right-of-way approvals, and property access agreements.
Utility connection approvals and infrastructure coordination.
Building occupancy permits and certificates of occupancy.
Construction permits and development approvals for improved and unimproved lands.
Stakeholder engagement and public agency coordination.
Environmental due diligence and site feasibility assessments.

Business Development and Client Engagement

Build and maintain senior-level relationships with key TMT clients.
Support strategic pursuits, capture planning efforts, and major proposal activities.
Actively identify opportunities for environmental, planning, permitting, and regulatory services.
Collaborate with business development and technical leaders to develop integrated client solutions.
Participate in client meetings, executive presentations, and pursuit strategy workshops.
Serve as Project Principal, Technical Lead, or Strategic Advisor on select key projects.

Project Delivery and Technical Excellence

Promote best-in-class project delivery practices across the TMT environmental practice.
Support project teams in developing innovative approaches to complex permitting and entitlement challenges.
Provide quality oversight and participate in HDR's project review processes.
Foster consistency, technical excellence, and knowledge sharing across offices and regions.
Develop and implement best practices, tools, and guidance documents for environmental services delivery.

Team Development and Leadership

Mentor and develop environmental professionals supporting the TMT sector.
Assist with strategic recruitment and succession planning initiatives.
Foster collaboration between environmental practitioners, planners, engineers, architects, and market sector teams.
Support career development, technical training, and leadership development.
Help build a connected, high-performing practice across regions and business groups.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in environmental planning, environmental science, urban planning, engineering, public policy, or related discipline.
Minimum 10+ years of experience leading environmental planning, permitting, and regulatory programs for major infrastructure, industrial, technology, telecommunications, or mission-critical projects.
Demonstrated expertise in land use planning, development entitlements, and construction permitting.
Extensive experience obtaining approvals from state, provincial, county, municipal, and local regulatory agencies.
Demonstrated experience leading permitting programs for large, complex development projects with aggressive schedules.
Strong knowledge of permitting requirements associated with site development, utility infrastructure, zoning, occupancy approvals, and construction activities.
Proven ability to build and maintain executive-level client relationships.
Demonstrated success supporting business development, project pursuits, and strategic growth initiatives.
Experience supporting data center campus development projects.
Experience with telecommunications, fiber, wireless, or digital infrastructure development.
Established industry reputation within the technology, telecommunications, mission-critical, or land development sectors.
Experience presenting at industry conferences and participating in professional organizations.
Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary teams across multiple geographic regions.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed.

Success Measures

The successful TMT Environmental Lead will:

Establish HDR as the premier environmental and permitting advisor for data center and digital infrastructure development.
Build a cohesive, high-performing environmental practice aligned with TMT market growth objectives.
Expand client relationships and increase HDR's market share in mission-critical and digital infrastructure services.
Deliver innovative permitting and entitlement solutions that accelerate project delivery while maintaining regulatory compliance.
Advance technical excellence, professional development, and collaboration across HDR's environmental practice.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a Professional, Architecture, Engineering or closely related field
A minimum of 10 years of experience in related field
For Business Class leadership roles for which the core service being overseen is technical design, the role must maintain a professional or Architecture/Engineering registration and has related technical experience
Experienced in development and management of diverse teams
Works cooperatively with other business class directors, operations managers, technical directors and marketing managers on business class efforts
Committed to quality, improvement and HDR values
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. Job Description

CDM Smith is seeking candidates for a mid- to senior-level Sediment Remediation Engineer position. The candidate must have demonstrated expertise working independently as well as leading a team of engineers and/or scientists on sediment remediation projects for a variety of clients including those in the Federal and/or Public sector. Sediment remediation experience will be considered on an individual basis, but experience in the following bullets is preferred.

Roles And Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To

Providing expertise in evaluating the feasibility of sediment remediation technologies and preparing sediment remediation designs for riverine, coastal, riparian/floodplain, and/or port site settings involving multiple stakeholders.
Understanding the scientific and engineering principles of sediment and contaminant transport, environmental site assessment, sampling/monitoring technologies, cap modeling, dredge approaches, remedial action design, and/or remedial action construction.
Providing support of mathematical/statistical evaluations of environmental data sets.
Serving as CDM Smith’s task manager on various components of complicated sediments sites. This includes having the ability to assess and understand a problem, develop and communicate a technical strategy to the client, and interact effectively with CDM Smith subject matter experts.
Possessing an in-depth expertise in the various CERCLA, GLLA, and/or other regulatory program steps/processes at contaminated sediment sites.
Serving as a technical liaison with the client, general public, and/or outside consultants, including communicating complicated technical evaluations and/or designs to non-subject matter experts.
Leading other staff in preparing/reviewing/scrutinizing technical information to provide a document that is technically sound and that conforms to applicable regulations and policy.

Skills & Abilities

Expert Knowledge of computer assisted design and drafting (CADD) 3D and 4D software and practices. Expert Knowledge of engineer principles of design. Expert Knowledge of Microsoft business software (excel, word, etc.). Excellent verbal and written communications skills. Expert knowledge of federal, state and local regulations.

About Avy

At Avy we develop and operate innovative high-tech drones to improve lives worldwide.

We are a young, fast-growing, international organization that values sustainability, trust and friendship. We offer people a place where they can learn, fail, thrive and excel.

Avy pioneers unmanned aviation technology for emergency services, healthcare logistics, and security and intelligence. We partner with innovative organizations that are among the first in the world to integrate long-range drone operations into their daily workflows.

At Avy, you will be part of an amazing adventure (did we already mention that this adventure includes working on our rooftop terrace, behind the piano, in the sauna, at the bar, or on our disco toilet?)

About The Role

We are looking for a skilled drone regulations expert to join our Flight Operations team as Regulatory and Compliance Manager.

We hope to find a candidate who is equally excited to work on documentation, connect with authorities and stakeholders and be an active part of our team.

As Regulatory & Compliance Officer
you will bri ng valuable expertise on risk analysis and your talent for analytical thinking;
you will grow into understanding the drone ecosystem and help Avy to enable life-saving drone flights throughout Europe.

Define, design and arrange approval for new types of operations with the SORA methodology
Support with, check & approve flight plans together with Avy's pilots
Act as point of contact between Avy and the aviation authorities (such as ILT, LVNL, EASA,...)
Conduct advisory projects for Avy and Avy’s customers
Understand and work with our LUC
Stay aware of any updates released by EASA that are related to Avy and ensure Avy’s operations are compliant with these
Compare and work with different drone regulations around the world

At Avy’s Flight Operations team, our mission is the overall planning, directing, managing, and implementing of groundbreaking VTOL drone operations. Our main directive is to ensure we deliver our customers with a well-tested and smoothly operating VTOL system.

We strive to conduct all our flights at the highest level of safety, guarantee operations that comply with all applicable regulations and enable our customers to uphold the same standards.

We hope you get as much energy from innovative aerospace & drone technology as we do, and that you share our passion to apply this exciting technology to have a positive impact
You have an all round knowledge of the activities and processes in drones and/or aviation

Strong English and Dutch proficiency, written and spoken
EU citizenship or a EU work permit
Having the following certificates would be a big bonus: EASA A1/A3 and EASA A2 licence, SORA, ISO 9001

A warm atmosphere with regular drinks and celebrations
A work culture based on freedom and trust
An awesome office in Amsterdam with a maker space, sauna, disco-toilet, and delicious (vegetarian) lunches

Dudek’s journey began in 1980 with a vision to serve Southern California’s water and wastewater agencies.

Today, we are a 100% employee-owned firm supporting clients nationwide and delivering projects that improve and protect the built and natural environments of communities throughout the United States. Our work has been recognized by leading industry organizations , and we’ve been honored with multiple national Top Workplace Awards.

Our employee-owners are unified by a singular commitment to supporting projects that address key societal issues, such as the transition to renewable energy, infrastructure hardening and repair, environmental protection, and community resilience.

Learn more about our award-winning culture
, the benefits and perks
of being a Dudekian , and the projects
you will have the opportunity to shape.

Position Overview

Who You Are

As an employee-owner
, you embrace accountability, working safely, and collaboration while thinking resourcefully and independently.

Like all Dudekians , you are curious and solution-oriented
, with the ability to adapt quickly to changes and approach challenges with a spirit of innovation
.

How You’ll Make An Impact

A Geospatial Analyst II assists in the collection, management, analysis, and visualization of geospatial data to support environmental, planning, and engineering projects. This role will support field data collection efforts, geospatial analysis, cartography, and technical report preparation under the guidance of senior staff. A Geospatial Analyst II will possess a strong foundational knowledge of geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and spatial data interpretation, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills. We are open to candidates that can come to the office on a hybrid basis. Ideal locations would be in NorCal: Auburn, CA/Oakland, CA or SoCal: Santa Barbara, CA, Pasadena, CA or Encinitas, CA

Duties And Responsibilities

Geospatial Data Management and Processing

Compiles, processes, and manages GIS datasets, ensuring data integrity and organization.
Uses publicly available data sources and discipline-based data models to support geospatial analyses.
Maintains and updates geospatial databases using ESRI’s ArcGIS platform, including ArcGIS Online and Enterprise GIS.

Spatial Analysis and Mapping

Conducts geospatial analyses to support a variety of practices including biology, cultural, compliance and urban forestry.
Develops and produces high-quality maps, figures, and spatial visualizations for reports and presentations.
Works with lidar, imagery, and other remote sensing datasets to extract relevant geospatial information.

Field Data Collection and Integration

Assists in field data collection using mobile GIS applications.
Ensures accurate georeferencing and integration of collected data into GIS workflows.
Supports environmental and engineering field teams with real-time mapping solutions.

Project Support and Collaboration

Works closely with project managers and analysts to interpret GIS needs and provide geospatial solutions.
Leads small GIS projects and provides support for larger interdisciplinary projects.
Communicates GIS concepts effectively to non-GIS team members to support decision-making.

Compliance and Best Practices

Ensures all GIS workflows comply with industry standards, project requirements, and regulatory guidelines.
Follows best practices in GIS data management, cartography, and geospatial analysis.
Manages time effectively to balance multiple projects and understand budget constraints.

Minimum Qualifications

Experience: 3+ years’ experience working with GIS, remote sensing, or geospatial analysis through internships, academic projects, or professional work.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Geography, Environmental Science, Geospatial Science, GIS, Engineering, or a related field. Master’s degree is a plus.

Preferred Qualifications

Proficiency in ESRI’s ArcGIS platform, including ArcGIS Pro and related extensions, ArcGIS Online, and Enterprise GIS.
Experience in acquiring and processing geospatial databases.
Familiarity with data collection tools, including GPS, and remote sensing applications.
Experience working with Lidar and image processing is a plus.
Experience with Python, SQL, or R for geospatial automation and analysis is a plus.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent attention to detail and organizational abilities.
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and manage multiple tasks efficiently.

Compensation: $65-000-75,000/annually*

Your work will include leading complex geospatial date development, quality control, and integration efforts that ensure accurate location validation and vehicle routability; administering geospatial platforms; developing applications and web maps; and providing expert customer assistance to internal OSP users, partner agencies, and public safety stakeholders. This position works at the senior professional (ISS6) level, addressing projects that introduce new technology or business processes, resolving conflicting data and stakeholder needs, and requires coordination across multiple jurisdictions and vendors.

OR

A Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field

AND One (1) Year Of Information Systems Experience In

Geographic Information Systems (GIS), including development, maintenance, quality control, and analysis of geospatial data using the Esri ArcGIS platform in an enterprise environment.

Experience developing, maintaining, modeling, and quality-controlling enterprise GIS datasets, including topology, ETL/data integration from multiple sources, and standards compliance in support of critical operational systems.

Are you passionate about marine conservation and looking for a role where your work can make a real difference? Want to combine scientific research, hands-on fieldwork and aquarium-based conservation?

Our Conservation, Welfare & Education team delivers conservation and research projects across marine and freshwater environments and we’re now looking for a Conservation Researcher to help deliver our local conservation work, beginning with an exciting seagrass restoration project.

The Enviva team is driven by our shared vision for a renewable energy future. We are a fast-growing, purpose-driven, global energy company specializing in delivering sustainable wood bioenergy solutions. We are the world's largest producer of sustainable wood pellets, providing biogenic carbon solutions for power and heat generation, industrial processes, chemicals, and advanced biofuels worldwide.

Job Purpose

Enviva seeks a motivated and detail-oriented Geospatial Analyst I to join its Sustainability team. Reporting to the Lead Geospatial Specialist, this role will support the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of geospatial data used in forestry operations, supplier traceability, sustainability reporting, and field-to-office workflows.

The position will initially focus on data editing, quality assurance, established workflow execution, and operational GIS support. The successful candidate will be expected to identify recurring data problems, recognize opportunities to replace manual efforts with automation, and suggest practical workflow improvements.

This is an early-career position for someone with a strong GIS foundation who wants to develop their experience in geospatial data management, automation, remote-sensing outputs, and interactive reporting in a fast-moving, innovative department.

Responsibilities

Review geospatial and tabular data for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and adherence to established standards.
Identify, document, and communicate geometry, attribute, identifier, relationship, attachment, and data-model issues via spatial hosted feature services. This will commence with data corrections for review, progressing into assumed responsibility for data quality assurance.
Understand, run, and examine results of established geoprocessing tools, scripts, SQL queries, data updates, and QA/QC checks.
Maintain authoritative tract, stand, supplier, and related operational datasets.
Investigate GIS application and workflow issues, with ability to distinguish incorrect source data, user error, and system flaws.
Provide first-line support for Field Maps and other operational GIS applications, escalating issues when appropriate.
Support supplier-data intake, standardization, validation, and loading into established GIS datasets.
Work with the Sustainability Analyst and operational teams to document, assign, track, and resolve identified data issues.
Support development and maintenance of geospatial error-flagging system for managing discrepancies, corrections, and recurring data-quality trends.
Support changes to field-to-office workflows and help implement attribute rules, validation processes, and data-enrichment methods.
Produce standalone maps and GIS data deliverables upon request.
Identify repetitive manual processes and recommend opportunities for improved efficiency, consistency, or automation.
Document workflows, processing decisions, identified issues, and completed corrections.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, geography, forestry, natural resources, environmental science, civil engineering, information systems, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
Two to four years of relevant GIS experience.
Ability to independently edit data, run geoprocessing tools, perform basic spatial analysis, and produce maps in ArcGIS Pro.
Understanding of feature classes, tables, joins, relates, coordinate systems, coordinate geometry, and common geospatial data formats.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify inconsistencies in spatial and tabular data.
Ability to investigate routine GIS problems, document findings, and seek guidance when needed.
Strong organizational, communication, and collaboration skills

Preferred Qualifications - What Will Set Them Apart

Experience in forestry, natural resources, utilities, civil engineering, conservation, or other field involving real-world spatial data.
Familiarity with forest-material operations, mobile data collection, or field-to-office workflows.
Experience with ArcGIS Online, hosted feature layers, web maps, Field Maps, GNSS survey equipment, photogrammetry, Survey123, or Dashboards.
Experience with SQL, ETL processes, schema mapping, or data validation.
Exposure to Python or another scripting language.
Familiarity with imagery, remote sensing, parcel data, or environmental datasets.

This role follows a hybrid schedule. Four days of in-office work per week will be expected during the initial onboarding and integration period, transitioning to a hybrid schedule of 2–3 days in-office per week once sufficiently integrated into the role.

Physical Requirements

Primarily computer-based work requiring extended periods of sitting and/or standing at a computer and typing.

Brief Job Description

The Research Specialist V performs highly advanced (senior-level) research and data dissemination work under minimal supervision, with extensive latitude for the use of independent initiative and judgment. This position designs and implements research and analytical studies; assesses the validity of statistical methods for appropriate application; plans and/or conducts highly advanced research on Medicaid, CHIP; and other agency programs, and applies advanced statistical and/or spatial data analyses techniques to health and human services related data.

Provides consultation and assistance to HHSC staff and other HHS agencies to develop methods and strategies for more effective reporting of data and analyses. Designs, builds, and maintains advanced scripts and code for computer based spatial analysis applications including data acquisition and cleaning. Prepares and presents a variety of reports, studies, and other deliverables containing analyses of health and human services data to agency management, policy analysts, the Legislature, and external customers to provide an understanding of health and human service agencies' programs and issues, including evaluating Managed Care Organizations compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements. Evaluates available spatial datasets and determines which are most appropriate for specific research projects.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Attends work on a regular and predictable schedule in accordance with agency leave policy and performs other duties as assigned.

EJF 1: Designs and conducts advanced research and analysis projects specific to Medicaid, CHIP, and other agency programs. Gathers data from multiple sources and performs transformation or pre-analytic processing as required. Ensures location data is accurately geocoded and/or configured for spatial analysis. Types of analyses include spatial distribution of clients, Medicaid providers and licensed practioners, assessing provider network adequacy, evaluating contract compliance, trend and anomaly detection and program change evaluation. (25%)

EJF 2: Works with MCDA Data Management staff to develop and maintain information systems to support ongoing research and analysis. Investigates and validates available reliable data sources, acquires, cleans, and transforms data as needed, reviews, plans and designs research and analyses requiring specialized methods to relate Medicaid/CHIP program and service area objectives to location-based information data and sources. Operates and maintains spatial data systems and programs in Windows and other environments, including evaluation, selection, installation, updates, and upgrades. This includes geocoding, editing, creating, maintaining, displaying, updating, and overlaying a wide variety of data and geographic layers to display the most appropriate and intuitive interpretation of Medicaid/chip related data. Documentation and database management for geospatial purposes are involved. (25%)

EJF 3: Effective professional consultation and collaboration with Medicaid/CHIP division and agency staff and researchers, governmental entities, and other stakeholders for the creation of high-quality research reports, including professional maps. Leads and participates in workgroups to identify the needs in the program areas, and review, develop and design spatial analyses to answer the questions and provide analysis. Communicates effectively with other analysts to share work details, develop plans, devise clear instructions, and formulates cogent inquiries. Presents a variety of graphs, maps, reports, and studies to Medicaid/CHIP staff, agency policy and executive decision makers, the Texas Legislature, and other stakeholders to demonstrate the patterns, trends, and anomalies on provider networks, clients’ services, and program utilization. The information is presented to Medicaid/CHIP leadership and is communicated to stakeholders and managed care organizations to improve program management and service delivery. (20%)

EJF 4: Performs project management functions. Leads and participates in meetings with customers to establish and clarify research and analytical goals, questions, and requirements. Ensures data sources and processes are well documented; that they include accurate technical details for analysts as well as non-technical descriptions appropriate for customers. (20%)

EFJ 5: Evaluates and monitors developments and advancements in GIS and statistical software and recommends the most appropriate software and solutions for research projects and analyses. Designs, develops, implements, and maintains custom-coded applications for data management, cleaning, transformations, and improvements that add efficiencies and accuracy to research and analyses projects. (10%)

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

List the knowledge, skills, and abilities critical to performance in this position:

Knowledge of advanced research concepts and methodologies.

Knowledge of advanced geospatial analysis and geographic information system concepts and

methods.

Knowledge of cartographic principles, techniques, and procedures.

Knowledge of advanced database management and query methods and systems.

Knowledge of structured programing concepts.

Knowledge of techniques for developing applications and publications for the Internet.

Knowledge of appropriate surveillance techniques for population-based research.

Skill in the use of ArcGIS software.

Skill in the use of Office365 software programs.

Skill in the use of personal computers.

Skill in the use of global positioning systems.

Skill in the use of large format plotters.

Skill in map composition.

Skill in the use of database systems, including SQL Server and Oracle.

Skill in building datasets for use with visualization software such as Tableau and Power BI.

Skill using statistical analysis software such as SAS and R

Skill in programming and scripting languages, such as Python, Visual Basic or PowerShell.

Skill in written and verbal communication for private, public, and professional group interactions.

Skill applying programming techniques to the analysis of large data sets.

Skill in designing, building, implementing and maintain automatic computer processes for data

acquisition, cleaning, transformation, loading and querying.

Skill and experience in the use of Structured Query Language (SQL) and reporting tools.

Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships, set priorities, and manage time

efficiently.

Ability to exercise good judgment, efficiently organize information and effectively solve problems.

Ability to communicate both verbal and written technical and analytical information to audiences from

diverse backgrounds with a wide range in levels of expertise.

Four years’ experience with data acquisition, data collection, management, analyses, visualization and presentation of health and human services-related data or large datasets.

Pay Range is the entire compensation range for the position.

The first review of applications will be on 08/28/2026.

The Pima County Department of Environmental Quality is seeking an Environmental Planner to assist with moderately complex environmental planning and rules analysis. This position will assist with the Department's rule writing and rule making process including drafting environmental rules through synthesizing information provided by the respective environmental program(s) into effective and concise proposed rules language. This role will also assist Department leadership with planning rule development and implementation strategies for the Department. The Environmental Planner is expected to have the ability to conduct formal rulemakings that include meaningful public processes (i.e. stakeholder meetings, public hearings, etc.). Additionally, the selected candidate must have the ability to understand and apply environmental rules and statutes; to follow guidance documents, standard operating procedures, and other technical instructions in performance of tasks; and to summarize completed tasks and/or monitoring data orally and in written communication.

Essential Functions

As defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act, this classification may include any of the following tasks, knowledge, skills, and other characteristics. This list is ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY and is not a comprehensive listing of all functions and tasks performed by incumbents of this class. Work assignments may vary depending on the department’s need and will be communicated to the applicant or incumbent by the supervisor.

Manages and supervises field operations for environmental monitoring programs, ensuring proper site maintenance, staff oversight, and adherence to safety protocols;
Leads and executes environmental planning and regulatory rulemaking processes to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental laws;
Interprets and applies federal regulations, particularly EPA QA requirements under 40 CFR Parts 50, 53, and 58, to align organizational practices with compliance standards;
Implements and maintains quality assurance systems, including QAPPs, SOPs, and Quality Management Plans, to ensure the integrity and defensibility of environmental data;
Conducts data validation and assessment, performing Level II reviews, statistical analysis, and certification audits to uphold the accuracy and usability of monitoring data;
Provides QA oversight and guidance, reviewing operations, issuing quality control directives, and coordinating corrective actions to resolve data or procedural deficiencies;
Manages program logistics and resources, including procurement, equipment tracking, permitting workflows, and budgeting processes;
Supports staff development, overseeing training programs and offering technical assistance to promote consistent understanding and implementation of QA practices;
Coordinates with stakeholders, engaging public water systems, agencies, and community representatives to foster collaboration, resolve issues, and facilitate access to resources;
Conducts regulatory reviews and field inspections, including well siting, septic system evaluations, water sampling, and sewage investigations to protect public health;
Manages administrative and reporting duties, from fee invoicing and CCR reviews to system activations, exemption determinations, and participation in regional work groups and meetings.

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a major in environmental science, biology, engineering or another program-related field, as defined by the department head at the time of recruitment AND four years of professional level experience in coordinating, monitoring, administering or managing program or specialized work unit activities.

(Relevant professional level experience and/or education from an accredited college or university may be substituted.)

Or

Two years of experience with Pima County as a Program Coordinator or other related position as determined by the department head at the time of recruitment.

Qualifying education and experience must be clearly documented in the "Education" and "Work Experience" sections of the application. Do not substitute a resume for your application or write "see resume" on your application.

Experience in research, evaluation and/or interpretation of federal, state and/or local environmental regulations necessary for an environmental rule making process.
Experience in professional writing to effectively communicate and document rule changes.
Experience in coordinating and hosting public meetings, hearings, and presentations for the regulated community and general public with the objective of achieving effective rulemaking changes.
Experience in collaborating with technical staff and/or various environmental programs to ensure proposed rules and regulations contain accurate and applicable information.
Experience in professional planning in environmental and/or technical programs.

jobs.description:
About Insignia Environmental

Insignia Environmental (Insignia) is a collaborative, fast-paced growing environmental consulting firm full of bright, motivated employees. Our services are focused on the unique needs of energy projects, including renewables, electricity, and gas. We pride ourselves on being solution-oriented and go beyond traditional environmental review and permitting to leverage innovative concepts and technology to deliver results for our clients. Our reputation in the industry precedes us, and we are extremely proud of it!

Why Join Us?

We love our employees, listen to their input, and strive to take care of them. We are constantly investing in and providing opportunities for development and growth through internal training programs and our professional development program. We frequently gather for teambuilding events to strengthen our relationships and celebrate our employees’ milestones. We value giving back to our community and hold several volunteer events for our employees every year.

In support of our goal of being the best place to work, Insignia offers a casual, flexible work environment with generous benefits, including a 401(k)-equivalent program, medical insurance (including partial coverage for significant others and dependents), and an above-industry amount of paid time off that escalates with tenure. Our canine friends are invited to “work” in the office with us!

Position Details

Insignia is seeking a Lead Environmental Specialist/Planner with Qualified SWPPP Developer and Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSD/QSP) certifications to support projects across Northern California. This is a full-time, hybrid role that includes regular travel for site visits and field inspections, with occasional overnight stays depending on project location.

Applicants must be based in California. While the preferred reporting locations is our Menlo Park office, we will consider candidates located elsewhere in Northern California who are not within a reasonable commuting distance. In these cases, remote work will be supported for technical and project management tasks when not in the field.

Prepare SWPPPs under the State Water Resources Control Board’s General Construction Permit Order 2022-0057-DWQ, including site best management practices maps.
Conduct regular SWPPP inspections, including pre-, during-, and post-rain event assessments, and water quality sampling during storm events.
Coordinate with project personnel, environmental inspectors, and hazardous materials specialists to ensure compliance with water quality mitigation measures.
Manage SWPPP documentation, inspection reports, project changes, equipment logs, and spill logs.
Develop permitting assessments, prepare permit applications, and support compliance management during project construction.
Assist with environmental impact analyses under the California Environmental Quality Act/National Environmental Policy Act (CEQA/NEPA), including preparation of planning documents, environmental review documents, and resource agency permits (e.g., Clean Water Act Section 404/401 and Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements).
Support the completion of environmental deliverables in accordance with approved budgets and schedules.
Participate in internal and client meetings related to project progress and milestones.
Collaborate with peers and provide clients with technical advice and guidance regarding compliance with environmental regulations.
Provide technical review and quality control of environmental assessment documents, permit application packages, technical studies, and related client deliverables.

Requirements

Bachelor of Science degree or higher in hydrology, earth sciences, environmental science, environmental planning, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in environmental consulting, with demonstrated experience in project management support and field inspection roles.
Must hold QSD and QSP certifications.
Additional certifications preferred, including Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control, Professional Engineer, or Professional Geologist.
Working knowledge of regulations pertaining to environmental protection, including CEQA/NEPA, the Clean Water Act, and the Endangered Species Act.
Previous experience participating in the management of projects, including client interaction, technical review of deliverables, schedule, and budget controls.
Demonstrated ability to complete projects on time and within budget.
Excellent communication and organizational skills, as well as confidence in dealing with clients, regulators, and team members.
Ability to exercise informed and independent decision-making.
Excellent writing and technical editing skills, with advanced experience in the Microsoft Office suite.
Rigorously detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy.

Other

Valid driver’s license and good driving record.
Ability to travel as needed for field inspections and project meetings.
Ability to perform physical tasks, including walking/hiking in varying terrain and working in inclement weather conditions.
Ability to lift up to 25 pounds.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and location. The annualized salaried range for this position is $70,000 to $95,000.
Insignia is proud to offer a comprehensive benefits program to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Insignia’s benefits include medical, dental, vision, life, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absence, voluntary benefits, employee assistance program, retirement savings plan, and bonuses.

Insignia is committed to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace where every team member can thrive. If you are passionate about making a difference in the environment and want to join a team that values excellence and camaraderie, we would love to hear from you!

Job Summary

The Environmental Engineering role performs a broader range of environmental engineering tasks related to the analysis, planning, and development of solutions that promote environmental protection, water use sustainability, and responsible water resource management. Working under general supervision of a professional engineer, this role contributes to technical work that improves environmental and public health outcomes across natural and engineered systems. This engineering position addresses environmental and public health protection, mitigation, and prevention of degradation of water, soils, air quality, and habitats. This role may work in one or more diverse areas including water and wastewater treatment and conveyance, stormwater management, solid waste management, hazardous waste management, and related areas. This role conducts analysis, planning, modeling, and design of treatment systems, preparing results, recommendations, plan sets, and other engineering deliverables.

Responsibilities

Perform technical analyses to support identification and evaluation of sustainable water and wastewater management solutions.
Prepare and review technical reports and documentation related to environmental engineering projects.
Assist in the planning and design of environmental protection systems to support public and ecosystem health.
Contribute to facility, watershed, or strategic resource management plans.
Analyze scientific and engineering data and perform quality control checks to support regulatory compliance.
Provide technical support for environmental projects, including modeling of treatment and conveyance systems, vendor coordination, and technical input for permitting and regulatory approvals.
Flexibility to adapt and execute various additional assignments based on evolving needs.

Mentorship

May provide mentorship, guidance, support, and knowledge-sharing to help less experienced team members develop their skills and grow within their roles.

Skills and Competencies

Working knowledge of environmental engineering principles and standard practices.
Developing problem‑solving and analytical skills.
Ability to interpret scientific and engineering data with accuracy and attention to detail.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Experience

Typically, a minimum of 2 years of related work experience in Environmental Engineering or related field.
Typically certified in the SMS Framework, and progressing through the SMS competencies.

Education

A bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering or related field is required.

Ability to support environmental engineering work involving operational data management, performance monitoring, and evaluation of water, wastewater, recycled water, or advanced treatment facilities.
Familiarity with dashboards, visualization tools, historian data, operational records, laboratory results, and other facility datasets used to communicate treatment system performance.
Understanding of key water treatment metrics, including production, recovery, flow, pressure, chemical use, membrane productivity, normalized performance, and related operating trends.
Ability to support advanced water treatment and membrane operational evaluations, including cleaning performance, membrane integrity, fouling assessments, troubleshooting, process optimization, and asset reliability reviews.

Experience developing or supporting dashboards, automated calculations, reports, or visualization tools that reduce manual data processing and improve access to decision-ready information.
Experience supporting membrane system operational evaluations, including review of transmembrane pressure, flux, permeability, recovery, differential pressure, specific flux, cleaning frequency, and production trends.

Post Date

8/18/2026

Details

ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OCCUPATIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH

The Department of Occupational and Environmental Health at the Hudson College of Public Health, University of Oklahoma Health Campus is hiring a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor.

Environmental And/or Occupational Epidemiology

We are seeking candidates whose work integrates emerging analytic techniques to address one or more of the following focus areas:

Environmental exposures linked to cancer outcomes,
Military and defense-related environmental exposures,
Environmental health concerns of Native American populations and tribes,
Children's environmental health, and/or
Water, food, and air quality impacts on population health.

Required Qualifications

Doctoral degree (Doctor of Philosophy, Doctor of Science, or Doctor of Public Health) in environmental health, industrial hygiene, environmental science, environmental engineering or a closely related field.
Record of publications in peer-reviewed national or international scholarly journals.
Evidence of potential to obtain extramural funding.
For the rank of Associate Professor, a history of external research funding.

Preferences

Established record of teaching at the graduate level
A record of mentoring graduate students, particularly from diverse backgrounds.
Experience in applying emerging analytical techniques (e.g. Big Data, AI, machine learning, geospatial modeling) to public health and environmental data.
Experience working on interdisciplinary or community-engaged research teams.

Application Instructions

Applicants must submit applications through Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/187378.
Applicants are required to provide a CV and cover letter, and three professional references with contact information. For questions about the positions, please contact Misty Wilson at Misty-Wilson@ou.edu.

The ideal candidates meet the required qualifications as an Assistant or Associate Professor and have a documented track record of extramurally funded research. They will contribute to the continued growth and excellence of the department and the university, supporting the University of Oklahoma's strategic plan to lead as a top-tier public research university and to meet AAU-level benchmarks for research, teaching, and service. This individual will contribute to expanding the program across the state with a strong commitment to student-centered values and respect for the student experience.

About Oklahoma City

Oklahoma City is the anchor of a rapidly growing, multicultural metropolitan area with a population of 1.3 million, over 300 days of sunshine annually, very affordable cost of living, excellent schools and a wide array of cultural amenities. The city boasts a strong job market with opportunities in sectors like energy, healthcare, and technology, making it ideal for professionals and families alike. Plus, our revitalized downtown area features arts, entertainment, and local events. To learn more about this impressive city, please take a few minutes to watch this short video.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

The University, in compliance with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations, does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, genetic information, gender identity/expression (consistent with applicable law), age (40 or older), religion, disability, political beliefs, or status as a veteran in any of its policies, practices, or procedures. This includes but is not limited to admissions, employment, housing, financial aid, and educational services.

Why You Belong At The University Of Oklahoma

The University of Oklahoma values our community's unique talents, perspectives, and experiences. At OU, we aspire to harness our innovation, creativity, and collaboration for the advancement of people everywhere. You Belong Here!

About The University Of Oklahoma Health Campus

The University of Oklahoma Health Campus is one of the most comprehensive academic health centers in the nation. Located near the vibrant and growing downtown area of Oklahoma City, it is one of only a few academic medical centers in the nation with seven schools of health in contiguous space (Public Health, Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, Allied Health, and Graduate College). It also includes several strategic research centers, institutes, and initiatives to promote research and encourage collaboration among researchers across various disciplines. These include Oklahoma's only National Cancer Institute-Designated Cancer Center, the Stephenson Cancer Center, the Oklahoma Clinical and Translational Science Institute, the Harold Hamm Diabetes Center, the Oklahoma Center for Microbial Pathogenesis, and the Oklahoma Center for Geosciences.

The latest Blue Ridge Institute for Medical Research rankings place OU Health at No. 102 in the nation for funding from the National Institutes of Health - our highest ranking ever. This 27-spot climb over the past two years places OU among the top 3.6% of all 2,838 institutions and entities that receive NIH funding.

Collectively, OU Health Campus researchers received $75.2 million in NIH funding in FY2024, as classified by Blue Ridge.

About The Hudson College Of Public Health

The Hudson College of Public Health, founded in 1967, is Oklahoma's only accredited college of public health and one of just 68 accredited institutions in the U.S. It plays a crucial role in health education and research, offering a top-tier education that prepares students for successful careers in public health practice and research. With a global alumni network spanning all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and 27 countries, and an international student body comprising 10% of the total, the college emphasizes a mission-driven approach to protect and improve health through education, workforce development, research, service, and advocacy.

Located on a vibrant health sciences campus, the Hudson College of Public Health, led by Dr. Dale W. Bratzler, fosters a welcoming culture that values respect and belonging. This environment promotes innovation and collaboration, empowering students to excel in accredited, research-based academic programs with a favorable student-to-faculty ratio.

The college's purpose is to promote healthier tomorrows through education and research today. The Strategic Plan for 2023-2028 emphasizes national recognition in public health research, leading educational and workforce development initiatives, improving health outcomes, and enhancing partnerships to strengthen the impact of its education and services. Through integrated planning and self-studies, the Hudson College of Public Health is committed to continuous improvement and academic excellence in its pursuit of advancing public health.

The Department of Occupational and Environmental Health at the Hudson College of Public Health has been in existence for the past 51 years and has graduated 250 doctoral and master's students. The Department has developed flexible and diversified programs of graduate study, field training, and basic and applied research to accommodate students with a wide range of academic and occupational backgrounds.

Students in the Department seek MS, MPH, and PhD degrees. The industrial hygiene program within the Department has been continuously accredited by ABET since 1994 and continuously supported by a NIOSH-funded training grant since 2004. Faculty are actively developing community engaged research agendas which have led to an EPA-funded Children's Environmental Health Center in U.S. Southern Great Plains and a research contract with the state health department. Faculty members in the Department have received several multi-year grants and contracts from NASA, NSF, CDC, EPA, State Health Department, Oklahoma Department of Commerce, and the Oklahoma Center for the Advancement of Science & Technology (OCAST).

Insignia Environmental (Insignia) is a collaborative, fast-paced growing environmental consulting firm full of bright, motivated employees. This senior-level position involves managing multidisciplinary teams, directing the preparation of environmental documents and regulatory permit applications, and serving as a primary liaison with clients and regulatory agencies. Apply expert-level knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations to guide project strategy and ensure compliance.

Assign, oversee, and manage technical staff and subconsultants while providing guidance and performance feedback.
Ensure environmental deliverables meet project requirements, agency expectations, and Insignia’s quality standards within budget and schedule constraints.

Support proposal development and business development efforts by contributing to scopes of work, budgets, and client outreach.
Maintain and advance professional knowledge through training, conferences, and industry engagement.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or higher in environmental science, biology, ecology, environmental planning, or a related field.
Minimum of 8 years of professional experience in a similar role, with experience in environmental consulting strongly preferred, and at least 5 years in a senior-level planner or project manager position.
Extensive knowledge of and experience with the CEQA, NEPA, and other relevant federal and state environmental regulations, including the Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
Proven ability to manage complex regulatory projects involving environmental permitting, environmental review, interagency coordination, and client engagement.
Technical expertise in one or more environmental disciplines, such as biology fields (e.g., botany, wildlife, wetlands), environmental policy, or land use planning.
Familiarity with California ecosystems, species, and regulatory environments.
Experience leading and mentoring teams of scientists or technical professionals, including supervision and workload coordination.
Strong record of delivering high-quality work within scope, budget, and schedule across multiple concurrent projects.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. Confidence and professionalism in interactions with clients, regulators, and internal teams.
Proficiency in preparing and reviewing technical documents with meticulous attention to detail and accuracy.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word and Excel.
Ability to make informed, independent decisions and manage competing priorities in a fast-paced consulting environment.

Other

Valid driver’s license and good driving record.
Willingness and ability to travel when needed.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The annual salary range for this position is $100,000 to $170,000.

Spatial Awareness: A good sense of spatial awareness is essential for maneuvering through traffic, parking, and other driving-related tasks. No History of Seizures or Blackouts: A history of seizures or blackouts could pose a risk while driving. Employers may have restrictions regarding these conditions.

Position Overview

This position is responsible for supporting environmental compliance projects across New England, from initiation through completion. This role involves coordinating and participating in stormwater sampling and inspection activities, preparing and implementing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans, performing comprehensive environmental compliance audits, and supporting other project-specific permitting obligations. The role combines technical fieldwork with office responsibilities to ensure that operational practices, documentation, and reporting meet stringent regulatory requirements. This position also supports mentoring junior staff and strengthening the firm’s overall environmental compliance capabilities.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering or related field.
6+ years in environmental consulting with demonstrated interest and progression in environmental compliance or permitting.
Strong working knowledge of relevant state-level regulations (New England region) and federal programs.
Experience implementing environmental compliance programs across multiple sites and coordinating with internal staff, vendors, clients, regulators and other stakeholders.
Demonstrated task/project management skills.
Intermediate data evaluation and analytical skills.
Excellent technical writing and communication skills.
Strong documentation and organizational skills.
Experience with common technical protocols and regulatory requirements.
Ability and willingness to support the technical growth of staff level professionals.
OSHA 40-hr HAZWOPER preferred.
Experience with EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX) platform (e.g., NetDMR and NetMSGP) preferred.

Essential Duties

Manage, coordinate and/or conduct routine stormwater compliance activities including inspections, sampling and reporting under the EPA’s MSGP and/or other NPDES program requirements, including the evaluation of field data to identify and determine future client needs and project requirements.
Develop, implement and update SWPPPs.
Prepare, maintain and audit SPCC plans.
Conduct routine site inspections to evaluate environmental compliance programs (stormwater, SPCC, air, hazardous waste) and make recommendations to address program deficiencies, as necessary.
Provide project management (scope development, scheduling and budget tracking) for compliance programs, including invoicing and general project administration.
Prepare regulatory reports and other submittals including DMRs.
Conduct regulatory research and permitting for miscellaneous client requests.
Support air permitting evaluations, regulatory research, compliance documentation, and preparation of related permit applications or submittals.
Conduct third-party reviews of permit applications to evaluate adequacy in conformance with local, state, and federal regulations.
Participate in the development of junior staff and work with senior management to continue to grow as a consultant and leader of the firm.

Physical Demands/Work Environment Conditions

This position works in the field as well as the office environment. In the field, candidate will be working independently or leading a larger team at exterior project sites to perform compliance audits, sample collection, recording of operational/meter parameters, and potentially oversight of subcontractors. Job Description

Are you an experienced environmental due diligence consultant, skilled in uncovering environmental risks and turning technical findings into clear, actionable advice for decision-makers? Do you enjoy working across EHS and ESG topics to help shape sustainable outcomes for transactions and post-acquisition strategies? Are you a detail-focused communicator who thrives on fast-paced due diligence work, site visits, and collaborative problem-solving?

If this sounds like you, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our CST Due Diligence UK & Ireland team as our new Principal Environmental Consultant- Due Diligence and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

As a Principal Environmental Consultant for Due Diligence (DD), you will be part of our busy UK transactions team supporting fast-paced UK and global M&A transactions. You will assist with the identification of key EHS and ESG risks and opportunities and provide high-quality, targeted advice to clients on both buy-side and sell-side due diligence projects

Our team advises on transactions across a wide range of sectors, typically including industrial, commercial and infrastructure assets and businesses, often for finance sector clients. We work closely with in-house specialists across several EHS and ESG disciplines to provide targeted due diligence advice. Our clients use this advice to support negotiations during the bidding process and o to make informed impactful decisions on sustainability priorities post-acquisition. 

You will play a key role in the team, principally delivering due diligence assessments, while also supporting project management and the development of client proposals. 

Your key responsibilities will be:

Preparation of proposals, including pricing/budgets and timescales. Participation in client discussions and support with developing new client relationships.
Project Management and coordination of medium to large projects including multi-site projects over several geographies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence.
Delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and Limited Environmental Compliance Review(LECR) assessments for a range of sites, including more complex manufacturing facilities; including participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing focussed client reports. 
Delivery of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) assessments of companies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence. This will include desk-based research (review of data rooms and publicly available information), participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing client focussed reports.

About You

Relevant degree/qualifications. Ideally in environmental studies/geography or similar.
Sound understanding of UK environmental regulations and an understanding of key environmental and sustainability regulations in Europe.
7 to 12 years of practical work experience in other companies where you have personally been involved in the delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments, LECR assessments, ideally including to ASTM standards, and ideally also ESG assessments. Have the ability to understand information quickly and work efficiently, proactively and autonomously.
Experience in supporting the preparation of proposals.  
Strong communication skills (both written and verbal), and be comfortable engaging with external clients and advisors.
Project Management experience.
A collaborative approach and willingness to travel, typically within the UK and Ireland.

Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles
A culture that welcomes you as the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
Flexible work environment
27 days annual leave plus bank holidays

Dewberry’s Geospatial and Technology Services creates geospatial and analytical solutions for real world engineering, environmental, and community problems. Dewberry is a leading, market-facing professional services firm with more than 60 locations and 2,500 professionals nationwide. What sets us apart from our competitors is our people. Are you a GIS Road Warrior with a spirit of adventure? At TelCom Construction, we are looking for a dedicated GIS Technician – Underground Fiber to join our team. Location: Must reside in Minnesota (reporting base out of Blooming Prairie/Rochester, MN area.)
