About The Role

At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future. Department Summary: MITRE’s Model-Based Analytics Department (L144) is looking for qualified applicants to bring their geospatial, machine learning, advanced analytics, and applied research skills to bear on solving problems of critical national importance. MITRE’s diverse work program provides opportunities to apply your expertise and creative thinking in challenging domains such as healthcare, transportation, and national security. Employees may also participate in MITRE’s internal research and development program, which provides funding for innovative applied research that addresses our sponsors’ hardest problems. Our department is an interdisciplinary department that thrives on having a large toolbox to support data- and model-driven decision making. We value people who can bring diverse and inclusive perspectives. Our department works to solve modeling and analytic problems in the public interest, in partnership with the government. We also actively conduct independent research in areas of interest to our government partners. If you are passionate about being a Data Scientist that specializes in Geospatial Information Sciences, your skill sets align with our capabilities, and you like working in a collaborative, team-oriented environment, we want to hear from you! Roles & Responsibilities: The successful candidate for this position is a geospatial data scientist who combines a solid theoretical and technical background with the ability to formulate problems, develop and evaluate solutions, and communicate results. Familiarity with advanced geospatial data science, modeling, and analysis techniques and methods (e.g., supervised and unsupervised machine learning, GeoAI, Geosimulation, patiotemporal graphs) is a plus. Hands-on software development skills are a must. Candidates should have a strong understanding of how to engineer spatial solutions for geospatial systems and architecture in both traditional and cloud computing environments. Lifelong learning and keeping up with the latest research and technologies is an essential part of working in this field. Roles and responsibilities include: Support the development of geospatial data science, modeling, analysis, visualization, and engineering deliverables for sponsor projects and programs, internal research and development, and corporate strategic initiatives. Remain current on open-source, industry, academia, and US Government techniques and tools for geospatial data science, modeling, analysis, visualization, and engineering. Apply a variety of spatial data science techniques to tackle customer challenges to include geospatial statistics, spatial optimization, spatial pattern analysis, geospatial artificial intelligence, spatial autocorrelation, activity-based intelligence, imagery analysis, remote sensing, and geospatial data visualization approaches. Build and test geospatial prototypes in MITRE, government, and commercial cloud environments. Basic Qualifications: Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 3 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience. Bachelor’s degree in Geospatial Data Science, Geospatial Intelligence, Geographic Information Systems, GeoInformatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or related degree. Applied experience with common GIS tools, developing geospatial workflows, and visualizations using Python. Applied experience in spatial analysis and modeling, and ETL of spatiotemporal datasets and managing spatial databases. Applied experience in the configuration of web-mapping, dashboard applications, and remotely sensed data. Familiarity with geostatistics, spatial machine learning, geosimulation, or GeoAI, and multispectral and hyperspectral imagery or synthetic aperture radar. Familiarity working with spatiotemporal data in graph databases, such as ArcGIS Knowledge, Neo4j, or ArangoDB. Familiarity developing web applications with common libraries, e.g. OpenLayers, Leaflet, ArcGIS JS API. Familiarity with geospatial data architectures and spatial database design and management, as well as containerization concepts. Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance. This position requires a minimum of 3 days on-site. Preferred Qualifications: Active TS/SCI with polygraph. Advanced degree in Geospatial Data Science, Geospatial Intelligence, Geographic Information Systems, GeoInformatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or related technical discipline. Experience leading technical development across multi-disciplinary teams. Applied experience with other software development languages, e.g., C++, Java, C#, JavaScript. Applied experience with spatiotemporal big data technologies, e.g., GeoMesa, GeoTrellis, Data Bricks, or GeoSpark (Apache Sedona). Applied experience with data architecture containerization concepts, e.g. Docker or Kubernetes. Applied experience working with remotely sensed data to include aerial and satellite imagery, multi- and hyper-spectral imagery, LiDAR, or synthetic aperture radar. Applied experience with applying spatial modeling and analysis techniques to the atmospheric, climate, marine, oceanic, hydrologic, geomorphologic, critical infrastructure, transportation, network, telemetry, or terrain domains. Experience leading or conducting research. Experience designing geospatial data science tasking and/or leading a team of geospatial data scientists. Applied experience with developing web applications with common libraries, e.g., OpenLayers, Leaflet, ArcGIS JS API. Familiarity implementing DevSecOps, DataOps, or Applied experience in architecting, resourcing, deploying, and administering a GID enterprise including physical and virtual machines, cloud-based components, and remote application delivery serving hundreds of users Applied experience maintaining multiple enterprise relations database management systems hosted in MS SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Oracle or similar. This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s): None This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s): Top Secret/SCI Salary compensation range and midpoint: $124,400 - $155,500 - $186,600 Annual Work Location Type: Onsite Commitment to Non-Discrimination All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local or international law. MITRE intends to maintain a website that is fully accessible to all individuals. If you are unable to search or apply for jobs and would like to request a reasonable accommodation for any part of MITRE’s employment process, please email recruitinghelp@mitre.org for general support and collegerecruiting@mitre.org for intern positions. The Environmental and Social (E&S) Manager is responsible for ensuring that ACWA and assets in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia comply with applicable Saudi environmental, labor, occupational health and safety, and social requirements, as well as international lender standards. jobs.description:
Company Description
Prism Specialty Restoration provides residential and commercial specialty contents restoration, supporting homeowners, businesses, contractors, and insurance professionals. The company focuses on restoring electronics, art, documents, and textiles using safety-focused, proven processes. Prism delivers consistent quality, cost-effective outcomes, and turnaround times that align with claims and broader restoration timelines. The team prioritizes transparency, clear communication, and documented restoration from pickup through delivery. Every item is treated with care and urgency to reduce downtime and help customers return to normal as quickly as possible.
Role Description
The Document Restoration Management role is a full-time, on-site position based in Indianapolis, IN. This role oversees the end-to-end restoration process for damaged or at-risk documents, including intake, assessment, cataloging, and tracking throughout restoration. Day-to-day responsibilities include coordinating document handling and storage, supervising restoration techniques such as drying, cleaning, and digitization, and ensuring accurate documentation of all work performed. The individual in this role will collaborate with field teams, clients, and insurance partners to provide updates, manage timelines, and help resolve questions about scope and status. The role also involves monitoring quality standards, enforcing safety and confidentiality protocols, and identifying process improvements to enhance efficiency and client experience.

Document restoration and preservation skills, including handling sensitive records, applying appropriate drying and cleaning techniques, and understanding basic archival or records management principles.
Operational and project coordination skills, such as workflow planning, task prioritization, inventory tracking, and schedule management in a fast-paced restoration environment.
Attention to detail and quality control skills, including accurate data entry, meticulous recordkeeping, and the ability to review work for completeness and compliance with company standards.
Customer service and communication skills, with the ability to provide clear updates to clients and insurance partners, explain processes, and address inquiries in a professional, empathetic manner.
Safety, confidentiality, and compliance awareness, including adherence to company safety protocols, secure handling of confidential or sensitive documents, and respect for regulatory and privacy requirements.
Basic technical skills, such as using office software, scanners, and other equipment related to document restoration and digitization.
Ability to work on-site in a physical environment, including standing, lifting, and moving boxes or equipment as needed, with a focus on safe work practices.
Previous experience in restoration, records management, or a related field is beneficial; a high school diploma or equivalent is required, and further education or certifications in restoration or archival work are an advantage.

jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Central Region Community Outreach and Environmental Education Specialist 3
within the Water Quality Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Assignment Pay

The salary listed includes 5% bilingual assignment pay.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day per week is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by August 25, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

You will be the community’s bridge to water quality awareness and action. As the Community Outreach Environmental Education Specialist, you will lead creative, hands-on learning experiences that inspire residents of all ages to become active stewards of their local environment. Through dynamic public engagement, innovative educational programming, and strong partnerships with schools, community groups, and regional partners, you will transform environmental challenges into opportunities for collective impact.

You will design and deliver outreach initiatives that make complex environmental topics accessible, relatable, and locally relevant—whether through interactive workshops, youth programs, public events, or multilingual communications. You will also help build long-term community relationships that support equitable participation and ensure every voice is heard in environmental decision-making.

What You Will Do

Partner with technical experts to craft community-centered engagement strategies that bring water quality science to life and connect residents directly to the mission of protecting the region’s waters.
Serve as a cultural and linguistic bridge by providing Spanish interpretation during workshops, public meetings, school events, and neighborhood canvassing—ensuring every community member can participate fully and confidently.
Spark public learning through accessible outreach—sharing information via presentations, email, web content, and educational materials that help people understand and act on water quality issues.
Translate key outreach materials into Spanish to support inclusive communication and make environmental information easier for more families to access.
Guide thoughtful, on-the-ground engagement efforts—planning, implementing, and evaluating community outreach while elevating community insights and identifying emerging environmental justice needs in the Lower Yakima Valley.
Remove barriers to participation by identifying gaps in access, developing best practices, and creating tailored outreach tools for underserved communities, local interests, governments, industry, and the general public.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Seven (7) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Communication Skills – Ability to share information clearly with diverse audiences to support understanding and informed participation.
Community Engagement – Ability to plan and carry out engagement activities to involve communities in program decisions and actions.
Cultural Humility and Inclusion – Ability to work respectfully with people from diverse cultures and backgrounds to build trust and improve access to agency services.
Outreach and Education Delivery – Ability to develop and deliver accessible outreach materials and learning opportunities to help the public understand program issues and resources.
Bilingual Communication (English/Spanish) – Ability to translate and interpret information accurately to ensure Spanish-speaking communities can fully participate in outreach and engagement activities. This includes: verbal (speaking/listening) and written (reading/writing).
Program and Environmental Knowledge – Ability to understand environmental issues, program activities, and regulatory requirements to share accurate information and support informed public engagement.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or natural science, education, health sciences, social services, communications or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Examples Of How To Qualify

7 years of experience.
6 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
4 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
3 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
2 years of experience AND a Master’s degree or above.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license or provide alternate reliable transportation for travel within the state of Washington.
Must pass the verbal (speaking/listening) and written (reading/writing) Spanish language proficiency tests.

Desired Qualifications

Lived or professional experience with underrepresented communities.
An understanding of environmental justice research, demographic data, and equity focused assessments.
Knowledge and practice of collaborative problem solving, conflict resolution, and participatory planning.
Experience with website and social media content development.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Duties

As the Industrial Wastewater Permit Manager, you will support Ecology’s mission and represent the Water Quality Program as an Environmental Engineer. Under the supervision of the Industrial Wastewater Permits Unit (IWPU) Supervisor, you will be responsible for developing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits, State Waste Discharge (SWD) permits, and accompanying fact sheets for industrial facilities in the Northwest region of Washington state. This work directly supports clean water protections and helps ensure industrial practices are safe, sustainable, and compliant.

In this role, you will review permit reports, conduct facility inspections, provide technical assistance, investigate complaints, conduct compliance reviews, and provide technical support for enforcement recommendations. Under the guidance of a licensed engineer, you will also review engineering reports submitted by the industrial facilities.

You will frequently collaborate with internal staff to offer technical assistance to industrial facilities and to support the development of compliance or enforcement actions. This position provides opportunities to grow your technical expertise, strengthen your engineering judgment, and contribute meaningfully to environmental outcomes across the state.

What You Will Do

Develop wastewater discharge permits.
Review water quality monitoring data to determine facility compliance.
Conduct facility inspections, provide technical assistance, and write inspection reports.
Conduct water quality sampling and analyze monitoring data to evaluate compliance.
Assist with the development of enforcement actions.
Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, and clearly explain complex technical issues in plain language.
Work with the Ecology Communications team to respond to media inquiries.
Learn to review engineering reports submitted for ISGP and individual NPDES permits.

Technical Collaboration – Ability to work constructively with facilities, Tribal nations, local governments, and colleagues to resolve technical questions, support compliance efforts, and ensure consistent understanding of engineering and environmental requirements.
Communication & Documentation – Ability to communicate technical concepts and prepare clear permits, reports, and correspondence to support regulatory decisions and partner understanding.

The Wildlife Ecology Laboratory ( WEL )
at Tennessee State University ( TSU )
is seeking a post-doctoral research associate to utilize environmental DNA as an early screening tool for aquatic invasive species in National Forests throughout the southeast United States. In addition to refining molecular approaches to screen for aquatic invasive species, the project will aim to compare eDNA screening approaches to traditional aquatic survey methods. The postdoc will work collaboratively with researchers from the USDA Forest Service Southern Research Station and Clemson University and will be expected to lead research efforts related to sample processing and post-processing of genome-scale bioinformatics data. Barr is seeking an environmental scientist to join our Bismarck, North Dakota, team. In this hybrid role, you will support our Water Resources group with challenging and fast-paced work on environmental impact assessment, permitting, and compliance projects.

A successful person in this role will have strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills. They possess exceptional organization skills with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment and have a flexible working style. They are also willing to occasionally modify their schedule to meet deadlines and/or client needs.

Your Impact – Key Responsibilities

Field support: conducting wetland delineations, inventories, functional assessments, protected species assessments, botanical inventories, and other ecological field investigations.
Permitting and regulatory support: conducting and writing environmental impact assessments and related documentation, interpreting regulatory and permitting processes, communicating with regulatory agencies and client contacts, and developing and reviewing environmental permit applications.
Environmental impact and reporting: performing desktop and field-based threatened and endangered species reviews and other biological and/or natural resources inventories (i.e., raptor surveys, migratory bird surveys, noxious weed inventories, etc.).

About The Opportunity

Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position is based out of Barr's Bismarck, North Dakota, office.

Work environment: some fieldwork locations include difficult terrain typical of backcountry (e.g., dense vegetation, fallen timber, poor footing soils, streams), roadway, and construction sites. Professional Wetland Scientist Certification.

jobs.title: Environmental Geoscientist | Energy
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Good environmental and geoscience work starts in the field. The quality of what gets recorded on site, how samples are handled, how monitoring is carried out and how findings are documented lays the foundation for everything that follows. At Stantec, we know that, and we look for people who take that foundation seriously.

We are looking for an Environmental Geoscientist to join our Energy and Resources Group, working across contaminated land, hydrogeology and ground investigation projects from our Warrington, Manchester or Shrewsbury offices. If you are practical, organised and ready to build your career in environmental geoscience within a strong, supportive team, we would love to hear from you.

About The Role

You will play a hands-on role in planning, coordinating and delivering environmental and geoscience siteworks across a varied portfolio of projects. Day to day, this will include supporting ground investigation supervision, undertaking groundwater, surface water and gas monitoring, coordinating samples, maintaining field records and upholding health, safety, security and environmental requirements on site.

Away from the field, you will contribute to the preparation of work plans, fieldwork specifications, HSSE documentation, desk studies and investigation reports. You will work closely with project managers, technical specialists, field teams, laboratories, subcontractors and wider multidisciplinary project teams, developing a broad understanding of how complex environmental projects come together from the ground up. A full clean UK driving licence and willingness to travel to project sites, including extended periods on site where required, are essential for this role.

Your Impact

The data you collect, the samples you coordinate and the records you maintain will feed directly into technical assessments and reports that shape how contaminated and complex sites are understood and managed. That is work with real consequences for the environments and communities around those sites, and your contribution at the field stage makes all the difference to the quality of what follows.

This is also a role with strong career growth potential. The breadth of project experience you will gain across contaminated land, hydrogeology and ground investigation will give you a platform to develop in whichever technical direction suits you best.

About You

You hold a BSc Hons or equivalent in Geoscience, Geology, Environmental Science, Environmental Geoscience, Earth Sciences or a related discipline. You bring a practical understanding of ground investigation, environmental monitoring and site-based data collection, and you are comfortable supporting the supervision of ground investigation works and coordinating site activities safely and efficiently.

You have experience in or a strong interest in groundwater, surface water and ground gas monitoring. You are thorough in managing sample handling, labelling, chain of custody documentation and laboratory coordination, and you prepare clear, accurate field records and factual reporting inputs as a matter of course.

You are well-organised, collaborative and HSSE-aware, with the kind of practical, grounded approach that makes fieldwork run smoothly and projects stay on track.

Why Join Us

We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies in 2025. Named 'Best Place to Work' and 'International Consulting Firm of the Year' at the NCE Awards 2024.
We do what is right: Industry-leading training and development, as well as paid professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan to support you in becoming chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment and Early Careers peer group, and a wider ERG network (see more on our ERGs here: Stantec Employee Resource Groups)
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the UK - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, bonus schemes, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard, as well as discounted gym membership and lots more.
Hybrid/Flexible working: Enjoy a healthy work-life balance with our hybrid approach to flexible work.

#UKEnergy

About Stantec

The Stantec community unites more than 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across 6 continents. We have been working with our clients and communities in the UK for over 150 years. We plan, design, deliver and manage the development and infrastructure needed to support the creation of sustainable, healthy and prosperous communities.

Our teams provide effective and relevant solutions, translating our clients’ vision into valued consents, deliverable plans for projects and programmes, and efficient designs for delivery, based on technical excellence and deep market insights. Job Title
Assistant/Associate Professor for Environmental Health and Safety

Department

Job Description Summary

The Department of Public and Environmental Wellness in the School of Health Sciences at Oakland University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor in Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ). The successful candidate will join a dynamic and multidisciplinary department committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement.

We seek a candidate who will initiate and maintain a successful program of research, scholarship, and service. The ideal candidate will contribute to both undergraduate and graduate instruction in Environmental Health and Safety, support the department’s mission, and actively engage in curriculum development and program growth.

Responsibilities Include

Developing and sustaining an active scholarship agenda in Environmental Health and Safety or a related field
Teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses in EHS and related topics
Engaging in service to the department, college, university, and professional communities
Advising and mentoring students
Contributing to program development, improvement, and accreditation activities
Participating in community engagement initiatives and, where appropriate, program leadership

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

A doctoral degree (PhD, DrPH, or equivalent) in Environmental Health, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Public Health, or a closely related field by the time of appointment
Evidence of teaching effectiveness and scholarly activity appropriate to rank

Preferred Qualifications

Attainment of the Certified Safety Professional ( CSP ) credential or other relevant professional designations (e.g., Certified Industrial Hygienist [ CIH ], Certified Hazardous Materials Manager [ CHMM ])
Experience with ABET accreditation processes and standards
Interest and experience in continuous program improvement, curriculum innovation, and academic leadership
Evidence of successful community engagement or interdisciplinary academic collaboration
Leadership roles or active participation in professional organizations related to Environmental Health and Safety (e.g., American Society of Safety Professionals [ ASSP ], National Safety Council [ NSC ], etc.), with a demonstrated commitment to advancing the field through these organizations

Special Instructions to Applicants

Applications must include a CV, cover letter, unofficial transcripts, names and contact information of 3 professional references, a teaching statement, and a research statement.

Contact information for references will be requested in the Professional References section of the application and a link provided through which references can submit letters.

School/College & Department/Program Summary

The Environmental Health and Safety faculty offer: a Bachelor of Science (BS), Master of Science (MS), a dual BS/MS program, and four graduate certificate programs within the Department of Public and Environmental Wellness ( PEW ). Guided by the mission of “Pursuing society’s big health challenges,” the department is dedicated to transforming students into leaders, connecting theory to best practices, and addressing the health needs of diverse communities.

Our EHS program focuses on translating knowledge and theory into best practices for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating hazards that pose risks to people, property, and the environment. While our degree and certificate programs are fully available online, we also provide access to well-equipped physical laboratories that enhance hands-on learning and research.

Faculty in the EHS program bring expertise in areas including:

Environmental standards and controls
Industrial hygiene
Industrial and robotics safety
Electrical systems safety
Construction safety
Safety systems management
Fire safety
Biomechanics and ergonomics
EHS program leadership and development

All within the broader context of public health and wellness.

More About Oakland University

The University is located on 1,443 acres of scenic land in the cities of Rochester Hills and Auburn Hills in Oakland County, Michigan. The University offers 142 bachelor’s degree programs and 138 graduate degree and certificate programs. Academics include programs in the College of Arts and Sciences, School of Business Administration, School of Education and Human Services, School of Engineering and Computer Science, School of Health Sciences, School of Medicine and School of Nursing. As an anchor institution in southeastern Michigan that is dedicated to building ongoing, collaborative relationships, Oakland University embraces community and civic engagement to enhance the lives of its students and positively impact the broader community. Learn more about Oakland University’s Mission & Vision
and Strategic Plan

jobs.title: Environmental Services Market Sector Leader
jobs.description:
Department:
Community Infrastructure
Location:
Remote- USA

Description

Waggoner Engineering, Inc. is seeking an Environmental Services Market Sector Leader
to join our team. The Environmental Services Market Sector Leader is a senior strategic-operations leader responsible for growing the firm in the environmental services market sector across all business units - growing talent, building high-performing teams, expanding the client base, and increasing profitable revenue and backlog in the water market. The role will elevate Waggoner’s brand and thought leadership, lead major client pursuits, and ensure excellent, consistent project delivery. Because the role has limited to no direct reports, success depends on leading through leadership influence - aligning Business Unit Leaders, Area Managers, Discipline Leaders, and Client/Project Teams around clear market priorities, development pathways, and quality outcomes for clients.

Sector Summary

Responsible for the strategy, growth, and delivery excellence of Waggoner’s Environmental Services Market across all Business Units, serving public- and private-sector clients with environmental planning, permitting, compliance, site investigation, remediation, natural resource services, and related sustainability/resilience needs. The leader serves as the primary market-facing champion for environmental services, helping clients navigate regulatory complexity, reduce risk, advance development and infrastructure programs, restore or redevelop impacted sites, and strengthen environmental stewardship and community outcomes. This framing aligns with how major engineering and environmental consultancies currently position environmental services: a multidisciplinary platform spanning permitting, remediation, compliance, natural resources, and climate/sustainability solutions.

Market Sector Scope
Primary clients: Federal, state, and local government agencies; transportation and utility agencies; port, aviation, and energy entities; industrial and commercial owners/operators; developers; and institutional clients with environmental permitting, compliance, remediation, restoration, or redevelopment needs.
Primary services: Environmental planning and permitting; NEPA/environmental documentation and agency coordination; environmental compliance and EHS support; site assessment and due diligence; contaminated site investigation and remediation; brownfields/restoration/redevelopment support; PFAS and other emerging-contaminant services; air quality and waste/resource management; natural and cultural resources support; sustainability, resilience, and climate-related environmental advisory services. These service areas closely reflect current market positioning across leading firms in the sector.
Boundary (clarity of leadership): The Environmental Services Market Sector Leader leads environmental work where environmental risk management, permitting, compliance, remediation, restoration, or environmental approvals are the primary driver of the client need or project scope. Environmental work that is integral to industrial facilities and operations - including plant-specific permitting/compliance or environmental services embedded within industrial capital programs - is led in coordination with the Industrial Market Sector Leader.
Environmental work embedded within public water, wastewater, stormwater, or watershed utility programs is coordinated with the Water Market Sector Leader.
Environmental services supporting transportation approvals, corridor studies, or transportation program delivery are coordinated with the Transportation Market Sector Leader.
In all overlap situations, the Environmental Services Market Sector Leader works with the applicable Market Sector Leader and Business Unit leadership to define clear lead/support roles for client management, pursuit leadership, and delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Market Strategy, Growth, and Thought Leadership
Develop and execute a multi-year market strategy and annual plan (targets, priority clients, services, staffing, investments).
Serve as a visible thought leader: publish, present, and represent Waggoner in industry forums to increase sector brand and market credibility.
Lead or oversee major pursuits, capture plans, teaming strategies, and client messaging; partner with marketing and business development on campaigns and collateral.

Client Development and Winning Work
Develop and maintain trusted advisor relationships with priority clients; lead account planning in coordination with Business Unit Leaders and Area Managers.
Lead capture planning and pursuit strategy for major programs, including go/no-go, teaming, pricing strategy inputs, and interview preparation.
Identify emerging client needs, regulatory/funding drivers, and competitive positioning; evolve service offerings accordingly.
Expand Waggoner's role with clients by connecting environmental services to broader infrastructure, industrial, redevelopment, resilience, and community objectives.

Delivery Excellence, Standards, Quality, and Risk
Ensure project delivery aligns with market strategy, client expectations, technical standards, and risk posture.
Partner with Business Unit Leaders and Area Managers to forecast workload and coordinate resources to meet commitments.
Promote consistent delivery methodologies, lessons learned, and knowledge-sharing across offices and disciplines.
Champion consistent project delivery standards and quality systems across the sector, including use of standard agreements and templates where client requirements allow (e.g., EJCDC-based agreements and front-end documents).
Support the development and use of firmwide templates and standards (e.g., supplemental conditions, spec/plan covers, standard details, report templates).
Lead or participate in QA/QC and risk reviews on key pursuits and high-risk projects; promote ‘do it right the first time’ delivery.
Advance safety in design practices, risk management, and a consistent project closeout process.
Contribute to proposal reviews and continuous improvement of win themes, deliverables, and client communications (including letter proposals where appropriate).

People Leadership and Talent Development (Matrix Organization)
Lead through influence in a matrix environment; align Business Unit Leaders, Area Managers, Discipline Leaders, and project teams to sector priorities.
Establish clear target markets, clients, and services; translate strategy into actionable plans, account plans, and pursuit roadmaps.
Coach, mentor, and develop staff across business units through project engagement, QA/QC reviews, and pursuit leadership—regardless of reporting lines.
Build and sustain high-performing teams by mentoring, recruiting, and aligning talent to the best and highest use in service of clients.
Develop communities of practice and technical development opportunities; encourage cross-office collaboration and staff visibility to sector work.
Support succession planning and development of future leaders.

Financial and Performance Management
Own sector performance and accountability (revenue, backlog, win rate, profitability, utilization, client satisfaction) in partnership with Business Unit Leaders and finance/operations.
Maintain a pipeline and forecast; communicate risks and opportunities to Strategic Operations leadership.
Help prioritize investment in capabilities, hires, teaming relationships, and target clients that strengthen long-term market position.

Cross-Sector Collaboration
Coordinate with other Market Sector Leaders when markets, clients, or services overlap; define clear lead/support roles for pursuits and client management.
Develop integrated solutions and cross-sector teams to deliver greater client value and expand relationships.
Use regular cross-sector planning, shared CRM/account plans, and joint pursuit reviews to prevent duplication and ensure a One Firm client experience.
Escalate and resolve priority or resourcing conflicts through the EVP of Strategic Operations as needed.

Measures of Success
Growth: achievement of annual net service revenue targets, healthy pipeline, improved win rate, and diversified client portfolio.
Brand: increased visibility through speaking, publishing, associations, and client references aligned to the sector strategy.
Delivery: strong client satisfaction, consistent QA/QC outcomes, reduced rework/risk events, and successful closeout on key projects.
People: improved engagement and retention, effective mentoring, and a developing bench of sector leaders and technical experts.
One Firm: effective collaboration across market sectors and business units with clear lead/support roles and integrated wins.

What you'll need

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Environmental, or Chemical Engineering. Geology, Environmental Science or related field (Master’s preferred).
Registered Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), or other relevant environmental professional credential preferred; equivalent environmental consulting leadership experience required.
Typically, 15+ years of progressive water experience, including 7+ years of client leadership and demonstrated pursuit leadership.

Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated success growing environmental client portfolios and leading multidisciplinary delivery teams across multiple service lines.
Experience leading complex environmental programs involving site investigation/remediation, permitting, due diligence, natural resources, PFAS/emerging contaminants, restoration, or redevelopment.
Experience integrating environmental services with water, transportation, industrial, energy, or community development programs. These are all service intersections commonly emphasized by major firms in the sector.

Core Competencies
Strategic thinking and market insight
Client relationship leadership and executive presence
Pursuit leadership and persuasive communication
Technical leadership and commitment to quality
Ability to influence without direct authority; collaborative leadership
Financial acumen and performance accountability
People development, mentoring, and team building
Risk management and regulatory awareness

Travel and Work Environment
Primarily office-based in any WEI location with flexibility; travel to client sites, Waggoner offices, and industry events as required.
Occasional evening and weekend work may be needed during pursuits or critical project milestones.

Why Join Our Team

About Waggoner

Waggoner is a multidisciplinary infrastructure and advisory firm focused on transforming communities and advancing the systems that support them. Our team brings together engineering, science, business, environmental expertise, digital innovation, program delivery, and strategic insight to solve complex challenges facing communities, industries, and governments.

We believe infrastructure is more than projects - it is the foundation of resilient communities, economic opportunity, and a stronger future. By integrating technical excellence with environmental stewardship, data-driven insights, and collaboration problem solving, Waggoner helps our clients realize what's possible and delivers solutions that create lasting impact for the people and places we serve.

Our culture is built on integrity, accountability, collaboration, and excellence. We empower talented professionals to lead, innovate, and work across disciplines to deliver meaningful outcomes for our clients and communities.

Our Vision

To be the trusted partner organizations turn to for integrated solutions that strengthen communities, advance infrastructure, and solve complex challenges.

Our Mission

Transforming communities. To improve the quality of life for our clients, communities, and employees by delivering innovative, resilient, and sustainable solutions that make a lasting difference.

We know work isn't only about what you do, it's also about who you work for and with! Waggo

jobs.title: Associate Director - Environmental Planning
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

We are looking for an experienced Associate Director - Environmental Planning
to join our growing team in London or Reading.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering environmental planning and assessment services across a diverse portfolio of energy transition, water resilience, development and critical infrastructure projects. You’ll work at the intersection of planning, environmental assessment and sustainable development, helping clients understand and navigate environmental considerations throughout the project lifecycle.

You’ll work alongside planners, environmental specialists, engineers and other technical experts, contributing to multidisciplinary projects and developing practical, sustainable solutions for our clients.

As an Associate Director
, you’ll have the opportunity to take ownership of project workstreams, build strong client relationships, contribute to business development and support the development of colleagues within the team.

About The Role

As an Associate Director, you will:

Lead and contribute to environmental planning and assessment projects across a range of development and infrastructure sectors.
Provide environmental planning and consenting advice to clients and multidisciplinary project teams.
Support and coordinate the preparation of Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA), Environmental Statements and associated environmental planning documentation.
Manage individual project workstreams, coordinating inputs from technical specialists and ensuring deliverables are completed to a high standard.
Provide advice on environmental constraints, opportunities and consenting requirements from project inception through to delivery.
Coordinate and contribute to stakeholder engagement, consultation exercises, workshops and project meetings.
Liaise with clients, local authorities, statutory consultees, regulators and other stakeholders.
Undertake environmental and planning research, including reviewing relevant legislation, policy and guidance.
Review technical information and reports, ensuring environmental considerations are appropriately reflected in project outputs.
Support project management, including programmes, budgets, resources and delivery against agreed timescales.
Build and maintain effective relationships with clients and contribute to the development of new opportunities.
Contribute to bids, tenders, proposals and business development activities.
Support and mentor junior colleagues, sharing technical knowledge and helping to develop the wider team.
Work collaboratively with colleagues across our wider planning, environmental and engineering teams to deliver integrated solutions.

Your Impact

You’ll play an important role in helping our clients deliver projects that are environmentally responsible, technically robust and capable of securing the necessary consents.

You’ll have the opportunity to work on a variety of complex projects across sectors including infrastructure, energy, development, transport and the built environment.

As an Associate Director, you’ll take increasing responsibility for project delivery and client relationships while developing your technical and commercial expertise. You’ll also have the opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of our environmental planning capability across the UK.

Working within a multidisciplinary organisation, you’ll have access to specialists across a wide range of environmental and engineering disciplines, enabling you to develop solutions that consider the wider environmental, social and technical context of each project.

About You

We’re looking for an experienced environmental planning professional who is confident working within a consultancy environment and is ready to take the next step in their career.

You Have

Experience in environmental planning, environmental consultancy, planning or a closely related discipline.
Good knowledge of the UK planning and environmental assessment framework.
Experience delivering or coordinating EIA and environmental consenting projects.
Experience managing project workstreams and coordinating multidisciplinary technical inputs.
A good understanding of environmental legislation, planning policy and relevant guidance.
Experience engaging with clients, stakeholders, local authorities, statutory consultees or regulators.
Good project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex environmental matters clearly and effectively.
An interest in developing client relationships and contributing to business development.
A collaborative approach and an enthusiasm for supporting and developing less experienced colleagues.

Qualifications

A relevant degree in environmental planning, environmental science, geography, planning or a related discipline is desirable.
Membership of a relevant professional body, such as the Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI), or another relevant professional accreditation, would be advantageous.
Most importantly, we’re looking for someone who is collaborative, motivated and passionate about delivering high-quality environmental solutions that make a positive difference.

Why Join Us

We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. Named ‘Best Place to Work’ and ‘International Consulting Firm of the Year’ at the NCE Awards 2024.
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A p rofessional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered with ICE.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment and Early Careers peer group and wider ERG network (see more on our ERGs here: Stantec Employee Resource Groups )
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the UK & Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, bonus schemes, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard as well as discounted gym membership and lots more.
Flexible working: Enjoy a healthy work-life balance with our hybrid approach to flexible working.

#EnvironmentalPlanning

About Stantec

The Stantec community unites more than 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across 6 continents. We have been working with our clients and communities in the UK for over 150 years. We plan, design, deliver and manage the development and infrastructure needed to support the creation of sustainable, healthy and prosperous communities.

Our teams provide effective and relevant solutions, translating our clients’ vision into valued consents, deliverable plans for projects and programmes, and efficient designs for delivery, based on technical excellence and deep market insights. We deal with today’s challenges, but also keep a fairer, better tomorrow in sight, looking at how we deliver clean growth, support radical changes in our economy and meet the needs of future communities.

We prohibit discrimination in decisions concerning recruitment, hiring, referral, promotion, compensation, fringe benefits, job training, terminations or any other condition of employment. Stantec is in compliance with laws and regulations and ensures equitable opportunities in all aspects of employment.

Building an inspired, inclusive work environment that attracts, supports, and develops world-class talent is a crucial key to our success. If you are excited by this role but worry that your experience doesn’t exactly align, we encourage you to apply.

Company Overview

SiteOne Landscape Supply is the largest national distributor of landscaping products across the United States and Canada. As a leading supplier of wholesale goods for green industry professionals, we have a long history of serving those who design, build, and maintain outdoor spaces – from lawns and gardens to golf courses, sport fields and more. At SiteOne, we are passionate about delivering an outstanding customer experience and will stop at nothing to help our customers win. We know that our associates are the key to this success, and our commitment to the SiteOne DNA and support for our associates through development programs, benefits, and perks align with our vision to "Be a Great Place to Work for Our Associates". We foster a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement. With over 700 locations and exciting expansion ahead, now is the perfect time to join SiteOne and grow Stronger Together™!

Position Overview

EHS Manager - Remote - East

Position Overview:

Reporting to the Sr. Director, Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS), the Manager, Environmental, Health and Safety, is responsible for assisting operations with implementing SiteOne Landscape Supply EH&S Management system, developing, and implementing effective injury prevention programs, driver safety and compliance initiatives, and ensuring compliance with company standards and regulatory requirements.

The Manager, Environmental, Health and Safety will have designated division responsibilities along with corporate program responsibilities while partnering closely with all levels of the SiteOne field leadership team and functional support teams to strengthen the EH&S culture and improve organizational performance. The successful candidate must have demonstrated skills in implementing processes that lead to sustained EH&S performance improvements.

Assist with the development and implementation of SiteOne’s EHS policies, standards and injury prevention programs
Lead regional level incident investigation reviews, including near misses, workplace injuries, and commercial vehicle accidents, while overseeing the root cause and corrective actions process to successful completion

Act as the primary subject matter expert on DOT/FMCSA requirements including roadside inspection performance, vehicle accident investigations, and FMCSA drug and alcohol clearinghouse.

Collaborate closely with field and functional teams, insurance adjusters to effectively manage OSHA investigations and insurance claims; serve as a company safety representative during litigation and settlement negotiations.

Review and analyze with large date sets and be able to identify risk and trends to support continuous improvement decision making and initiatives
Routinely visit company-wide locations to provide support to field associates

Bachelor’s Degree in Safety, Environmental, Risk Management or Engineering field
Minimum of 5+ years of experience in an EHS role required
Practical hands-on working knowledge of OSHA, DOT/FMCSA, and EPA regulations required
Experience developing and leading commercial driver safety and DOT/FMCSA compliance programs for a large commercial fleet required
Strong interpersonal skills to establish credibility and trust with colleagues, branch associates and field leaders
Strong organizational, project management, data analytics, and problem-solving skills to assist with developing trend analysis and performance indicators that support the development and execution of continuous improvement strategies
Proven ability to successfully manage multiple projects to completion
Relevant technical certifications such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), DOT, Smith Systems, environmental (CHMM) certifications preferred
Experience working in warehousing, wholesale, or distribution industry a plus

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Check out this video and find out why our team loves to work here!

Join Us! CDM Smith – where amazing career journeys unfold.

Imagine a place committed to offering an unmatched employee experience. Where you work on projects that are meaningful to you. Where you play an active part in shaping your career journey. Where your co-workers are invested in you and your success. Where you are encouraged and supported to do your very best and given the tools and resources to do so. Where it’s a priority that the company takes good care of you and your family.

Our employees are the heart of our company. As an employer of choice, our goal is to provide a challenging, progressive and inclusive work environment which fosters personal leadership, career growth and development for every employee. We value passionate individuals who challenge the norm, deliver world-class solutions and bring diverse perspectives. Join our team, and together we will make a difference and change the world.

Job Description

CDM Smith is looking for an entry-level Environmental, Water Resources, or Civil Engineer to join our Water Services Group
. This position offers early-career candidates the opportunity to apply their engineering skills to innovative and sustainable water projects while building technical expertise and growing within a dynamic team.

In this role, you will support the planning, design, and implementation of water and wastewater treatment facilities, sewer systems, pipelines, and associated infrastructure.

Responsibilities

Support site assessments, field investigations, and project studies.
Assist with design development and adjust design parameters based on project requirements and field findings.
Perform water quality analyses, hydraulic and hydrologic modeling, and other engineering analyses.
Prepare technical reports, project documentation, presentations, and other deliverables for client meetings and industry conferences.
Use tools such as ArcGIS, HEC-RAS, SWMM, CADD, Excel, and other engineering software to support project design and analysis.
Office and in-field coordination to support regional lead service line rehabilitation projects.
Participate in fieldwork and construction management activities, providing exposure to projects throughout the full project lifecycle.

This role offers the opportunity to work on challenging and sustainable water infrastructure projects while developing technical skills, gaining real-world project experience, and learning from experienced professionals across the Water Services Group.

Skills & Abilities

Basic Knowledge of computer assisted design and drafting (CADD) 3D and 4D software and practices. Basic Knowledge of engineer principles of design. Knowledge of Microsoft business software (excel, word, etc.). Good verbal and written communication ability.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Civil, Environmental or Chemical Engineering or related discipline. 0 years. Domestic and/or international travel may be required. The frequency of travel is contingent on specific duties, responsibilities, and the essential functions of the position, which may vary depending on workload and project demands. Equivalent additional directly related experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Amount Of Travel Required

10% or less

EEO Statement

We attract the best people in the industry, supporting their efforts to learn and grow. We strive to create a challenging and progressive work environment. We provide career opportunities that span a variety of disciplines and geographic locations, with projects that our employees plan, design, build and operate as diverse as the needs of our clients. CDM Smith Inc. and its divisions and subsidiaries are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, pregnancy related conditions, childbirth and related medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression), national origin, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Regional Environmental Manager (REM), Environmental Assurance and Protection (EAP)
jobs.description:
Description

This Regional Environmental Manager (REM) is responsible for owning the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across Southern California Amazon Last Mile Delivery Stations.

The REM shapes and evolves the regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and designing programmatic solutions that close compliance gaps at scale. The REM translates senior leadership vision into executable program frameworks, defines success criteria, and owns the roadmap for implementation across the region.

The REM works with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, designers, construction, operations, and other key stakeholders. This REM will own environmental compliance across up to 15+ Amazon Delivery Stations in the region, with oversight of Multi-Site Environmental Managers (MSEMs) and Environmental Specialists.

This is a hands-on leadership position that includes time in the yard and on the floor of busy delivery stations conducting inspections and audits, mentoring MSEMs, ensuring program quality, leading regulatory interactions, and driving accountability across multiple departments and all levels of employees throughout the operation.

Key job responsibilities

Own the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across the region — from strategy through execution and continuous improvement.
Shape regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and proposing scalable programmatic solutions before they require escalation.
Design and sustain program controllership mechanisms (business reviews, metric dashboards, escalation triggers) that operate independently without requiring manager intervention.
Independently proxy for the Sr Mgr in weekly and monthly forums (WBRs, MBRs) with full ownership of environmental sections — able to answer, defend, and commit.
Force multiply by designing scalable systems, processes, and training that enable MSEMs and operational stakeholders to execute at higher quality with less intervention over time.
Mentor MSEMs and Environmental Specialists; set the quality bar for root cause analysis and corrective action.
Lead COE/A3 investigations independently to closure with leadership, ensuring root causes explain systemic "why" rather than describing "what."
Own procedures and change management for the region, driving adoption end-to-end.
Lead regulatory agency interactions — including inspections, enforcement responses, and agency negotiations — and drive follow-up requirements to closure.
Manage and oversee local, state, and federal environmental regulations and Amazon policy.
Develop strategic programs by integrating with engineering, construction, and operations. Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization.
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards. Provide comprehensive oversight to 3P environmental vendors and consultants.
Drive environmental metrics — build tools and dashboards that give stakeholders the information they need to make good decisions at scale.
Assess emerging regulations and proactively design mitigation plans before regulatory deadlines create urgency.
Own or coordinate construction and launch activities for new sites within the region to ensure environmental compliance at or before operational readiness.
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company.
Navigate ambiguity effectively — find paths forward where solutions are not pre-defined and coordinate cross-functionally without deferring decisions upward.
Manage resource trade-offs and competing priorities across the region, escalating only when decisions genuinely exceed authority.
Submit time-critical reports to various governmental agencies.
Up to 50% travel.

A day in the life

Own regional execution of environmental procedures and ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, regional, and local regulations.
Design and implement scalable compliance mechanisms across the region — covering air emissions, surface water, wastewater, waste, and other environmental media.
Manage and prepare site-specific and regional environmental reporting to regulators and within Amazon.
Analyze systemic defect patterns and environmental metrics; review weekly and monthly trends to determine where programmatic improvements are needed.
Drive corrective action where targets are not met — negotiate resources and priorities across organizations to ensure programs are delivered on time and at the required quality standard.
Lead root cause analyses for environmental incidents; ensure corrective actions prevent recurrence at a systemic level, not just site-level fixes.
Conduct and oversee environmental audits and inspections for continuous improvement; set the quality bar for inspection rigor.
Monitor and provide strategic guidance on multi-site performance against applicable environmental regulations, programs, and Amazon global standards.
Design and sustain business review cadences and escalation triggers that surface risk in real time.

About The Team

The mission of the Environmental Assurance and Protection organization (EAP) is to transform environmental regulatory compliance into a zero-defect process through simple, scalable, and sustainable solutions.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project Management experience
8+ years of compliance, audit or risk management experience
Knowledge of Microsoft Office products and applications at an advanced level
- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, or related field of study
- Experience working with and managing third party consultants and vendors

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
Experience leveraging technology and implementing lean principles / Six Sigma methodologies to drive process improvements or equivalent
Master's degree or equivalent
Experience communicating across technical and non-technical audiences, including executive level stakeholders or clients
Experience in project management, delivery and/or program management

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

El Paso County will be a trusted regional leader known for excellence in county service delivery.

Job Summary

Associate Geospatial Analyst / Geospatial Analyst / Senior Geospatial Analyst

Map Data. Drive Decisions. Shape the Future.

Are you someone who sees the world in layers—of data, design, and discovery? Do you enjoy transforming information into robust planning, infrastructure, and public service tools? El Paso County is seeking a talented Geospatial Professional to join our Department of Public Works team and help build smarter, more connected communities through innovative GIS and asset management.

This is a career progression opportunity, with openings at the Associate, Analyst, and Senior Analyst levels.
Whether you're just starting your geospatial journey or are a seasoned GIS pro, there’s a place for you here to grow and make an impact.

What You’ll Do

As part of the Geospatial Analyst team, you’ll be key in maintaining and analyzing asset data for transportation systems, public infrastructure, and County resources. You’ll support everything from road maintenance planning and crash data analysis to field data collection and custom map development.
Your work will support day-to-day operations, long-term infrastructure planning, and innovative solutions that make our county run more efficiently. From scripting and database development to GIS app creation and stakeholder collaboration, your expertise will help power decisions that matter.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You have strong technical skills in GIS, asset management systems, and data analysis.
You’re fluent in tools like ArcGIS, SQL, Python, ModelBuilder, and GIS dashboards.
You can turn raw spatial data into actionable insights, maps, and visuals.
You’re a collaborative problem-solver who enjoys working with cross-functional teams.
You have a passion for public service and building tools that improve communities.
You're adaptable, self-motivated, and thrive in a fast-paced, detail-driven environment.

Why Join El Paso County?

Your Work Has Meaning – Help plan and maintain the infrastructure that residents rely on every day.
Room to Grow – Our career progression path means your role grows as your skills do.
Use the Latest Tools – Get hands-on experience with cutting-edge GIS, programming, and asset management systems.
Collaborate Across Departments – Work closely with engineers, planners, field staff, and local agencies.
Be Part of a Mission-Driven Team – We’re passionate about service, innovation, and supporting each other.

jobs.description:
Initial Posting Date

09/04/2026

Agency

Salary Range

$5,712 - $8,757

Position Type
