Position Title

Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)

Job Description

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality strives to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable environment that embraces and values diversity. Employees at all levels of the agency work together to foster fairness, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We strive to be a workplace where we share our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals, and while collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations. We celebrate and appreciate diversity, champion equity, and treat each other with respect and dignity.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status , gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, age, or physical or mental disability in the administration of our programs and activities. Visit DEQ’s Civil Rights and Environmental Justice page .

Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?
If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full-time opportunity available for an Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)
in Medford, Oregon.

Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

About DEQ!

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.

The Water Quality Division’s mission is to protect and improve Oregon's water quality. Protecting Oregon's rivers, lakes, streams, and groundwater quality keeps these waters safe for a multitude of beneficial uses such as drinking water, fish habitat, recreation, and irrigation. This is accomplished by developing and implementing water quality standards and clean water plans; regulating sewage treatment systems, industrial dischargers, and individual onsite septic systems; collecting and evaluating water quality data; providing grants and technical assistance to reduce non-point pollution sources; and providing loans to communities to build treatment facilities.

Over 30% of Oregonians dispose of wastewater from their homes and businesses through the use of septic systems. The siting, design, installation, and ongoing operation and maintenance of septic systems, as well as sewage disposal service licensing, are regulated through the Onsite Wastewater Management Program. Without this oversight, septic systems can fail or malfunction and sewage may be disposed of improperly, thus polluting Oregon’s land and waterways with raw sewage and creating public health hazards.

The Onsite Wastewater Management Program (septic systems) is administered through intergovernmental agreements for 33 counties and is directly administered by DEQ in 3 counties. This position will support Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties.

For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

What you will do!

You will serve as an Onsite Wastewater Management Program technical expert in the evaluation, inspection, and permitting of onsite septic systems in Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties. Hundreds of onsite applications are submitted to the Medford office each year from individual homeowners, small businesses, and licensed installers. In addition to these applications, the Medford office receives technical questions from the public regarding the program’s requirements and the care and maintenance of septic systems. The office also receives complaints regarding potential septic system violations, some of which can lead to enforcement actions. In addition, local interested parties occasionally request the assistance of the local onsite technical expert to attend meetings and present information.

What’s in it for you!

The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

This is a full-time, AFSCME represented position.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

What are we looking for?

Minimum Qualifications for Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist:

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration).
10 hours of soil science courses in Introductory Soil Science, Soil Morphology, Physical Geology, and Geomorphology.

Minimum Qualifications For Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist Trainee or Waste Water Specialist Trainee. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Applicants do not need to have current registration at the time of hire, but must demonstrate that they meet the requirements to obtain a trainee registration within 30 days of employment.)

Substitutions

Bachelor’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 3 of the required years of experience.
Master’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 4 of the required years of experience.
Doctorate degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 5 of the required years of experience.

The underfill option is available to you if you do not meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist upon hire. In order to retain this appointment, you must be able to meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist by obtaining your Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Office and by completing 10 hours of soil science courses within 3 years of employment. Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration. If hired as an underfill, you will be brought in at the Natural Resource Specialist 3 salary scale instead of the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist salary scale.

Candidates who are most competitive will also reflect the following desired attributes:

Demonstrated understanding of environmental justice and the historical impacts for marginalized and underrepresented communities; ability to take personal responsibility for increasing their knowledge of environmental justice and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Knowledge and skill in the classification, characteristics, and behavior of soils and the transport of water and wastewater through soils is required.
Knowledge of onsite wastewater treatment system technology and requirements for permitting; experience inspecting and evaluating onsite septic systems.
Experience investigating environmental complaints.
Experience reviewing design plans for new construction, alterations, and repairs of wastewater treatment systems.
Experience regulating sewage treatment systems including issuing permits and authorizations for new construction, alterations, or repairs of onsite septic systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to provide clear, concise, and compelling communication of policy and technical information tailored to the needs of diverse audiences; skill in writing and presenting clear and concise reports that include qualitative and quantitative analyses, recommendations, and conclusions to diverse audiences.
Demonstrated experience building and fostering relationships with a diverse group of partners including colleagues, interested parties, communities, organizations, and businesses.

Working Conditions

DEQ believes in a diverse and inclusive work environment. All employees are expected to contribute to a work environment that collectively values and benefits from respecting its diversity and promotes a culture of inclusiveness.

This position will be based out of DEQ’s Medford office; however, the successful candidate may be eligible for hybrid work. The logistics of hybrid work will need to be worked out with the Hiring Manager prior to your hire and may be changed at any time given specific job duties and business needs. jobs.description:
United Infrastructure is a dynamic and rapidly expanding business, focused on delivering critical infrastructure projects, across the utility and social infrastructure sectors.

Our team of highly skilled and hardworking specialists deliver innovative solutions to the complex challenges our clients face.

Our company is split into two business areas:

Utility Infrastructure
–

-

Equal Opportunities Statement - At United Infrastructure, we are committed to making every interaction a positive and inclusive experience. If there is anything we can do to support you, remove barriers, or make the process more accessible, please let us know — we want this to be the best possible experience for you.

Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) – Scotland

Reporting To:
SHEQ Manager

Location:
Scotland – project based with regular travel to live construction sites

Function:
SHEQ / Environment

Role Purpose

The Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) will provide specialist ecological advice, assurance and site-based support across major infrastructure and construction projects throughout Scotland.

Reporting to the SHEQ Manager, the role will ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with Scottish environmental legislation, planning requirements, protected species licences, client requirements and project environmental commitments.

The role will have a strong field-based component, working alongside project management, construction and environmental teams to identify ecological constraints, develop practical mitigation and provide ECoW supervision of activities in environmentally sensitive locations.

The position will be particularly important on linear power infrastructure projects where construction activities may interact with protected species, designated sites, peatland, watercourses, forestry and sensitive habitats.

Key Responsibilities

Ecological Clerk of Works

Act as ECoW for construction activities requiring ecological supervision.
Undertake pre-construction ecological checks and surveys.
Provide watching briefs during sensitive construction activities.
Monitor compliance with ecological mitigation requirements.
Identify emerging ecological risks and advise project teams on appropriate controls.
Establish and monitor ecological exclusion zones and buffers.
Stop, pause or escalate activities where there is an immediate risk of ecological harm or legal non-compliance.
Maintain accurate records of ecological inspections, observations and interventions.

Protected Species

Provide specialist advice and support relating to protected and notable species including, where relevant:

Otters.
Badgers.
Bats.
Red squirrels.
Pine martens.
Water voles.
Great crested newts.
Reptiles and amphibians.
Breeding birds.
Schedule 1 birds.
Raptors.
Freshwater pearl mussels.
Fish and aquatic ecology.
Invasive non-native species.
Other protected or priority species relevant to project locations.

Ensure works are undertaken in accordance with relevant licences and Species Protection Plans.

Surveys & Assessments

Undertake or coordinate Preliminary Ecological Appraisals.
Undertake habitat and protected species surveys within the individual's competence.
Support UKHab and other appropriate habitat classification and condition assessments.
Review ecological survey information provided by consultants.
Identify requirements for additional surveys or specialist ecological support.
Support ecological inputs into Environmental Impact Assessments and project environmental documentation.

Construction Support

Review RAMS and construction methodologies for ecological risks.
Provide ecological input into Construction Environmental Management Plans.
Develop and implement Species Protection Plans and ecological mitigation measures.
Undertake pre-start ecological briefings and toolbox talks.
Provide practical ecological advice to Site Managers, Engineers, Supervisors and subcontractors.
Attend planning and construction meetings where ecological constraints could affect delivery.

Sensitive Habitats & Peatland

Support the protection and management of sensitive Scottish habitats including:

Peatland and deep peat.
Blanket bog.
Wet heath.
Ancient woodland.
Native woodland.
Riparian habitats.
Freshwater environments.
Protected and designated sites.

Support implementation and monitoring of habitat and peatland restoration and reinstatement requirements.

Designated Sites

Provide ecological support for projects potentially affecting:

Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs).
Special Areas of Conservation (SACs).
Special Protection Areas (SPAs).
Ramsar sites.
National Nature Reserves.
Ancient Woodland.
Local Nature Conservation Sites.

Ensure project teams understand and implement controls associated with designated sites.

Biodiversity & Habitat Enhancement

Support delivery of project biodiversity objectives.
Identify opportunities for habitat enhancement and restoration.
Monitor habitat reinstatement following construction.
Support biodiversity monitoring programmes.
Assist with development and implementation of Biodiversity Enhancement Plans and client commitments.
Maintain evidence demonstrating delivery of ecological mitigation and enhancement measures.

Environmental Compliance

Provide ecological advice relating to applicable Scottish requirements including:

Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004.
Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.
Conservation (Natural Habitats, &c.) Regulations 1994, as amended.
Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
Environmental Authorisation (Scotland) Regulations 2018, where relevant.
Applicable planning conditions, licences, consents and client requirements.

Maintain awareness of legislative changes and guidance affecting ecological management in Scotland.

Ecological Incidents

Respond to ecological incidents and unexpected discoveries.
Immediately advise project teams where protected species or previously unidentified ecological constraints are encountered.
Support environmental incident investigations.
Escalate significant issues to the SHEQ Manager and Environmental Manager.
Support liaison with statutory bodies where required.
Capture and communicate lessons learned.

Stakeholder Engagement

Develop effective relationships with clients, project teams, landowners, ecological consultants, local authorities and statutory bodies including NatureScot, SEPA and relevant planning authorities.

Represent the project at ecological and environmental meetings as required.

Reporting & Assurance

Produce ecological inspection and monitoring reports.
Maintain ecological constraints registers.
Maintain records of licences, mitigation and monitoring requirements.
Track ecological actions through to closure.
Provide ecological information for project SHEQ reports.
Support environmental audits and client assurance visits.
Maintain auditable evidence demonstrating compliance with ecological commitments.

Key Accountabilities

The role is accountable for:

Effective management of ecological risks across project activities.
Competent delivery of the ECoW function.
Compliance with protected species legislation and licences.
Protection of sensitive habitats and designated sites.
Implementation of Species Protection Plans.
Accurate and timely ecological records.
Effective escalation of significant ecological risks.
Supporting habitat restoration and biodiversity commitments.
Prevention of avoidable ecological harm.

Essential Qualifications

Degree or equivalent qualification in Ecology, Environmental Science, Conservation Biology or a related discipline.
Appropriate membership of CIEEM or equivalent professional body.
Strong working knowledge of Scottish ecological legislation and protected species requirements.
Full UK Driving Licence.

Desirable Qualifications

Associate or Full Membership of CIEEM.
Protected species licences relevant to Scottish infrastructure projects.
CSCS/ECS or equivalent construction site competence.
ECoW training or demonstrable equivalent experience.
UKHab training.
Peatland assessment/restoration experience.
Environmental auditing qualification.

Essential Experience

Practical ecological experience within construction, utilities, infrastructure or a similar sector.
Experience undertaking ecological surveys and site inspections.
Experience working as an ECoW or providing equivalent construction-phase ecological support.
Strong knowledge of protected species and habitat management.
Ability to interpret ecological reports, Species Protection Plans and licence conditions.
Experience communicating ecological requirements to construction teams.

Desirable Experience

Power Transmission & Distribution projects.
Overhead line, underground cable and substation construction.
Major infrastructure projects in the Scottish Highlands and remote environments.
SSEN Transmission or SP Energy Networks projects.
Experience working around peatland, forestry and watercourses.
Experience working within or adjacent to internationally and nationally designated sites.
Experience managing ecological interfaces across geographically dispersed construction work fronts.

Skills & Competencies

Strong field ecology capability.
Excellent understanding of Scottish protected species requirements.
Ability to translate ecological requirements into practical construction controls.
Strong communication and influencing skills.
Confidence to challenge or stop activities where ecological harm may occur.
Strong technical reporting and record keeping.
Ability to work independently in remote and challenging environments.
Collaborative and solutions-focused approach.

Values & Behaviours

The Ecologist / ECoW will demonstrate professional integrity, sound ecological judgement and visible environmental leadership. They will work collaboratively with project teams to enable successful infrastructure delivery while ensuring Scotland's habitats, species and natural environment are appropriately protected.

The role holder will be fully empowered and expected to challenge, pause or stop activities where there is a foreseeable risk of significant ecological harm, breach of licence conditions or environmental non-compliance

jobs.title: Research Scientist and Project Director - College of Engineering - Environmental and Public Policy
jobs.description:
Carnegie Mellon University is a private, global research university that stands among the world’s most renowned education institutions. With ground-breaking brain science, path-breaking performances, creative start-ups, big data, big ambitions, hands-on learning, and a whole lot of robots, CMU doesn’t imagine the future, we invent it. If you’re passionate about joining a community that challenges the curious to deliver work that matters, your journey starts here!

The Department of Engineering and Public Policy (EPP) is a unique department in the College of Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University which addresses important problems in technology and policy. We educate technically skilled students to be leaders in policy-focused research; we work on policy problems in which the technology matters.

Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) seeks a Research Scientist to serve as Project Director for Industrial Futures within the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation. The position will lead research and programmatic activities at the intersection of industrial transformation, energy and climate, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, and regional economic development. The Research Scientist will lead the Industrial Futures focus area within the Scott Institute, working with faculty, researchers, students, and external partners across Carnegie Mellon and a network of domestic and international collaborators. The position

combines applied and scholarly research with project leadership, external engagement, policy communication, and mentorship. The Research Scientist will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

A central objective of the Industrial Futures initiative is to understand how technological change and the energy transition reshaping industry, firms, workers, and regions are — and how policy, innovation, and entrepreneurship can contribute to competitive, resilient, and sustainable industrial transitions. The portfolio connects research and engagement in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with international

research and partnerships addressing similar challenges around the world.

The Research Scientist will have substantial responsibility for two major components of this portfolio: CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, an international research collaboration focused on industrial transformation and decarbonization, and its links to CMU’s engagement in the Regional Technology and Infrastructure Consortium (RETI), which focuses on industrial innovation, hardtech entrepreneurship, and supporting policies. As Project Director, the Research Scientist will help shape the intellectual agenda of these initiatives while managing research programs, coordinating partners, developing new projects, and translating research findings for policy and practitioner audiences.

Core Responsibilities

Research Leadership:

Develop, lead, and contribute to applied research on industrial transformation, energy and industrial policy, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and regional economic change.
Help define and advance the research agenda for the Industrial Futures focus area and lead or co-lead projects from research design through analysis, publication, and dissemination.
Conduct rigorous quantitative and qualitative research using methods appropriate to the research question, including quantitative empirical analysis, operations research, econometrics, labor-market and regional economic analysis, qualitative and interview-based research, and techno-economic or energy-systems analysis.
Maintain and develop datasets, analytical tools, and methodological frameworks that support research across multiple projects.
Develop and contribute to peer-reviewed publications, policy reports, working papers, and other scholarly outputs.
Collaborate with researchers across Carnegie Mellon and partner institutions, connecting research on industrial transformation in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with related international research and identifying opportunities for new interdisciplinary work.

Program And Project Leadership

Serve as Project Director for the Industrial Futures portfolio, providing intellectual and programmatic leadership across its research and engagement activities.
Coordinate complex, multi-institution research projects, including developing and reviewing deliverables, maintaining timelines, leading project meetings, monitoring progress, and addressing barriers to project success.
Serve as a primary point of contact for research partners, subcontractors, funding organizations, and other collaborators.
Support CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, including coordinating research across partner institutions, managing a collaborative seed-grant program, and leading knowledge-sharing activities such as newsletters, workshops, and study tours.
Coordinate project reporting and communications with research sponsors and contribute to new grant proposals, including research design, technical narratives, work plans, and partnership development.
Connect researchers across the Scott Institute and broader university who are working on related topics or methodologies and facilitate opportunities for collaboration.

External Engagement And Policy Impact

Build and maintain relationships with industry, government, nonprofit and community organizations, research institutions, funding partners, and other stakeholders.
Engage with firms, policymakers, entrepreneurs, workforce organizations, and regional stakeholders to understand the opportunities and challenges associated with industrial and technological transformation.
Represent Carnegie Mellon and the Scott Institute in external meetings, workshops, conferences, study tours, working groups, and other convenings.
Translate research into accessible and decision-relevant formats, including policy briefs, reports, presentations, data visualizations, and other communications for policymakers and practitioners.
Work with Scott Institute communications and policy staff to disseminate research findings and contribute to policy-informing activities such as briefings, testimony, public comments, and workshops.

Advising And Mentorship

Advise or co-advise student and researcher projects associated with the Industrial Futures portfolio.
Mentor students and junior researchers on research design, quantitative and qualitative methods, data analysis and visualization, and research writing.
Provide feedback on research products, manuscripts, presentations, and policy communications.
Contribute to a collaborative, intellectually engaged, productive, and supportive research culture within the Scott Institute and collaborating research groups.

Adaptability, excellence, and passion are vital qualities within Carnegie Mellon University. We are in search of a team member who can effectively interact with a varied population of internal and external partners at a high level of integrity. We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work

Qualifications

Ph.D. in engineering, public policy, economics, management, or a related field.
Approximately 3–5 years of relevant research or professional experience. Significant and directly relevant research, project leadership, or stakeholder- engagement experience obtained during doctoral training may count toward this requirement.
Demonstrated research experience in one or more of the following areas: energy, industrial transformation, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, or regional economic development.
Demonstrated ability to design and conduct rigorous applied research using multiple quantitative and/or qualitative approaches. Relevant methods may include quantitative empirical research, operations research, econometrics, labor-market or regional economic analysis, qualitative and interview-based methods, and techno-economic or energy-systems analysis.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex datasets using R, Python, Stata, or comparable analytical software.
Experience developing scholarly research products, including peer-reviewed publications, working papers, or major research reports.
Strong project-management and organizational skills and the ability to coordinate activities and collaborators across complex projects.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical research to academic and nonacademic audiences.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across disciplines and institutions.
A combination of education and relevant experience from which comparable knowledge is demonstrated may be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

Research or professional experience related to industrial decarbonization, industrial or energy policy, hardtech innovation and entrepreneurship, or regional industrial transformation.
Experience working at the intersection of academic research and policy or practice and engaging directly with industry, government, community organizations, or other external stakeholders.
Experience managing multi-institutional or interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Experience developing research proposals or contributing to externally funded research programs.
Experience translating academic research into policy-relevant communications for nonacademic audiences.
Experience mentoring students or junior researchers.
Experience working in international research collaborations or comparative research settings.

Requirements

Successful background check

Position Characteristics

This position is designed for a researcher who enjoys moving between rigorous research and real-world engagement. The successful candidate will be comfortable leading research while also building partnerships, managing collaborative projects, mentoring students, communicating findings to policymakers and practitioners, and developing new research opportunities.

The role requires intellectual curiosity, independence, initiative, strong organizational skills, and a collaborative approach. Because the Industrial Futures portfolio connects local, national, and international research and engagement, the position may involve periodic domestic and international travel.

The Research Scientist will be based at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

Work arrangement:
In-person expected

Benefits eligible employees enjoy a wide array of benefits including comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision insurance as well as a generous retirement savings program with employer contributions. Unlock your potential with tuition benefits, take well-deserved breaks with ample paid time off and observed holidays, and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.

Additional perks include a free Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus pass, access to our Family Concierge Team to help navigate childcare needs, fitness center access, and much more!

For a comprehensive overview of the benefits available, explore our Benefits page.

We appreciate your unique skills and the perspective you bring. Job Type

Full-time

Description

About You

You are an experienced environmental chemist or scientist with experience reviewing and validating environmental data and supporting field programs. You are a strategic thinker who thrives on the challenges of these complex, interdisciplinary environment matters. A lifelong learner, you want to keep growing intellectually and professionally. Collaborating with colleagues with diverse expertise is exciting for you, and you are also comfortable working independently. Quality management and integrity are among your strongest principles.

About Integral

Integral Consulting Inc. is a science and engineering firm delivering sound technical solutions to meet today’s challenges in the health, environmental, and natural resource arenas. We are a values-driven collaborative team that is as passionate about company culture as we are about the work we do for our clients. Since our founding in 2002, we have operated with a demonstrated commitment to the well-being, diversity, and professional development of our staff and an equal commitment to strong partnerships with our clients and teaming partners. We are a company where people come to solve today’s toughest environmental challenges through innovative ideas, exceptional teamwork, and dedication to accuracy and technical quality.

About The Job

We are currently seeking a chemist with 3 to 5 years of experience who has the desire to also do some field work with our Sediment and Water Investigations and Monitoring practice in our Santa Cruz, California office. The position supports multiple clients and projects, with day-to-day responsibilities that primarily include reviewing and validating of laboratory data, managing a small wet laboratory, supporting field efforts, and on occasion performing some fieldwork. The selected candidate will work closely with project team members on water quality monitoring, stormwater planning and monitoring, and sediment sampling efforts across the Bay Area and Northern California.

This position is primarily in-office, but opportunities for hybrid work may be available.

Requirements

Responsibilities

As a Scientist, your job functions will include, but not be limited to:

Assisting with sample control procedures for multiple projects
Tracking submission of samples to chemistry laboratories and receipt of associated data for multiple projects
Adhering quality control and quality assurance procedures to ensure data integrity
Communicating with laboratories regarding data quality questions or corrections that may be needed.
Performing quality assurance reviews of technical analyses and results
Managing laboratory and data validation subcontractors
Reviewing CEDEN EDDs and applying the Quality Assurance codes associated with chemistry excursions
Performing Stage 2B and Stage 3 data validation and reporting following EPA’s National Functional Guidelines
Assisting in writing formal QAQC reports
Executing laboratory bottle cleaning procedures and maintaining facility organization
Managing and maintaining a small wet laboratory
Collecting river, stream, creek, ocean, and stormwater samples
Collecting sediment and surface water samples both on land and from boats
Maintaining accurate field and laboratory logs
Adhering to company, project, state, and federal safety policies

Fieldwork will occasionally be required; those responsibilities may include long days in the field, extended exposure to the elements (sun, rain, wind), prolonged standing, and other physically demanding tasks such as lifting equipment or materials. You must have the ability and willingness to work outdoors in a wide range of weather conditions. Your work schedule at times will be defined by storm forecasts and may include working nights and/or weekends.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
The Department of Public Health prioritizes equitable and inclusive access to quality healthcare for its community and values the importance of diversity in its workforce. All employees at the Department of Public Health work to advance equity, inclusion, and diversity with a specific lens and focus on race, ethnicity, gender, sex, sexuality, disability, and immigration status.

This is a Citywide Exam posting. Your application to this posting is an application to take a citywide exam.

Application Opening – Friday, November 7, 2025
Application Deadline - Continuous
Salary:  $133,588 - $162,266 Annually
Appointment Type: Permanent Civil Service
Recruitment ID: CCT-6120-H00189 [REF58141O]
Work Arrangement: Onsite

San Francisco is a vibrant and dynamic city, on the forefront of economic growth & innovation, urban development, arts & entertainment, as well as social issues & change. This rich tapestry of culture and ideas is sustained by our City's commitment to heighten the quality of life for the diverse population of San Franciscans and residents of the greater Bay Area. Our employees play an important role not only in making our City what it is today, but also in shaping the future of San Francisco. 

The Mission of the San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH) is to protect and promote the health of all San Franciscans. Fulfilling this mission requires employees working across our hospitals, clinics, programs, and offices to deliver services and support the communities we serve. Individuals interested in joining SFDPH should expect to work in person across these settings.

The San Francisco Health Network, Population Health, Behavioral Health Services, and Administration are the core divisions of SFDPH. The San Francisco Health Network is the City’s only complete system of care and has locations throughout the City, including Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center, Laguna Honda Hospital and Rehabilitation Center, and over 15 primary care health centers. The Population Health Division (PHD) provides core public health services for the City and County of San Francisco: health protection, health promotion, disease and injury prevention, and disaster preparedness and response. Behavioral Health Services operates in conjunction with SFHN and provides a range of mental health and substance use treatment services.

START with this
⚠️ REQUIRED ASSESSMENT✅ at: https://forms.gle/px3en7zsY8Arv72M6.

Then
, submit an  online application

Role description

Under direction, the 6120 Consumer Protection Environmental Health Inspector conducts inspections of housing, industrial plants and premises, solid waste facilities and vehicles, sources of noise emission, fixed and mobile food facilities, and public health and safety hazards in order to enforce established laws, ordinances and regulations pertaining to abatement of violations found; recommends appropriate actions to remedy situations; issues citations; prepares pertinent reports; implements various environmental health programs and services; and performs related duties as required.

Essential Duties Include

Enforces provisions of the health, housing, planning and air pollution codes; State health and safety, industrial relations, administrative, agricultural and penal codes, State general safety orders, and sanitary aspects of meat plant construction, local ordinances and noise abatement and other environmental hazards; may be required to specialize in any of these or other activities related to the duties of the class.
Investigates complaints involving buildings; takes necessary action to abate illegal health, sanitary and safety conditions; coordinates efforts with the various city department in the enforcement of the building, electrical, plumbing, fire and police codes; appears as witness in court litigation when required and testifies in cases involving food establishments, housing, commercial buildings, and other matters.
Conducts complaint inspections of dwellings, hotels, apartment houses, business establishments and other multiple dwellings; checks for sanitation, general maintenance of structural and operational features, light, ventilation, use and occupancy, safety and for compliance with applicable codes; detects violations; coordinates efforts with applicable city departments in the enforcement of appropriate codes; makes follow-up inspections to assure ordered corrections have been made; makes recommendations for order of vacation or condemnation of buildings remaining in violation; prepares condemnation reports; appears and testifies at condemnation hearings.
Conducts complaint inspections at sites of noise sources to determine the noise source; prepares legal notices of violations of noise ordinance; recommends corrective action to be taken by the violators; prepares cases for argument before the Variance Board.
Conducts food and drink establishment inspections; detects violations; orders corrections to effect compliance with established requirements, recommends alternative design modification and equipping to comply with applicable codes and regulations; processes and insures compliance of applicable portions of building permit applications and plans; advises operators and employees on proper handling procedures and sanitary methods; may obtains samples of products and submits same for laboratory analyses, examinations and tests; conducts foodborne illness investigations; recommends issuance or denial of permits to operate food establishments or suspension or revocation of existing permits; appears and testifies at hearings; prepares related notices to courts, records and correspondence pertaining to duties performed, observations made, violations found and actions taken.
Conducts miscellaneous inspections of facilities, including laundry establishments, ambulatory homes for the aged, overnight animal boarding for compliance with pertinent regulations, and recommends issuance or denial of permit to operate; investigates growth of poison oak and other noxious weeds; investigates and adjudicates refuse removal rate disputes between scavenger companies and the public; investigates all complaints regarding the lack of required refuse collection service and/or un-lawful disposal of refuse, debris and garbage accumulation on lots, streets, public places, yards; investigates infestations of rodents and other vermin; investigates mosquito complaints; checks applications and plans for construction of swimming pools; issues permits for small water supplies; inspects for cross connections and approves backflow prevention devices.
Performs other special and miscellaneous duties as required, including sanitation and hazardous materials surveys, domestic water supply sampling, recreational water facilities; reclaimed waste waters; participates in meetings and educational conferences.

The 6120 Consumer Protection Environmental Health Inspector may perform other duties as assigned/required.

Please note that incumbents in this classification may be required to perform duties as listed in the class specification, which can be found on DHR’s website: https://careers.sf.gov/classifications/)

How to qualify

Minimum Qualifications (required)

License and Certification:

Possession of a REHS (Registered Environmental Health Specialist) Certificate, issued by the State of California Department of Public Health Services
Possession of/ability to obtain a valid California Driver's License.

Please include your California REHS number with your application and/or upload a copy of your California REHS certificate.

Only applicants who are certified in California can qualify for this recruitment. You can find more information on the CDPH REHS website (https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DRSEM/Pages/EMB/REHS/REHS.aspx), including information for those who are certified in other jurisdictions or want more information on How to Become a Registered Environmental Health Specialist.

Verification

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications as listed in the job ad. Review SF Careers Employment Applications for considerations taken when reviewing applications.  

Note:
Falsifying one’s education, training, or work experience or attempted deception on the application may result in disqualification for this and future job opportunities with the City and County of San Francisco.

What else should I know?

Selection Procedures

After application submission, candidates deemed qualified must complete all subsequent steps to advance in this selection process, which includes the following.

Training and Experience Evaluation (Weight: 100%):
Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications will be invited to participate in a Training and Experience Evaluation that is designed to measure the knowledge, skills, and abilities in job-related areas which may include but not be limited to: Knowledge of environmental health sciences, of legal requirements, of field inspection; Decision Making ability, Written communications ability, Oral communication ability, Interpersonal relations ability; Ability to utilize technology, to manage time effectively.

You can complete the Training and Experience Evaluation now at: https://forms.gle/px3en7zsY8Arv72M6.

The link to the training and experience evaluation will also be emailed to the address listed on the candidate’s online application. Candidates will be required to respond to the training and experience evaluation in the time frame indicated and must submit the completed questionnaire as directed to have it evaluated. Responses cannot be changed once submitted. Candidates will be evaluated based on their responses.

Candidates must achieve a passing score on the training and experience evaluation to continue in the selection process and will be placed on the confidential eligible list in rank order according to their final score.

Additional selection processes may be conducted by the hiring department prior to making final hiring decisions.

Certification

Eligible List/Score Report

A confidential eligible list of applicant names that have passed the civil service examination process will be created and used for certification purposes only. An examination score report will be established, so applicants can view the ranks, final scores and number of eligible candidates. Applicant information, including names of applicants on the eligible list, shall not be made public unless required by law. jobs.title: Senior Environmental Program Manager
jobs.description:
Applications will be reviewed regularly, and interviews may be conducted prior to the application close date.

As a Senior Environmental Program Manager, you will lead the day-to-day management and compliance of National Pollutant Discharge Elimination (NPDES), King County Industrial Waste Discharge, and support other stormwater elements for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). You will lead staff members to provide technical oversight of field monitoring, inspection, documentation, contract management and reporting. The position requires complex program implementation as well as environmental program development in response to new and changing regulations, environmental goals and Airport operations.

You will lead and define both the long-term and short-term stormwater strategies related to planning, implementation and oversight of SEA’s stormwater management programs, including maintaining compliance with industrial stormwater permits, stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPP), stormwater monitoring, best management practices, and water quality improvement initiatives.
You will serve as SEA’s technical expert on stormwater regulations and water quality requirements, providing guidance on the SEA NPDES permit, Washington State stormwater regulations, Clean Water Act requirements and emerging regulatory issues affecting airport operations.
You will provide strategic and technical leadership during planning, design, and construction of airport capital projects by reviewing stormwater infrastructure, drainage design, treatment systems, construction activities, and operational impacts to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and Port policies.
You will negotiate strategic and technical requirements and compliance strategies with regulatory agencies, airport tenants, consultants, contractors and internal departments while representing SEA during inspections, permit discussions, audits, enforcement matters and interagency coordination efforts.
You will manage consultant contracts and outside technical services supporting stormwater planning, engineering evaluations, monitoring, modeling, regulatory compliance and implementation of stormwater improvement projects. You will develop scope of work, budget, schedule and performance requirements while reviewing and approving technical deliverables.
You will act as a key member of the environmental spill team, responsible for responding by vehicle to incidents at the airport, monitoring spill response, directing cleaning resources and providing input on impacted stormwater resources.
You will supervise a team of up to 3 stormwater professionals, responsible for all aspects of development, performance and evaluation.

Who you are:

Experienced – You have five (5) years of experience in environmental and/or sustainability, to include two (2) years of lead, mentor or supervisory experience including leading a project or process.
Desired – We hope you have a bachelor’s degree in environmental science or environmental engineering, civil engineering or a related discipline. We hope you have certifications such as a Professional Engineer (PE), Licensed HydroGeologist (LHG), Certified Professional in Stormwater Quality (CPSWQ), Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC).
Committed to Equity – You will apply equity and exemplify shared values, behaviors, and practices in all aspects of the work. At the Port of Seattle, equity is a daily responsibility and a foundational expectation for all Port employees.
Technical Expert – You possess recognized expertise in stormwater management principles, hydrology, drainage systems, stormwater treatment technologies, water quality monitoring and environmental compliance practices. You have extensive knowledge of stormwater regulations, including National Pollutant Discharge Elimination (NPDES) permitting requirements, Clean Water Act regulations, Washington State stormwater requirements and related environmental standards. You have knowledge of airport, industrial, transportation or other highly regulated environmental programs.
Efficient Communicator – You have proven effective verbal and written communication skills and are adept at communicating complex technical, regulatory and environmental information to diverse audiences including executives, regulators, airport tenants, contractors, consultants elected officials and the public. You have proven negotiation, facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, as well as experience building and maintaining effective relationships with regulators.
Leader – You can effectively lead multidisciplinary people and project teams on complex environmental programs while collaborating with airport operations, engineering, maintenance, planning, tenants, consultants, and regulatory agencies. You understand how operational requirements, regulatory obligations, emerging environmental issues, and community expectations influence airport decision-making.
Analytical Problem-Solver – You can analyze complex stormwater and environmental challenges, analyze technical data, interpret changing regulations, and develop strategic, innovative, and practical solutions. You can identify compliance risks, recommend improvements, and support decisions affecting airport infrastructure, operations, and long-term environmental performance.

What Else You Need To Know

Driver’s License – You will need a valid Washington State Driver’s License, or the ability to obtain one, is required in order to travel locally to project sites.
Work Schedule – Your normal work schedule will be Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (40 hours per week). Slightly more flexible start and end times are available in this role. You may be required to work any and all assigned shifts, including weekends and holidays. You will have a rotation responsibility (approximately 7 weeks per calendar year) for 24 hours on call spill response and may be required to work during emergencies.
Work Environment – This is a field-based position. You will work throughout Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), maritime facilities, and other Port of Seattle properties, with occasional work in an office setting for administrative tasks, meetings, or training.
Washington State Residency Requirement – Employees must establish a residence in Washington state within 30 days of their first day of employment and must maintain a residence in Washington State during their employment with the Port of Seattle. If a position is eligible to telework, work performed while teleworking must be performed in Washington State.
Security Requirements – As the successful candidate, you must pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check as well as a criminal history background check with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Your employment will be contingent upon obtaining a Port of Seattle ID badge upon clearance.

Why You'll Love It Here

The Port of Seattle offers an extensive benefits package that rewards our staff for their valuable contributions towards the Port‘s mission. In addition to the summary below, benefit details for non-represented positions can be found
on the Port of Seattle‘s website.
If the position is represented by a union, please refer to the “
Collective Bargaining Agreement
” or contact the appropriate Union Representative for specific information related to benefits and eligibility.

Healthcare – Medical, Dental, and Vision Care with options that work for you and your family.
Paid Vacation – Just about four weeks per year that increases with tenure to rest and rejuvenate.
Paid Sick Leave – At least one hour of sick leave for every 40 hours worked.
Holidays – More than ten days per year to celebrate with family and friends away from work.
Pension/Retirement Plans – A pension and additional savings plans to prepare for your future after the Port.
Getting to Work – From subsidized parking and a low-cost public transit card to alternative work arrangements giving you an opportunity to work hybrid.
Parental Leave – Six weeks of paid leave to spend with new additions to your immediate family.
Development – From tuition reimbursement, training, stretch assignments and internal internships, we support a learning culture.
Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion – The Port of Seattle values diversity as a source of innovation and strength. We are actively working across the organization to create a culture where all employees – regardless of race, gender, and other identities – succeed and reach their fullest potential.
Work-Life Balance – We provide the resources to help you create habits to be healthy and balanced.
Mission Driven – We are focused together in promoting economic opportunities and quality of life in the region by advancing trade, travel, commerce, and job creation in an equitable, accountable, and environmentally responsible manner.

Why the Port of Seattle:

Every role at the Port of Seattle is vital to our thriving community. We are a leader in moving people and cargo across the country and around the world. With facilities and property ranging in scope from a half-acre park to one of the largest airports and container terminals on the West Coast, we maximize the public assets in our portfolio with an eye toward best uses and environmental sustainability. Find out more here.

Our vision is to create a Port that mirrors – throughout its breadth of operations and services and within its leadership – the diversity of our communities, instill principles of equity into its culture, and ensures a fair and intentional distribution of opportunities to expand economic development and quality of life for all in our region. Find out more about how our values RAISE us up and our commitment to equity.

Based in Western Canada for over 110 years, McElhanney offers innovative and practical engineering, surveying, mapping, planning, landscape architecture, and environmental services. to help lead the growth of our practice within the energy, mining, natural resource, and industrial sectors
across Western Canada.

The successful candidate will play a key role in growing McElhanney's presence in the Energy & Resources market by identifying opportunities, developing client relationships, and leading multidisciplinary environmental projects from proposal through completion.

Air Quality Testers (AQT)

Position Highlights

10% uncapped personal sales commission

Career advancement into senior consulting and project management

About Air Quality Testers

Air Quality Testers is an independent environmental consulting firm specializing in science-based environmental testing, building investigations, and indoor environmental assessments.

AQT performs third-party testing and consulting and does not perform remediation. This allows our consultants to provide clients with objective findings and independent recommendations.

Our services include:

Mold and moisture assessments

Indoor air quality testing

VOC and formaldehyde testing

Asbestos inspections and sampling

Lead inspections and testing

Fire and smoke contamination assessments

Industrial hygiene services

Allergen testing

Water and soil testing

Post-remediation verification

Building-related environmental consulting

The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced and certified Environmental Consultant who is comfortable managing the full client experience—from the initial consultation and project sale through inspection, sampling, documentation, and final recommendations.

AQT provides inbound client opportunities, environmental testing equipment, personal protective equipment, laboratory coordination, operational support, and report-production assistance.

This position is designed for a consultant who wants the flexibility of a part-time to full-time schedule, hourly security, and significant commission-based earning potential.

Consultants who provide excellent service, close more projects, and appropriately expand project scopes can substantially increase their earnings.

Primary Responsibilities

Consult with inbound residential and commercial clients

Understand client concerns and recommend appropriate environmental testing

Develop project scopes, pricing, and sampling plans

Close assigned client opportunities

Schedule and confirm projects

Identify appropriate additional testing when site conditions support it

Perform environmental inspections and sample collection

Conduct moisture, infrared, and visual building assessments

Inspect attics, crawlspaces, and other accessible building areas when safe

Document observations through photographs, videos, and detailed field notes

Complete chain-of-custody and laboratory documentation

Maintain accurate project, CRM, and timekeeping records

Communicate preliminary observations professionally without overstating findings

Review laboratory results and report drafts

Add project-specific findings, recommendations, and corrections

Coordinate with AQT’s report-writing and quality-assurance team

Maintain and protect company equipment

Follow company safety, ethical, and quality-control procedures

Hourly Compensation

The consultant is paid hourly for all compensable work, including:

Client consultations and sales calls

Follow-up communication

Compensable business travel

Inspections and sampling

Laboratory drop-offs

Equipment and supply stops

Field documentation

Report review and recommendations

Meetings and training

Required administrative work

Consultants using an approved personal vehicle for authorized company business receive separate mileage reimbursement, plus reimbursement for approved parking and tolls.

Commission Compensation

The consultant earns:

10% of qualifying collected AQT service revenue from projects personally closed by the consultant.

The written commission agreement will explain:

What qualifies as personally closed revenue

When commission is earned

When commission is paid

Client payment requirements

Cancellations and refunds

Shared projects

Onsite additions

Adjustments and employment termination

Commission is uncapped, meaning there is no maximum amount the consultant can earn from qualifying revenue.

Required Qualifications

Currently holds at least one relevant environmental, indoor-air-quality, mold, asbestos, lead, industrial-hygiene, or building-science certification

Professional experience performing environmental inspections, testing, sampling, or building assessments

Strong client-consultation and sales-closing ability

Ability to develop appropriate testing scopes and sampling plans

Strong technical documentation and report-review skills

Ability to explain technical information clearly and professionally

Strong attention to detail and commitment to objective consulting

Ability to work independently in residential and commercial environments

Comfortable accessing attics, crawlspaces, and other building areas when safe

Valid driver’s license

The Geo-Spatial Analyst supports HII Mission Technologies by delivering precise, high quality geospatial products and analysis that enhance mission readiness and decision-making for defense, intelligence, and national security customers. Maintain and update process documentation, data standards, and report templates aligned with HII quality expectations.
Generate maps, geospatial visualizations, and supporting materials for briefings, presentations, and mission reports.

5 years relevant experience with Bachelors in related field; 3 years relevant experience with Masters in related field; 0 years experience with PhD or Juris Doctorate in related field; or High School Diploma or equivalent and 9 years relevant experience.

Strong data analysis skills, including Excel functions such as PivotTables, formatting and standardization, and formula creation.

Under the direction of the Environmental Superintendent or Senior Environmental Engineer, assist with the implementation of programs and procedures to ensure environmental compliance for KG Mining (Bald Mountain), Inc., Bald Mountain Mine, located in White Pine County Nevada. This is a high-impact global role for an accomplished scientist or engineer who can move confidently between technical depth, strategic direction and practical implementation. Set the global environmental technology strategy across waste, wastewater, air emissions, vent treatment, recovery and recycling, informed by Best Available Techniques (BAT).

jobs.description:

Conservation Agriculture (Fixed-Term)

Organization

One Acre Fund

Posted 4 Sep 2026 Closing date 3 Dec 2026

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.

Responsibilities

Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.
Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.
Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.
Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning.

Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption

Provide hands-on technical guidance to field teams delivering farmer trainings, workshops, Farmer Field Schools, and demonstration plots.
Build the capacity of field staff and local extension agents to effectively promote and support conservation agriculture adoption.

Agronomic Research, Practice Optimization & Impact

Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability.

Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models.

Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership

Build and manage strategic relationships with public, private, NGO, academic, and other technical partners supporting conservation agriculture initiatives.
Coordinate project plans, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and data sharing across internal teams and external consortium partners.
Represent the conservation agriculture program in technical discussions and ensure strong alignment between farmer needs, organizational priorities, and partner objectives.
Identify opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and resource mobilization that strengthen program quality, scale, and long-term impact.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Master’s degree in Agronomy, Agroecology, Crop Science, Soil Science, or a closely related agricultural field.
Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, conservation agriculture, regenerative agriculture, or agroecological farming systems.
Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder projects involving government, NGOs, research institutions, academia, or private-sector partners.
Strong hands-on experience working directly with smallholder farmers and field teams, with willingness to travel extensively and spend significant time in rural settings.

Tetra Tech is looking for an Ecological Clerk of Works
to join Us in Shaping the Future of Ecological Delivery.
We have opportunities available across Scotland including Inverness, Edinburgh and Glasgow.

Join our collaborative Ecology team to support some of Scotland’s most exciting renewable energy, residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects. This is an opportunity to play a hands-on role in protecting biodiversity while helping clients deliver projects safely, compliantly, and efficiently. You’ll work within a technically strong, multi-disciplinary environment where your ecological expertise, practical judgment, and communication skills will make a visible impact on project outcomes.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As an Ecological Clerk of Works, you will provide day-to-day ecological supervision and monitoring on large-scale construction and development sites across Scotland. You will help ensure ecological mitigation, protection measures, and site controls are implemented effectively, while supporting contractors, clients, and project teams with practical, proportionate solutions.

The role supports a wide range of ecological services for renewable energy, residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects, including onshore elements of major wind developments, as well as onshore wind and solar schemes. You will contribute to compliant project delivery by carrying out site inspections, supervising ecological surveys, maintaining accurate records, and responding to unexpected ecological issues on site.

Your Impact in This Position

You will help shape successful project delivery by protecting ecological interests while keeping works moving in a practical and compliant way. Your contribution will support regional and national project success, strengthen client confidence, and help maintain the organisation’s reputation for technical quality, innovation, and sustainable outcomes.

You will also play an important mentoring role, supporting junior ECoWs and technicians, sharing knowledge, and helping build capability within the wider ecology team.

Core Capabilities

Technical Expertise

Apply strong ecological knowledge and field-based experience to deliver effective site supervision, make sound decisions on site, and support protected species and mitigation requirements.

Project Management

jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

About The Role

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is seeking a Lead Business Analyst
to serve as the senior BA lead on a federal environmental data integration program. In this role, you will bring expertise in Endangered Species Act - Section 7 consultation processes and federal environmental platform workflows to drive requirements, compliance validation, and cross-agency coordination at the highest level.

Work Location:
Remote

Roles And Responsibilities

Serve as the senior business analysis lead across the full project, providing SME-level expertise in Endangered Species Act - Section 7 consultation processes, platform workflows, and multi-agency coordination
Lead requirements elicitation and documentation for all platform changes including species display, decision logic updates, template updates, and consultation routing
Conduct gap analysis between current platform capabilities and integration requirements, documenting findings for technical deliverables
Facilitate joint requirements workshops with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Ecological Services and NOAA Fisheries SMEs
Lead the development of consultation logic alignment documentation for joint agency use
Support compliance validation by verifying that species list generation, decision logic, template content, and consultation routing meet regulatory requirements
Coordinate with government SMEs to obtain required approvals and sign-offs on compliance-critical deliverables
Lead pilot consultation workflow design, defining scenarios covering all consultation types
Analyze pilot results and live consultation feedback, translating findings into actionable system updates
Lead the development of the Pilot Report with Metrics, capturing consultation cycle times, completion rates, defect summaries, and actionable findings from pilot workflow execution
Lead the development of the Endangered Species Act - Section 7 Compliance Validation Checklist, documenting validation criteria for species list generation accuracy, decision logic correctness, template content completeness, and consultation routing
Coordinate government review and acceptance of Updated DKeys and Consultation Package Builder Assets, ensuring all content meets regulatory requirements and agency sign-off is obtained
Contribute to final operational documentation and year-end reporting

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

Bachelors degree and 10 years professional experience or a Masters degree and 8 years professional experience or an Associates degree and 12 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 16 years' professional experience.
U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance
Extensive years of business analysis experience on federal IT programs
Expertise in Endangered Species Act - Section 7 consultation processes
Experience with federal environmental regulatory systems and multi-agency coordination
Strong requirements elicitation, documentation, and stakeholder facilitation skills
Experience supporting compliance validation activities on federal programs
Experience capturing and reporting pilot metrics including cycle times, completion rates, and defect summaries
Experience facilitating OMB or executive-level government reviews and demonstration preparation

Preferred Qualifications

CBAP or equivalent BA certification preferred
Direct experience with the FWS Information for Planning and Consultation (IPaC) platform, Ecological Services, or NOAA Fisheries systems
Experience with DOI, FWS, or NOAA Fisheries programs
Familiarity with data migration or system integration projects in a federal context
Active Public Trust Clearance

Details

Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual's experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. A full listing of available benefits can be viewed at https://www.careers.peraton.com/benefits.

However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Takes part in providing local technical assistance for the collection, identification, and compiling of observational and spatial data concerning a variety of biological, physical, and earth sciences.
