jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Senior Environmental Scientist – Environmental Permitting & Compliance
to support our Earth & Environment Team in New York
. This position will support a diverse portfolio of energy, transportation, infrastructure, and development projects, with opportunities to work across environmental permitting, natural resources, and construction environmental compliance.

The successful candidate will be a versatile environmental professional with experience working in New York City and Long Island and comfortable supporting projects both in the field and in the office. Field responsibilities may include natural resource surveys, wetland delineations, environmental inspections, construction compliance monitoring, and coastal or marine field assignments. Office responsibilities may include preparation of environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, agency coordination materials, and environmental compliance documentation.

Your Impact

Conduct environmental field investigations, including wetland delineations, habitat assessments, natural resource surveys, and construction compliance inspections.
Support federal, state, and local environmental permitting for projects in New York City and Long Island.
Prepare environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, agency coordination materials, and compliance documentation.
Interpret permit conditions, environmental commitments, construction plans, and environmental specifications and communicate requirements to project teams and contractors.
Perform environmental inspections and construction compliance monitoring for energy, transportation, utility, infrastructure, and development projects.
Support coastal and marine environmental compliance activities, including field monitoring and coordination with construction contractors and environmental specialists, as needed.
Review construction work plans and method statements for activities occurring in or adjacent to environmentally sensitive resources.
Identify environmental compliance issues and work with project managers, contractors, and technical specialists to develop practical corrective actions.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, planners, environmental scientists, construction managers, regulatory specialists, and subcontractors.
Provide technical guidance and QA/QC oversight to junior environmental staff and field personnel.
Support multiple projects and assignments depending on project needs, including a combination of office-based technical work and field assignments.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
5 to 7 years of experience in environmental consulting, environmental permitting, natural resource assessment, and/or construction environmental compliance.
Experience working on environmental projects in New York City and/or Long Island, with familiarity with the region’s regulatory environment and infrastructure setting.
Experience conducting environmental fieldwork, which may include wetland delineations, natural resource surveys, construction monitoring, or environmental inspections.
Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience preparing environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, or similar environmental documentation.
Ability to interpret environmental permits, construction drawings, environmental specifications, and regulatory requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with project managers, contractors, field crews, clients, and regulatory agencies.
Ability to work independently in the field while also collaborating effectively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify environmental risks and recommend practical solutions.
Ability and willingness to work in a variety of field conditions, including construction sites, wetlands, coastal environments, and potentially vessel-based settings.
Ability to travel throughout New York City, Long Island, and the surrounding region based on project needs.
Proven commitment to workplace health and safety and compliance with WSP health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, or a related discipline.
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) certification or progress toward certification.
Experience with environmental permitting and agency coordination involving NYSDEC, USACE, NYC agencies, Nassau County, Suffolk County, and other applicable local regulatory authorities.
Familiarity with wetland, waterway, coastal, and natural resource permitting requirements applicable to New York City and Long Island.
Experience supporting energy, utility, transportation, infrastructure, or development projects in the New York metropolitan area.
Experience with coastal or marine environmental compliance and monitoring.
Experience leading field teams or providing technical oversight to junior staff.
40-Hour OSHA HAZWOPER training (29 CFR 1910.120) preferred.
Basic First Aid and Adult CPR training desired.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary (all locations): $100,000 - $130,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
**About the engagement**  
A state regulatory agency needs a spatial analysis of licensed delivery operations in a regulated market: where delivery service exists, where it does not, and which populations sit outside any current service area. The agency will use the resulting map to evaluate service area expansion requests and to identify underserved geography. The product becomes a standing tool the agency maintains after the engagement ends.

**What you would do**

* Geocode and validate licensed operator and delivery asset location data provided by the client
* Build service area layers using defensible assumptions, including drive\-time isochrones rather than simple radius buffers
* Overlay coverage against population, density, and relevant demographic geography to identify and quantify service gaps
* Produce an interactive web map that agency staff can use without desktop GIS software or a paid license
* Produce static, print\-quality map exhibits suitable for a report submitted to a state legislature
* Document data sources, projections, service area assumptions, and update procedures so agency staff can refresh the map in future cycles
* Deliver clean project files and layers in a format the client retains

**Required**

* Three or more years of applied GIS work with a portfolio of finished maps
* Proficiency with ArcGIS Pro or QGIS, and comfort producing web\-deliverable output (ArcGIS Online, Leaflet, Mapbox, Felt, or comparable)
* Geocoding and address validation experience with messy administrative data
* Network or drive\-time service area analysis experience
* Strong cartographic judgment. Output will be read by policymakers, not analysts
* Ability to document methods clearly enough for someone else to reproduce them
* Availability to deliver against fixed dates in November and December

**Preferred**

* Bachelor's or master's in geography, GIS, urban planning, public health, or a related field
* Experience with public sector or regulatory clients
* Python scripting for geoprocessing automation
* Experience with accessibility or service coverage analysis in any sector, including health care, transit, food access, or broadband

Pay: $65\.00 per hour

Expected hours: 35\.0 per week

Work Location: Remote

INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.

GENERAL INFORMATION

Project: AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay
Duty station: Asunción, Paraguay
Part-time/Full-time: Full-time
Number of Workdays Estimated: 75 days (From 23.09.2026 to 19.03.2027)
Consultant Level: Level 4

PROJECT BACKGROUND

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), through funding from the Climate Technology Accelerator Fund (CTAF), is implementing the project “AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay”. The project aims to strengthen climate resilience and renewable energy planning through the development and demonstration of an AI-enabled geospatial platform integrating satellite-derived renewable energy resource mapping, climate risk analytics, and decision-support tools.

Paraguay's electricity sector remains highly dependent on hydropower, which increases vulnerability to climate-induced droughts and hydrological variability. At the same time, the country has significant untapped solar and wind energy potential, particularly in the Chaco region. However, the lack of high-resolution geospatial information limits evidence-based planning and investment decision-making. The project will address this gap by generating solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability datasets and demonstrating an interoperable geospatial platform to support government institutions, academia, and other stakeholders in advancing the country’s renewable energy matrix diversification.

Key Objectives Include

Develop and validate high-resolution renewable energy and climate risk maps.
Support the deployment of a prototype web-based geospatial platform.
Strengthen institutional and technical capacity in the use of geospatial tools for climate and energy planning.
Support stakeholder engagement, validation, and scale-up planning.
Generate evidence for future replication and investment opportunities in Paraguay and the wider Gran Chaco region.

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The Geographic Information System (GIS) and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will provide technical support for the collection, processing, analysis, validation, visualization and reporting of geospatial data required for the implementation of the CTAF project.

The key tasks of this consultant position are as follows:

Collect, organize, and assess spatial datasets from government institutions and public sources.
Conduct GIS processing and spatial analysis using appropriate software and methodologies.
Develop and validate renewable energy resource mapping products, including geospatial analyses to support renewable energy planning and investment decision-making. Generate, analyze, and validate climate-risk layers, including drought and flood-related information, and develop decision-support products for national stakeholders. Prepare geospatial databases, metadata, and cartographic products.
Support testing and validation of spatial data integrated into the project platform.
Participate in stakeholder consultations, deliver training sessions, and technical meetings.
Contribute to the preparation of reports, presentations, and technical documentation.
Provide recommendations for data management, interoperability, and future scale-up of the platform.
Liaise with relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment of information generated and interoperability with the systems in place.
Serve as the national geospatial specialist and coordinate technical aspects with the consulting firm responsible for system deployment, ensuring the quality, consistency, and integration of geospatial datasets and analytical outputs.
Provide technical review and quality assurance of datasets, platform components, metadata, and interoperability mechanisms delivered by the consulting firm responsible for developing the platform.
Support validation of platform integration requirements and future interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM.

SCOPE OF WORK

The GIS and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will be part of the project implementation team and will work under the direct supervision of the CTAF Project Manager at GGGI Paraguay and in close coordination with national counterparts.

The consultancy is expected to deliver the following key results:

Geospatial Data Assessment and Coordination Report: Compile, review, organize and assess national geospatial datasets availability, quality, accessibility, and suitability related to renewable energy resources, climate risks, topography, infrastructure, and environmental information. Develop metadata catalogue and geospatial database inventory. Identify technical requirements and recommendations to facilitate interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM, and coordinate with consulting firm.
Technical Review and Validation of Climate and Renewable Energy GIS Dataset Package: Review and validate generation, processing, integration, quality control, accuracy, and validation of solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability layers. Support quality assurance and consistency checks of geospatial datasets developed under the project. Prepare technical documentation and metadata.
GIS Platform Support and Validation Report: Support data preparation, testing, visualization, validation, and demonstration of geospatial layers within the prototype web-GIS platform. Assess compliance with national data management requirements and interoperability standards. Review repository structures, metadata management procedures, and data-sharing mechanisms. Document validation results and recommendations for SIAM Integration.
Capacity Building and Final Technical Report: Deliver technical support for workshops and stakeholder consultations. Participate in technology-transfer activities conducted by the consulting firm. Support knowledge transfer and institutional capacity-building activities with designated MADES personnel. Review training materials, user guidance documents, lessons learned, and final consultancy report summarizing all activities undertaken during the consultancy.
The Consultant must integrate the comments of GGGI, and the technical focal points of other institutions involved, within 5 days after receiving the comments or requests for revision of the deliverables. All reports will be produced in Spanish and English and will follow GGGI's format requirements and will be submitted along with full raw data sets, research materials, minutes, interviews, and participant listings. Executive summaries will be delivered in English, and the final consolidated product of the consultancy must include a full English translation.

REPORTING ARRENGEMENTS

During the first week of assignment the consultant will define the reporting arrangements of the consultancy, in consultation with the national counterpart and the Project Manager. The consultant shall provide his/her own computer equipment and maintain access to ArcGIS Pro and any other software required to successfully perform the assignment.

Payments will be made against delivery of the products with prior approval from MADES, and approval from the GGGI Project Manager.

The consultant is expected to work in close coordination with MADES and other relevant institutions and may be required to work from MADES offices or other locations designated by the Project Manager.

Qualifications/Experience/Knowledge

Academic Qualifications

Master's degree in Geography, Geomatics, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Environmental Sciences, Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a related field; or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

Professional Experience

Minimum 5-8 years of professional experience (preferred 7) in GIS, spatial analysis, or geospatial data management.
Demonstrated participation in at least 5 projects involving geospatial analysis and mapping, preferably related to natural resources management, environmental monitoring, climate change, land use planning, energy, or infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience in at least 3 projects involving integration, management, or development of geospatial databases and metadata systems, remote sensing, Earth observation, or satellite imagery processing.
Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects involving climate risk analysis, environmental assessment, disaster risk management, or related fields.
Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects implemented with government institutions, international organizations, development partners, or public-sector entities.
Demonstrated experience in geospatial database management, metadata development, and spatial data governance, preparing technical maps, reports, and geospatial products for decision-making.
Experience working in Paraguay or in the Latin America and Caribbean region.

The Following Will Be Considered Assets

Experience in renewable energy resource assessment, solar and/or wind potential mapping, renewable energy suitability analysis, or GIS-based energy planning.
Experience in web-GIS platforms, spatial data portals, online dashboards, or geospatial visualization tools.
Experience delivering capacity-building, technical training, or knowledge-transfer activities related to GIS and remote sensing.
Experience using Google Earth Engine (GEE), Python, or other tools for geospatial analysis and remote sensing applications.

Skills and Knowledge

Strong analytical and cartographic skills.
Knowledge of spatial data management and metadata standards.
Demonstrated proficiency in ArcGIS Pro for geospatial analysis, geodatabase management, metadata development, and cartographic production.
Ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Strong report writing and presentation skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken, is a mandatory requirement, as the consultant will be required to conduct meetings, prepare deliverables, and communicate with international stakeholders in English.

About The Company

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.

In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.

Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.

Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.

Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.

Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.

Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.

The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.

Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. jobs.title: Environmental Professional, Biologist and Wetland Specialist
jobs.description:
Wilson & Company, Inc., Engineers & Architects, a national multi-disciplined engineering and architecture consulting firm, is currently seeking a full-time Environmental Professional – Biologist and Wetland Specialist to join our Rocky Mountain Region team in one of our offices in Utah or Colorado. You’ll join our growing team of environmental professionals from across the company to perform biological surveys, wetland delineations, draft reports and site forms, conduct environmental analyses, and deliver quality documents supporting our federal, state, local, and tribal clients under the Clean Water Act (CWA), the Endangered Species Act (ESA), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and other applicable federal and state regulations for environmental resource management.

In this position, you will perform fieldwork, evaluate potential environmental impacts and mitigation requirements, and write technical reports for wetland and biological resources on a variety of transportation, railroad, land development, and stormwater/wastewater projects. Biological resources include, but are not limited to, wetland delineation and mitigation, threatened and endangered species, wildlife, vegetation, noxious weeds, and environmental permitting. Aside from biological resources, we will also have you assist in compliance with NEPA and other environmental laws. Strong writing skills are required and experience with GIS is preferred. For the right candidate, this position has the potential to provide rapid growth.

All Wilson & Company environmental staff work collaboratively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across the firm to meet project goals, and with other key staff to build relationships both locally and in all states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work. Strong communication skills are required.

Essential Job Functions

Serve as project and/or task manager for environmental/NEPA projects in Rocky Mountain Region and firmwide; coordinate with and support others for overall project performance and deliver projects to clients on schedule and on budget.
Support the national environmental program through marketing, proposal preparation, and environmental analysis and documentation.
Work collaboratively and communicate effectively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across Wilson & Company to meet project goals, and other key staff to build client relationships in the states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work.
Provide technical environmental resource expertise for wetland and biological resources
Conduct fieldwork as it relates to project needs, includes travel throughout Colorado, Utah, and out-of-state travel to support a national environmental program.
Prepare biological resource reports, including Technical Memos, Biological Assessments, and Biological Evaluations.
Consult with jurisdictional and regulatory agencies and other stakeholders, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, etc.
Collaborate on the preparation of environmental and NEPA documentation, in part or in whole, including resource-specific technical reports, EIDs, CEs, EAs, and EISs.
Plan and conduct field delineations of Waters of the U.S., including wetlands, and conduct stream assessments.
Prepare delineation reports, functional assessments, mitigation plans, and Jurisdictional Determinations (JD) requests.
Prepare permit applications under Sections 404/401 of the Clean Water Act and NPDES Section 402.
Coordinate with state, federal, and local regulatory agencies.
Conduct vegetation and species habitat surveys.
Complete database reviews and background research to support NEPA documents and prepare NEPA documentation.
Prepare Section 7 consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Landscape Architecture, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Planning, or a related discipline; advanced degrees preferred
Experience managing environmental projects and supporting NEPA compliance efforts, including technical writing and preparation of environmental documentation, is preferred.
2+ years of experience conducting wetland delineations, threatened and endangered (T&E) species assessments, permitting, reporting, and mitigation planning utilizing the Arid West, Western Mountain, Great Plains, and/or Midwest Regional Supplements. Candidates with 5+ years of experience are strongly preferred.
Experience preparing wetland delineation reports, T&E assessment reports, Section 404 permit applications, and mitigation plans.
Strong field skills in wetland delineation and T&E assessments, including GPS data collection and ArcGIS/GIS applications.
Ability to identify wetlands, jurisdictional waters of the U.S., and associated soils, vegetation communities, wildlife species, and habitats common to the Intermountain West, Colorado, Utah, and Midwest regions.
Experience coordinating with federal, state, local, tribal, and regulatory agencies; Colorado permitting experience and familiarity with CDOT projects is preferred.
Professional certification as a Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT), Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), or the ability to qualify for PWS certification is preferred.
Proven ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams, manage tasks and budgets, and deliver work on schedule.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ArcGIS.

$52,000 - $90,000

Position Summary

The Drone Pilot / Surveyor is responsible for performing aerial data collection, mapping, surveying support, and construction documentation across utility-scale solar EPC projects. This position utilizes Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), survey equipment, and specialized mapping software to collect accurate field data used to support engineering, estimating, construction, project controls, and site management.

Working within a fast-paced, self-perform EPC construction environment, the Drone Pilot / Surveyor will support projects throughout the construction lifecycle—from existing-condition and preconstruction surveys through earthwork, pile installation, electrical construction, progress tracking, quantity verification, and final project documentation.

The ideal candidate combines strong UAS flight capabilities with practical surveying and construction knowledge and understands how accurate, timely field data directly impacts the successful execution of large-scale solar projects.

Key Responsibilities

Plan and conduct UAS/drone flight operations across large utility-scale solar construction sites in accordance with FAA regulations, company procedures, and project requirements.
Collect high-resolution aerial imagery and survey data for mapping, topographic surveys, construction progress, inspections, and project documentation.
Perform photogrammetry and aerial mapping to produce Ortho mosaics, digital terrain models (DTMs), digital surface models (DSMs), point clouds, and other project deliverables.
Support site surveying activities utilizing GPS/GNSS, RTK, robotic total stations, and other survey equipment as required.
Establish, verify, and maintain survey control throughout the duration of construction.
Support construction layout and verification activities for roads, grading, drainage, equipment pads, pile locations, electrical infrastructure, substations, and other project components.
Perform existing-condition and preconstruction aerial surveys to document site conditions prior to mobilization and construction.
Conduct routine progress flights to document construction status and provide project teams with current aerial imagery.
Assist with earthwork quantity calculations, stockpile measurements, cut/fill analysis, and verification of completed work.
Support grading operations by providing accurate surface data and comparing existing conditions against design surfaces.
Provide survey and aerial data to support pile installation, tracker/racking construction, module installation, underground electrical systems, inverter/transformer locations, and other solar construction activities.
Compare collected field data against IFC drawings, design models, and project specifications to identify potential discrepancies.
Support quality control activities by documenting installed conditions and assisting with verification of completed construction.
Process and manage drone imagery and survey data using applicable photogrammetry, CAD, GIS, and mapping software.
Coordinate with Project Managers, Superintendents, Survey Managers, Engineers, Project Controls, and field personnel to determine survey and aerial data requirements.
Maintain accurate flight logs, survey records, field notes, control documentation, and project files.
Organize and maintain aerial imagery and survey data so information is readily accessible to project teams.
Identify potential site, design, or construction issues through review of aerial and survey data and communicate findings to project leadership.
Maintain UAS equipment, batteries, survey instruments, and associated technology in proper working condition.
Perform pre-flight inspections and evaluate weather, airspace, site conditions, and potential hazards prior to flight operations.
Ensure all UAS operations comply with FAA Part 107 requirements and applicable federal, state, local, client, and company requirements.
Coordinate flight activities with project safety and field leadership to ensure drone operations do not interfere with cranes, equipment, electrical work, or other construction activities.
Support multiple projects and travel between active construction sites based on project needs.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, GIS, or related technical discipline preferred.

Previous experience operating drones/UAS for surveying, mapping, engineering, or construction applications.
Working knowledge of surveying principles, coordinate systems, elevations, benchmarks, and construction layout.
Experience collecting and processing aerial imagery for photogrammetry and mapping applications.
Experience with GPS/GNSS and RTK survey equipment.
Ability to read and interpret civil plans, grading plans, site layouts, construction drawings, and specifications.
Understanding of survey control and the importance of horizontal and vertical accuracy in construction applications.
Strong computer and data-management skills.
Ability to work independently in large, active construction environments while coordinating effectively with field personnel.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and priorities across multiple projects.
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
Ability and willingness to travel extensively based on project requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience supporting utility-scale solar, renewable energy, heavy civil, power generation, or large-scale EPC construction projects.
Experience working for a self-perform EPC or heavy civil contractor.
Experience with DJI Enterprise, Trimble, Leica, Topcon, or similar professional UAS and survey equipment.
Experience with photogrammetry and mapping platforms such as Pix4D, DroneDeploy, Propeller, Trimble Business Center, or similar applications.
Working knowledge of AutoCAD, Civil 3D, GIS, or comparable design/mapping software.
Experience creating Ortho mosaics, point clouds, surface models, contour maps, and volumetric reports.
Experience performing cut/fill analysis and earthwork quantity verification.
Experience with Ground Control Points (GCPs), checkpoints, RTK/PPK workflows, and survey-grade drone mapping.
Familiarity with solar site grading, pile installation, tracker systems, access roads, drainage systems, underground electrical collection systems, substations, and related utility-scale solar construction.

Job Description

Welcome to the Oregon Department of Forestry

Our Mission
– To protect and promote resilient forests that benefit all Oregonians.

The Benefits Of Joining Our Team

Work/life balance, 11 paid holidays a year, flexible work schedules, competitive benefits packages and so much more. Great Benefits Package - watch this video here. You’ll be part of the ODF team that serves our fellow Oregonians relying on regulation and protection of both public and private forest land in our great state of Oregon! Click here .

This position will be located at and report to the Salem office daily. The position will require work in the office, or field, full-time during the first month of employment and may be eligible for a hybrid/remote work schedule with the ability to report to Salem when business or operational needs are dependent on onsite activities . Occasional travel may be required.

What We Are Looking For

This position is part of the Water Quality and Monitoring Unit in the Forest Resources Division in Salem. The purpose of this division is to encourage economically efficient forest practices that ensure the continuous growing and harvesting of forest tree species, consistent with the sound management of soil, air, water, fish and wildlife resources and to assure the continued benefits of these resources for future generations; and to provide technical and financial assistance to non-federal forest landowners to improve management on private forest lands. The benefits derived from this program affect all Oregonians.

The Compliance Monitoring Program within the Forest Resources Division is responsible for monitoring the implementation of forest practice rules and analyzing compliance rates. The program collects information that allows for improvement in landowner compliance with the forest practices rules through training and education. Therefore, the compliance monitoring program works closely with the ODF Training Program to deliver presentations and other forms of communication to targeted audiences including landowners, operators, and ODF field foresters. Withing the compliance monitoring program, a team of Monitoring Specialists plan, implement, and report out on monitoring studies annually.

The Monitoring Specialist Duties Include

Plan, conduct, analyze, and report on forest monitoring projects statewide.
Perform extensive fieldwork, with some overnight travel, to collect environmental and forest practice data.
Manage, organize, and analyze complex datasets and GIS data using using ArcGIS Pro.
Train, lead, and oversee seasonal staff and/or work teams performing data collection.
Develop, coordinate, and oversee work completed by contractors, as assigned.
Interpret monitoring results and provide recommendations or, further study needs, to the Monitoring Coordinator and program managers.
Apply technical knowledge of the Forest Practices Act, DEQ water quality standards, and state and federal regulatory requirements to support program objectives.
Provide support to the Protection from Fire Program during wildfire or other emergency incidents.

Two years of experience in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field, and
a bachelor's degree in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field.

OR

Three Additional Years Of Related (pertinent) Experience

OR

One year of experience in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field and
a master's degree in Forestry or a closely related natural resource field.

jobs.title: Senior Geospatial Project Manager
jobs.description:
Wilson & Company is looking for an experienced Geospatial Project Manager to lead delivery on LiDAR, photogrammetry, and GIS projects — both existing client accounts and new work you help bring in. This role is primarily about running projects well: managing scope, schedule, budget, and technical quality, and being the client's trusted point of contact throughout delivery. Alongside that, you'll spend a meaningful slice of your time — roughly a quarter — on business development: nurturing client relationships toward repeat work, supporting proposals, and helping win the next project for accounts you manage. You'll have solid technical grounding in geospatial production and an established production team to deliver alongside, so your focus stays on running the project and the client relationship rather than production mechanics.

What You'll Do

Lead project delivery from award through closeout on both existing accounts and newly won work: scope, schedule, budget, technical direction, and QC.
Serve as the primary client contact for assigned projects and accounts, managing expectations and communication throughout delivery.
Manage project financials: budgets, fee tracking, earned value, margin, and utilization, reporting status to leadership.
Coordinate with the existing LiDAR, photogrammetry, and GIS production team to staff and execute projects, providing technical direction and quality control.
Dedicate roughly a quarter of your time to business development: identifying opportunities on existing accounts, supporting proposal development, and helping pursue new work.
Build client relationships during delivery that lead to repeat business and expanded scopes.
Develop project schedules and resource plans, coordinating across production, survey, and CADD staff as needed.
Provide technical review and troubleshooting on LiDAR, imagery, and GIS deliverables to ensure they meet client specifications and industry standards.
Coordinate with other service lines (transportation, transmission, water/wastewater, environmental) to identify cross-selling opportunities on your accounts.
Mentor project staff assigned to your projects, supporting their technical and professional development.
Prepare and present project status updates, risk assessments, and change management communications to clients and leadership.

What You Bring

Solid technical background in LiDAR, photogrammetry, and GIS, with hands-on project delivery experience.
History of project development from early client interaction through proposal, award, and delivery.
Track record managing project and operational financial metrics (budgets, margins, utilization, forecasting).
Strong client management skills, with a track record of building trust, managing expectations, and sustaining long-term relationships.
Some business development experience — comfortable identifying opportunities and supporting proposals, even if BD hasn't been your primary role.
Self-starter who can operate independently while collaborating effectively across a matrixed team environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable presenting to clients and leadership.
Bachelor's degree in Geomatics, Geography, GIS, Surveying, Civil Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
Typically 7+ years of progressive experience in geospatial project delivery, with prior project management responsibility.
Professional licensure or certification (PLS, GISP, or equivalent) a plus.
Willingness to travel to client sites, project locations, and industry events as needed.

Why Wilson & Company

Wilson & Company is an employee-owned engineering and geospatial services firm with an established national presence across transportation, transmission, water/wastewater, environmental, planning, and architecture. Our geospatial practice carries long-standing anchor client relationships and a fully staffed LiDAR, photogrammetry, and GIS production team — so you're stepping into an established operation, not building one from scratch. We're also investing in automation and next-generation production capability to keep our teams at the leading edge of the industry.

To Apply

Submit your resume and a brief note on a project you're proud of — one where you managed the client relationship and technical delivery, and it led to more work. We review applications on a rolling basis.

Please note that Wilson & Company is not currently sponsoring applicants for work visas.

Annual Salary Range: $50 - $70 per hour depending on experience

About Us

For nearly a century, Wilson & Company, Inc., Engineers & Architects, has provided award-winning engineering, architecture, planning, environmental, surveying, geospatial, and construction management services. With employees across multiple offices in the Midwest, Southwest, Rocky Mountain, and Western regions in the United States, we bring people together to practice their craft, create value, and accomplish great things.

Guided by our purpose, we help clients move from concept to completion, transforming unused spaces into productive places, underutilized facilities into efficient ones, and rural or urban challenges into achievable solutions.

At Wilson & Company, we focus on your specific needs, delivering excellence with lasting Higher Relationships in mind. By employing our core values—discipline, intensity, collaboration, shared ownership, and solutions—we create genuine experiences and lasting connections for our clients, employees, and communities.

We support our employees’ success and well-being with a comprehensive benefits package, including options for health insurance, life insurance, disability coverage, paid time off, and retirement savings plans. We are proud to be an EEO employer and maintain a drug-free workplace, conducting pre-employment background checks.

Join us and be part of a culture committed to helping you achieve personal and professional success.

Duncan-Parnell is a leading provider of geospatial, positioning, unmanned, construction, and technology solutions throughout the Southeast. jobs.description:
Our Work Matters

At Kindeva we make products that save lives, ensuring better health and well-being for patients around the world.

The Impact You Will Make

This position is accountable for serving as EHS point of contact for SME for supporting operations at a pharmaceutical device manufacturing site.

This Includes

providing EHS expertise and inputs in support of bench-scale process development, maintenance and engineering, hazardous waste, incident investigation, JHA, and best safety practices at an operational pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.
serving as an EH&S liaison with operations during safety pre-start up, PPE, Safety Committee, and safety audits.
supporting implementation and continuous improvement efforts.
orchestrating relevant incident investigations, industrial hygiene assessments, training, and risk management.

Role Responsibilities

Analyze existing and potential new products, processes, equipment, facilities, and programs; develop and implement proactive EHS strategies to minimize injury, illness, property loss, impact on the environment, and business.
Identify and evaluate environmental, health and safety hazards as part of standard process, procedure, product, and operational review practices. Assess the probability and potential impact of identified risks, and develop and propose feasible, cost-effective EHS risk mitigation solutions. Provide timely consultation and active support as required for EHS issues relating to implementation of new business.
Develop, implement, and administer industrial hygiene programs to proactively identify, evaluate, and control workplace hazards.
Collaborate with key stakeholders to ensure understanding of their operational and product support needs, connect with EHS and sustainability requirements, align appropriate plans and execute actions to support the requirements.
Conduct appropriate environmental, health & safety assessments on operational activity, assess compliance with applicable governmental EHS regulations, policies, and guidelines, and recommend and support implementation of actions to reduce corporate vulnerability and assuring compliance and preventing business interruption.
Maintain a thorough understanding and working knowledge of existing and proposed changes in federal and state industrial hygiene, safety, and environmental regulations, which affect operations.
Participate in regulatory inspections and inquiries involving environmental, health and safety issues. Act as a EHS consultant/ technical expert during resolution of any proposed corrective actions.
Successfully complete training required to perform job assignments and seek out additional training opportunities to enhance skills and abilities for program compliance and improvements.

Bachelor Degree in a relevant discipline or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant work experience.
3+ years of progressive work experience and proven initiatives in occupational safety, environmental, and industrial hygiene in a pharmaceutical or CDMO environment.
Knowledge in current good manufacturing practices (cGMP)
Willing to continue EHS development as necessary, learn new skills and assist in creating a world-class environment.

jobs.description:
MANAGER (m/w/d) - Environmental, Health & Safety

Vollzeit / Unbefristet

In dieser Position übernehmen Sie eine zentrale Rolle bei der strategischen und operativen Weiterentwicklung von Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) sowie Health & Wellbeing im europäischen CSL Plasma Netzwerk. Sie stellen die Einhaltung relevanter gesetzlicher und regulatorischer Anforderungen sicher und unterstützen die Standorte bei der Umsetzung wirksamer Maßnahmen zur Prävention, Risikominimierung und kontinuierlichen Verbesserung. Gleichzeitig fördern Sie eine nachhaltige Gesundheits- und Sicherheitskultur, stärken Führungskräfte und Mitarbeitende und treiben die Integration von Gesundheit, Sicherheit und Nachhaltigkeit in die täglichen Arbeitsabläufe voran. Dabei arbeiten Sie eng mit internen und externen Stakeholdern sowie den lokalen EH&S-Verantwortlichen zusammen und leisten einen wesentlichen Beitrag zu einem sicheren, gesunden und nachhaltigen Arbeitsumfeld.

Diese Aufgaben Erwarten Dich

Leitung von EH&S Plasma Europa:

Unterstützung bei der Umsetzung der globalen und regionalen EH&S-Strategien und -Programme von CSL Plasma sowie Sicherstellung der Ausrichtung an den übergeordneten CSL EH&S-Zielen.
Identifikation und Bewertung wesentlicher EH&S-Risiken, Entwicklung geeigneter Maßnahmen zur Risikominderung sowie proaktive Prävention von Gesundheits- und Sicherheitsvorfällen und Minimierung von Umweltauswirkungen.
Beratung und Befähigung von Führungskräften und Teams zur Stärkung des Sicherheitsverständnisses und zur Verankerung von Sicherheit und Gesundheit als gemeinsame Führungsaufgabe.
Förderung einer nachhaltigen EH&S-Kultur mit Fokus auf Gesundheit, Prävention und Wellbeing sowie auf die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung der Sicherheitskultur.
Förderung der funktionsübergreifenden Zusammenarbeit und Kommunikation sowie transparente Berichterstattung zu EH&S-Risiken, Strategien und Leistungen an die Geschäftsleitung.

Bereitstellung Von EH&S-Fachwissen Für CSL Plasma

Sicherstellung der EH&S-Compliance und regulatorischen Anforderungen, einschließlich gesetzlicher und behördlicher Berichte, Genehmigungen sowie Unterstützung im Austausch mit staatlichen und nichtstaatlichen Behörden und weiteren Stakeholdern.
Technische EH&S-Beratung und -Prüfung bei Anlagen, Prozessen, Arbeitsverfahren, Arbeitsmitteln und neuen Projekten sowie regelmäßige Begehung und Bewertung von Arbeitsstätten, Arbeitsbedingungen und Ergonomie.
Unterstützung der Standorte und Führungskräfte bei der Integration von Gesundheit, Sicherheit und Nachhaltigkeit in den Arbeitsalltag sowie bei der Standardisierung und kontinuierlichen Verbesserung des EH&S-Systems.
Begleitung von Veränderungen und Verbesserungsinitiativen, z. B. bei neuen Anlagen, Testprojekten, Prozessoptimierungen und Kaizen-Aktivitäten, einschließlich der Bewertung von Standorten und der Umsetzung erforderlicher Maßnahmen.
Verantwortung für besondere EH&S-Themen und Ereignisse, einschließlich Krisen- und Notfallmanagement, Arbeitsunfällen und Berufserkrankungen sowie Umwelt- und Wellbeing-Themen.

Health & Wellbeing Management

Verantwortung für die Weiterentwicklung und Umsetzung eines ganzheitlichen Gesundheits- und Wellbeing-Managements im europäischen CSL Plasma Netzwerk unter Berücksichtigung globaler Vorgaben und lokaler gesetzlicher Anforderungen.
Entwicklung, Steuerung und Erfolgskontrolle von Gesundheitsprogrammen in den Bereichen Prävention, Ergonomie, Mental Health, Resilienz und Wellbeing sowie Analyse relevanter Gesundheitskennzahlen und Ableitung von Verbesserungsmaßnahmen.
Förderung einer nachhaltigen Gesundheitskultur durch Sensibilisierung, Kommunikation und Beratung von Führungskräften und Mitarbeitenden mit dem Ziel, Gesundheit, Wohlbefinden, Leistungsfähigkeit und Anwesenheit zu stärken.
Koordination und Zusammenarbeit mit internen und externen Stakeholdern wie Betriebsärzten, Gesundheitsdienstleistern, Krankenkassen, Behörden sowie dem Wellbeing-Champion-Netzwerk zur Umsetzung wirkungsvoller Gesundheitsinitiativen.
Unterstützung globaler Health- und Wellbeing-Initiativen sowie Sicherstellung der lokalen Umsetzung und Integration in bestehende EH&S-Prozesse in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Health & Wellbeing Management Lead Marburg.

Menschen Und Teams

Unterstützung bei Rekrutierung, Bindung, Schulung und Entwicklung der Mitarbeitenden sowie Förderung eines Umfelds, in dem Teams und Einzelpersonen ihre Potenziale entfalten und sich kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln können.
Förderung von Mitarbeiterengagement und Eigenverantwortung durch eine Kultur der effizienten Umsetzung, kontinuierlichen Verbesserung und aktiven Beteiligung an Gesundheits-, Sicherheits- und Nachhaltigkeitsthemen.
Stärkung einer offenen und inklusiven Sicherheits- und Gesundheitskultur, in der Risiken transparent angesprochen und Verbesserungspotenziale gemeinsam identifiziert und umgesetzt werden.

Umwelt- Und EHS-Management

Sicherstellung der Einhaltung aller relevanten Umwelt-, Gesundheits- und Sicherheitsvorschriften an den europäischen CSL Plasma-Standorten sowie Überwachung der Umsetzung durch die lokalen Verantwortlichen.
Steuerung und Weiterentwicklung zuverlässiger EH&S-Prozesse und -Systeme zur kontinuierlichen Verbesserung der EH&S-Performance sowie der Mitarbeiter- und Spendererfahrung.
Verantwortung für Umweltgenehmigungen und behördliche Berichterstattung, einschließlich Überwachung von Fristen, Verlängerungen und standortspezifischen Anforderungen.
Koordination mit den lokalen EH&S-Verantwortlichen zur Sicherstellung der kontinuierlichen Einhaltung aktueller Umwelt- und Sicherheitsregularien.
Steuerung und Überwachung von EH&S-Projekten im Rahmen von Investitions- und Kapitalprojekten.

jobs.description:
About The Role

The GIS Analyst is responsible for the development, maintenance, and quality control of geospatial data and mapping products in support of high-voltage transmission line and right-of-way (ROW) construction projects. This role serves as a core contributor across project lifecycle phases – from preconstruction survey coordination through as-built deliverable production.

Company Overview

Established in 1891, The L.E. Myers Co. (L.E. Myers) – the oldest MYR Group Inc. subsidiary – is recognized as a premier electrical contractor of large utility construction projects across the nation. We are proud to offer our employees the opportunity to complete training, projects, and collaborative learning alongside our family of subsidiaries. We offer stability, with long-term clients and continuous expansion, which allows our tenured employees and new team members space to grow.

At L.E. Myers, we provide structured and strategic occupational growth opportunities for our valued staff. Comprised of long- and short-tenured employees, we are interactive amongst our growing family of subsidiaries, which allows employees to participate in clean energy projects, as well as complete our long-time transmission and distribution projects

Essential Functions

Geospatial Data Management & Mapping
Develop and maintain GIS maps and databases for transmission line construction projects, including structure locations, ROW boundaries, access routes, environmental constraints, and project layers in ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online; continuously update and manage data to support field operations and ensure teams have access to current, reliable information
Produce high-quality maps, exhibits, and spatial deliverables for internal and external project teams
Perform spatial analysis including buffer analysis, route comparisons, conflict identification, and land ownership overlays
Manage and QA/QC geospatial data from multiple sources including survey, LiDAR, aerial imagery, and CAD conversion

Transmission Line & ROW Support
Support permitting teams with accurate construction-specific mapping designs
Coordinate with survey and engineering teams to integrate field data into GIS deliverables and ensure alignment with project design drawings
Update GIS records to reflect field changes and design revisions throughout construction.
Assist with as-built documentation and final record mapping for transmission line projects

Field & Cross-Functional Coordination
Maintain internal GIS users, including onboarding new users, managing permissions, and coordinating ArcGIS Online (AGO) map sharing to ensure appropriate access, data security, and consistent use across project teams
Utilize ArcGIS Field Maps for data collection, field verification, and real-time updates during active construction
Collaborate with Project Managers, ROW agents, Environmental staff, and Survey crews to ensure GIS deliverables meet project milestones
Communicate with client GIS teams to align data standards, projections, and file format requirements

Essential functions of this position are to be performed in a Company-designated office or field location
Regular and predictable attendance
Other duties as assigned
Understand and comply with the Company's Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and other industry-specific professional and ethical conduct standards

ABOUT YOU

Qualifications

Minimum of 3 years of GIS experience with a focus on utility, transmission, or linear infrastructure projects
Experience with coordinate systems, projections, and datum transformations
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:
Experience working for an EPC contractor, transmission contractor, or utility in a GIS capacity
Familiarity with ArcGIS Online, and/or ArcGIS Field Maps for field data collection
GISP certification or ESRI Technical Certification
CAD experience (AutoCAD Civil 3D or MicroStation) for cross-functional data exchange

Preferred Education

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Geomatics, Civil Engineering Technology, or a related field; combination of relevant education and experience considered in lieu of degree

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Proficiency in ArcGIS Pro and/or ArcGIS Online (Esri platform)
Proficiency with geodatabases, feature classes, and geoprocessing tools
Working knowledge of transmission line construction processes, ROW fundamentals, and land ownership data
Ability to read and interpret survey plats, legal descriptions, construction drawings, and one-line diagrams
Strong attention to data accuracy and QA/QC discipline
Knowledge of NERC/FERC transmission standards, NESC structure classifications, or utility asset management frameworks is preferred
Proficiency in MS Office Suite
Strong communication skills, verbal and written
Ability to travel 25%

Salary

jobs.title: Analyst, Geospatial (GIS)
jobs.description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

Position Overview

Invenergy is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Geospatial Analyst
to join our collaborative Engineering & GIS team. This entry-level role is perfect for individuals eager to grow their technical skills while learning how geospatial data drives decisions across energy project lifecycles.

As a Geospatial Analyst, you will gain valuable experience supporting projects that power homes and businesses. You will learn not only technical GIS workflows but also how those workflows fit into the broader development process—giving you insight into multiple aspects of the energy business. This role is an excellent foundation for advancing into a specialist, developer, or project-focused roles while making a meaningful impact as you learn how energy infrastructure projects are built.

As a Geospatial Analyst, you will be part of a team that supports multiple departments—Development, Engineering, Environmental, and Land—ensuring geospatial data and mapping are accurate, accessible, and useful. You’ll gain exposure to many aspects of the business process, from project siting and permitting to construction and operations.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborative Mapping & Data Support

Work closely with GIS Analysts and Developers to deliver high-quality maps, data, and interactive, online products.
Partner with Development and Engineering teams to meet project needs and deadlines.
Incorporate feedback from multiple stakeholders to refine deliverables.

Project & Workflow Support

Assist with map requests, spatial data integration, and basic analyses.
Support project intake by organizing surveys, parcels, and environmental datasets.
Learn how geospatial workflows contribute to siting, land acquisition, permitting, and design.

Data Management & Learning

Maintain centralized GIS databases with attention to standards and version control.
Learn project geospatial data needs and support holistic data management for project data.
Follow established practices for metadata and file management.
Learn automation and efficiency practices to streamline repetitive tasks.

Team Contribution & Growth

Participate actively in team meetings, knowledge-sharing, and problem-solving sessions.
Build an understanding of how GIS connects across departments and contributes to business decisions.
Actively learn how the GIS team operates and contribute to ongoing improvements.
Take advantage of opportunities for skill development in GIS software, scripting, and renewable energy workflows.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or related field.
Proficiency with ESRI software (ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online / ArcGIS Enterprise).
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to communicate clearly and work as part of a team.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Preferred Qualifications

Internship or academic experience applying GIS in real-world projects.
Familiarity with renewable energy, environmental datasets, or land records.
Exposure to automation tools (Python, SQL) or interest in learning them.
Exposure to raster analysis and image interpretation and processing

Base Pay

$65,000.00 - 79,000.00 USD Annual

Bonus: 15%

The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills.

jobs.title: Environmental Data Management Technician – Mid Level (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
The Role – What You’ll Do

Barr is seeking an environmental data management technician to join our team. In this hybrid role, you will support the Assessment and Remediation business unit. The person in this position will work primarily in the environmental database EQuIS and heavily in Microsoft Excel. Assigned work tasks may include entering data into the EQuIS database; manually checking data thoroughly against original documents; entering geologic data and producing boring logs; producing charts and reports; performing advanced formulas and functions in Microsoft Excel; following processes set by the data management department; and discussing data and projects with other data management staff and project teams.

The ideal candidate for this position is a clear and confident communicator who thrives in both collaborative and independent work environments. They are adaptable, organized, and proactive, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills grounded in scientific reasoning and technical expertise. They bring a high level of attention to detail and demonstrate accuracy and completeness in managing large environmental datasets using tools like EQuIS and Microsoft Excel. For more experienced candidates, leadership, mentoring, and the ability to build strong client relationships are also important. Above all, they value teamwork, quality, and integrity in delivering impactful environmental solutions.

Your Impact – Key Responsibilities

Technical knowledge: apply scientific and environmental knowledge to manage, validate, and analyze large datasets using EQuIS and Microsoft Excel. Use advanced Excel tools such as pivot tables, macros, and formulas to support data-driven environmental projects with precision and consistency.
Project support: contribute to the success of environmental projects by supporting data workflows, coordinating with technical teams, and helping ensure that data deliverables meet project timelines, quality standards, and client requirements. Develop scopes of work, budgets, and timelines according to client specifications and needs.
Problem solving: apply deductive reasoning and scientific thinking to identify data discrepancies, assess data quality, and assist in the resolution of technical issues in environmental datasets. Interpret site data within regulatory and environmental frameworks while contributing to accurate, complete, and meaningful data deliverables.
Communication: prepare clear and concise data summaries, charts, boring logs, and figures for internal use and project documentation. Provide concise status updates to project managers and stakeholders.
Interpersonal savvy: work effectively with various stakeholders to ensure data quality and project success. Show a proactive and professional attitude while learning technical systems and growing within a supportive team environment. 

About The Opportunity

Compensation: anticipated range of $28.90–$36.70 per hour. Compensation will vary based on relevant experience, education, skill level, and other compensable factors. Employees in this position may also be eligible for a discretionary cash bonus based on team and individual performance. This position is classified as non-exempt (hourly) under the Fair Labor Standards Act.
Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position can be based out of Barr's Minneapolis or Duluth, Minnesota, offices.

About You – Required Core Competencies

Education: bachelor’s degree in environmental studies/sciences, geology, chemistry, biology, or a related field.
Experience: 3+ years of professional experience working with databases and advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience with charts, macros, pivot tables and other functions.
Software: strong computer skills, including experience with EQuIS and Microsoft Suite.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future.

Helpful Additional Experience (not Required)

Software: knowledge and experience with the following applications: Access, Python, R, and/or Power BI.
Knowledge of chemistry and/or geology.
Knowledge of state and federal environmental regulations.

Benefits - What We Offer

We are committed to providing an employee experience that attracts and retains top talent. That's why we offer a competitive package of employee benefits - including some unique offerings not found at other companies. At Barr, we also believe that learning doesn't stop when you get your degree, which is why we provide coaching, mentoring, and support for ongoing educational opportunities to foster professional development at every stage of your career.

Competitive, affordable insurance plans: Medical, dental, vision, life, disability, accidental death insurance, and flexible spending accounts for medical and dependent care
Retirement benefits: 401(k) retirement savings plan with company contribution and an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) with company contribution in Barr stock
Profit distribution: Barr has a "no retained earnings" model and distributes all profit to our employees through our annual bonus distribution plan, ESOP, and dividends to shareholders
Professional development benefits: Annual time and expense allowances, mentorship program, and many internal training opportunities
Work/life balance: Paid time off, holidays, overtime for non-exempt/hourly staff, and compensatory time for exempt/salaried staff (time off or pay for extra time worked), paid family leave
Wellness focus: Ergonomic analysis and equipment, Personal Protective Equipment allowance, wellbeing-focused educational opportunities

Please note that benefits eligibility is determined and may change based on part-time, reduced-time, or full-time status.

About Us - Why Choose Barr

At Barr, you'll join a community of engineers, scientists, and professionals who will help you achieve your ambitions and build a meaningful, rewarding career. You'll serve as a trusted advisor to clients who value Barr's tailored solutions and commitment to exceptional service.

As part of our employee-owned firm, you'll contribute to a culture of commitment and camaraderie where staff can thrive as professionals. We value diverse perspectives and experiences and believe an inclusive workplace is critical to our success.

AECOM
 has an exciting opportunity for a Mid-level Environmental Planner - Transmission focus
to join our Environmental Planning and Permitting (EPP) team in the Midwest region. AECOM's EPP team serves numerous private industry and public utility energy clients, on a variety of energy projects including transmission, grid modernization, and renewable energy developments. In this role you will lead or support project teams and work with our environmental planning practitioners and technical subject matter experts to prepare environmental documents, with a particular focus on supporting permitting and entitlement work for our growing line of work with energy developers and utilities. Projects range from regional transmission programs and grid modernization efforts to large-scale renewable energy developments and complex, multi-jurisdictional permitting efforts.

This role would involve serving as a seller-doer, responsible for developing and maintaining client relationships, leading pursuits and project teams, and expanding AECOM's energy permitting and environmental planning portfolio across the Midwest and supporting strategic growth initiatives throughout the U.S.

The responsibilities of this role would include, but are not limited to:

Lead or support environmental planning and compliance efforts for energy infrastructure projects, and coordination and filings with state utility regulatory agencies and public service commissions to support transmission siting, routing, permitting, and certificate approval processes across Midwest jurisdictions, especially within MISO, PJM, and SPP regions. Will include preparation of technical studies and NEPA documentation.

Provide project management on small to mid-sized projects, and support large-sized projects, including developing and tracking project schedules, budgets, invoicing, and coordination with clients, technical staff and subconsultants.
Work on environmental documents and entitlements related to high-profile infrastructure projects, with particular emphasis on energy sector projects.
Support projects across the Midwest and other U.S. markets by leveraging AECOM's national technical and project delivery platform.
Contribute to marketing and business development, preparation of proposals, and formulating proposal cost estimates as a seller-doer.
Mentor and develop junior and mid-level staff by reviewing work products, providing technical guidance, and supporting career development.

Bachelor's degree in environmental planning, environmental science, geography, natural resources, engineering, or a related field.
4 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education in electric transmission and renewable energy (e.g., solar, wind, energy storage) through supporting the preparing state utility permitting applications, routing and siting analysis, critical issues analysis, land use entitlement applications and/or overseeing multi-disciplinary technical teams for resource technical studies and permitting.

Electric transmission and renewable energy (e.g., solar, wind, energy storage) experience through preparing or supporting state utility commissions documents, routing and siting analysis, critical issues analysis, land use entitlement applications and/or overseeing multi-disciplinary technical teams for resource technical studies and permitting, as well as NEPA documentation.

Project or deputy project management experience on environmental planning projects, including client interaction, schedule and budget controls, and invoicing.
Experience supporting client development, proposal preparation, and/or business development pursuits.
Experience in managing or supporting environmental planning or permitting projects, including scope, schedule, budget, and client communications.

Position Summary

The Environmental Engineer is responsible for managing environmental permitting, compliance, and project support for assigned asphalt and emulsions manufacturing facilities. This role serves as a key environmental resource to Operations and EHS teams, ensuring facilities comply with federal, state, and local regulations while supporting operational and capital projects across the company's national footprint.

This position works independently on routine matters and collaborates closely with plant leadership, corporate teams, and regulatory agencies to mitigate environmental risk and support business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance

Manage day-to-day environmental compliance for assigned facilities, including air, water, waste, and spill prevention programs.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulations such as:
Clean Air Act (Title V, minor source, NSR)
Clean Water Act (MSGP stormwater, wastewater, SPCC)
RCRA hazardous and non-hazardous waste requirements

Maintain compliance calendars, records, and reporting schedules.
Lead responses to internal audits, regulatory inspections, and agency inquiries.
Identify compliance risks and develop corrective and preventive actions in coordination with site teams.
Support environmental incident response, investigations, and reporting as needed.

Permitting

Lead preparation, submittal, and management of environmental permit applications, renewals, and modifications.
Evaluate operational and process changes for permitting impacts.
Coordinate technical data collection (emissions, throughput, equipment changes) to support permitting efforts.
Serve as a primary point of contact for routine regulatory agency communications related to permits.
Track permit conditions and ensure operating requirements are communicated clearly to facilities.

Projects & Continuous Improvement

Provide environmental support for capital projects, plant expansions, equipment installations, and process changes.
Conduct environmental reviews to identify permitting or compliance requirements early in project planning.
Support implementation of best practices and standardized environmental procedures across facilities.
Participate in environmental improvement initiatives, including emissions reduction, waste minimization, and operational efficiency projects.
Contribute to environmental data tracking and corporate reporting initiatives.

Collaboration & Leadership

Act as an environmental advisor to plant managers, operations, and maintenance teams.
Partner with Corporate EHS and Engineering on environmental strategy and risk management.
Mentor Environmental Engineer I staff and support training and knowledge transfer.
Communicate regulatory requirements clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field.

Experience

3–6 years of environmental engineering or compliance experience in manufacturing or industrial settings.
Experience supporting multiple facilities or a geographically dispersed footprint is preferred.

Knowledge & Skills

Strong working knowledge of environmental regulations affecting asphalt, chemical manufacturing, or heavy industry.
Experience with air permitting and/or water and waste compliance strongly preferred.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
Ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical operational guidance.

Travel

Ability to travel approximately 25–40%, depending on facility needs and project scope.

Preferred Qualifications

Engineer‑in‑Training (EIT) or Professional Engineer (PE) license.
Experience working directly with regulatory agencies.
Familiarity with asphalt plants, emulsions, terminals, or related materials manufacturing.
Experience supporting environmental aspects of capital projects or acquisitions.
