jobs.title: Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialist (Environmental Specialist 4)(Two Positions)
jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring two Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialists (Environmental Specialist 4)(Two Positions)
within the Shorelands & Environmental Assistance
(SEA) program.

Note:
This is a temporary position that will end on June 30, 2027. T here is potential to extend based on funding availability.

Location Options:

These positions can be based at any of the following duty stations:

Headquarters Office (HQ) in Lacey, WA .
Central Region Office (CRO) in Union Gap, WA .
Northwest Region Office (NWRO) in Shoreline, WA .

One position will be based in NWRO. The other position will be based in either in HQ or CRO. Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the selected duty station.

Note
: If the selected duty station is the Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, the salary will include an additional 5% premium pay due to its location in King County. Salary range: $6068-$8163 per month.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires reporting to the office one day every two weeks.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by September 15th, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

These Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialist positions provide an opportunity for two senior technical experts to advance Ecology’s mission to protect Washington’s shorelines, wetlands, and riparian areas. In these roles, you will assist with regional implementation of the Shoreline Master Program (SMP) audit and technical assistance effort, support the development of a proactive compliance program, and strengthen state–local partnerships that ensure shoreline development achieves no net loss of ecological functions. You will work directly with local governments to evaluate shoreline permits, assess compliance with SMP requirements, improve monitoring systems, and resolve unauthorized activities affecting priority shorelines and riparian environments.

You will serve as regional enforcement specialists, independently developing cases, conducting investigations, preparing formal enforcement documents, and representing Ecology in complex proceedings involving violations of the Shoreline Management Act. Through collaboration with the Shoreline Policy Lead, SMA Compliance Lead, regional counterparts, and the Attorney General’s Office, you will help implement an adaptive feedback loop that improves statewide consistency, reinforces local permitting systems, and strengthens environmental protections.

What You Will Do

Implement the regional SMP audit and technical assistance program, evaluating shoreline permits, monitoring reports, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection measures to ensure consistency with the SMA and local SMPs.
Provide targeted compliance support to local governments, helping develop monitoring processes, evaluation methods, and systematic approaches to track permit effectiveness and ecological performance.
Conduct field verification for priority shoreline projects, confirming as-built conditions, validating monitoring findings, documenting ecological outcomes, and providing follow-up direction to permittees and local partners.
Lead regional shoreline enforcement activities by identifying unauthorized activities, developing defensible case documentation, conducting site investigations, preparing notices of violation and administrative orders, and coordinating enforcement actions with the SEA Program Enforcement Coordinator and the Attorney General’s Office.
Represent Ecology as senior technical experts in enforcement hearings, settlement discussions, and legal proceedings involving complex shoreline violations and high-priority environmental resources.
Serve as project officers for compliance-related grants and agreements, negotiating work elements, tracking deliverables, and ensuring alignment with shoreline protection and SMP improvement goals.
Collaborate closely with regional shoreline planners, headquarters staff, local governments, and tribal, state, and federal partners to ensure consistent implementation of shoreline management requirements and improve overall SMP compliance statewide.
Contribute to development and refinement of statewide shoreline compliance tools, guidance, training, and best practices that support adaptive management and improve long-term ecological outcomes across Washington.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine (9) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of this position, which includes the following:

Shoreline and Environmental Permit Review: Ability to interpret and evaluate shoreline authorizations, permit conditions, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection requirements for consistency with the Shoreline Management Act (SMA) and local Shoreline Master Programs (SMPs).
Compliance Evaluation and Field Verification: Skill in assessing compliance with SMP provisions through document review and site inspections, including verifying as-built conditions, monitoring reports, and ecological performance standards.
Enforcement Case Development: Experience gathering defensible environmental data, documenting violations, preparing enforcement documents (e.g., notices of violation, administrative orders), and coordinating with enforcement leads and legal partners.
Grant and Agreement Administration: Ability to serve as a project officer—developing, negotiating, and monitoring grant or agreement terms, reviewing deliverables, and ensuring alignment with program objectives.
Intergovernmental Coordination: Skill in working effectively with local governments, state and federal partners, tribal entities, and internal regional staff to support consistent and effective implementation of shoreline compliance activities.
Clear and Professional Communication: Ability to communicate technical, regulatory, or enforcement-related information clearly in writing and verbally to varied audiences, including permittees, local partners, and legal representatives.

Education:
Involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Examples Of How To Qualify

9 years of experience.
8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree.

Desired Qualifications

Knowledge of regulatory programs and Ecology’s statutory authority under the SMA.
Knowledge of local government roles and responsibilities under the SMA.
Demonstrated understanding of environmental legislation and regulations at the federal, state, and local level.
Demonstrated understanding of complex environmental permitting processes.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

Application Attestation: By submitting an application, you are affirming that the information contained in your application and on all attachments is complete and truthful. The state may verify this information, and any false or misleading answers may result in rejection of your application or dismissal if employed.

Need an Accommodation?

If you need reasonable accommodation during the application and/or screening process, including this job announcement in an alternate format:

Please contact us at 360-407-6186 or careers@ecy.wa.gov
If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 711 or 1-800-833-6384.

Questions?

For specific questions about the position location options, schedule, or duties, please contact Chad Yunge at Chad.Yunge@ecy.wa.gov
If you need assistance applying for this job, are inquiring about the status of your application, would like to request the full position description, or have any other questions, please contact the Recruitment Team at careers@ecy.wa.gov

About

About the Shorelands and Environmental Assistance (SEA) Program

The mission of the SEA Program is to create community conservation partnerships to protect and restore our shorelands, wetlands, and floodplains.

About The Department Of Ecology

As the State of Washington’s environmental protection agency, we are deeply committed to protecting, preserving, and enhancing Washington’s environment for current and future generations. Joining Ecology means becoming part of a team dedicated to protecting and sustaining healthy land, air, water, and climate in harmony with a strong economy. A career in public service at Ecology allows you to help solve some of the most challenging problems facing our state, while keeping your health and financial security a priority. We combine one of the most competitive benefits packages in the nation with a strong commitment to life/work balance. We invest in our employees to create and sustain a working environment that encourages creative leadership, effective resource management, teamwork, professionalism, and accountability.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Ecology employees may be eligible for the following: Medical/Dental/Vision for employee & dependent(s) , Public Employees Retirement System (PERS) , Vacation, Sick, and other Leave *, 11 Paid Holidays per year *, Public Service Loan Forgiveness , Tuition Waiver , Long Term Disability & Life Insurance , Deferred Compensation Programs , Dependent Care Assistance Program (DCAP) , Flexible Spending Arrangement (FSA) , Employee Assistance Program , Commute Trip Reduction Incentive , Combined Fund Drive , SmartHealth * Click here for more information

Department Information

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado.

At The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE) we are dedicated to the Colorado for All philosophy - working toward a Colorado where everyone has the opportunity to succeed.

We support the basic human rights of our neighbors regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, education level, disability, socio-economic status, or any other visible or invisible identity. We are committed to increasing the diversity of our staff and providing culturally responsive programs and services. Therefore, we strongly encourage individuals from diverse backgrounds to apply.

Be BOLD.....Make a REAL difference . . .
join us in serving our communities advancing Colorado's health and protecting the places we live, work, learn, and play, to create a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations thrive.

Mission -
To advance Colorado's health and protect the places we live, work, learn, and play.

Vision -
To create a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations thrive.

CDPHE Offers

Free parking and access to RTD bus lines.
Flexible working arrangements
Retirement ( PERA options), Medical and dental health plans
Defined Benefit Plan or the PERA Defined Contribution Plan, plus optional 401K and 457 plans
Paid life insurance

11 paid holidays per year and generous personal time off

Career advancement opportunities throughout the State system

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program. For more information, go to: https://studentloans.gov/myDirectLoan/pslfFlow.action#!/pslf/launch

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Institutions Unit is under the direction of the Deputy Division Director and is responsible for assuring compliance with the requirements of the food laws and sanitation regulations of the State for assisted living residences, swimming pools, child care facilities, and schools. These duties are accomplished through inspections, recall coordination, outbreak investigations, compliance assistance, and compliance assurance; by reviewing registration information, plan review submissions, and other field-generated information for assisted living residences (for retail food regulation compliance), swimming pools, child care facilities, and schools within the State. The school and child care programs are delegated through contracts to Local Public Health Agencies (LPHA). LPHAs conduct inspections and day-to-day program functions at the local level. This unit provides direct service for schools and child care facilities in the absence of a local program. The Division performs program audits and inspection standardization exercises with the delegated LPHAs. The unit, in cooperation with LPHAs, is responsible for assuring compliance with the requirements of the institutional environmental health laws and regulations of the State. The Unit determines the appropriate response, which may include informal or formal inquiries, such as embargo, condemnation, seizure, injunctive relief, and recalls, requesting additional field investigations, recommending and subsequently researching and recommending administrative or judicial enforcement actions, and developing and negotiating assessments. The Unit is also responsible for drafting new regulations, completing State Board of Health documents, and coordinating stakeholder meetings.

What You Will Do

The purpose of this position is to serve as an environmental protection specialist within the school and childcare programs. This position conducts regulatory inspections; prepares inspection reports, compliance advisories, LPHA assessments, and orders or recommendations for enforcement. Additionally, this position serves as a trainer in school and childcare programs. The position conducts training and joint inspections for LPHA staff and develops guidance materials for the programs. In addition to direct facility inspection oversight, this position provides compliance assistance, guidance, and training to the regulated community and local public health agencies. This position is expected to be a junior-level inspector with the goal of being fully operational as a senior-level inspector. This position requires wide-ranging oversight from the supervisor.

Key Responsibilities

Writes technical reports, creates and maintains accurate records, and initiates appropriate enforcement actions such as follow-up inspections, voluntary condemnations, and voluntary closures as necessary when non-compliance is identified within school or childcare operations.
Works collaboratively with epidemiologists to investigate illness and outbreak investigations.
Through research of technical reports, governing regulations, statutory requirements, and other resource materials, creates and drafts responses to questions and inquiries presented by local public health agencies' staff, school administrators, childcare providers, and the public.
Actively monitors progress and reviews reports submitted by LPHAs for completeness and contract requirements.

Residency Requirement

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description

I3A2T* Environmental Protection Specialist I

Minimum Qualifications

Experience Only:

Five (5) years of professional experience working in a field related to the work assigned to the position, such as environmental health inspections or in an occupation directly related to the work assigned in this position.

Or

Education And Experience

A combination of related education from an accredited college or university in Biology, Environmental Science for a field of study closely related to the work assignment and One (1) year of experience in a field related to the work assigned to the position, such as environmental health inspections or in an occupation directly related to the work assigned in this position to equal five (5) years.

NOTE: An applicant may meet the minimum qualifications for this job in one of two ways: They may qualify through their work experience alone or through a combination of education and work experience.

**This experience must be substantiated within the Work Experience section of your application. "See Resume" will not be accepted. In addition, part-time work will be prorated.**

Preferred Qualifications

In addition to the minimum requirements, the successful candidate in this position will have the following highly desirable experience and competencies:

Experience conducting regulatory inspections in child care facilities, schools, retail food establishments or a related industry.
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders including state and local governments, non-profits, community groups, private regulated entities and federal agencies such as EPA.
Advanced Interpersonal and conflict management skills e.g. displays understanding, courtesy, tact, empathy and concern.
Develops and maintains effective relationships, deals skillfully with people who are difficult, hostile or distressed,effectively manages and resolves conflicts, confrontations and disagreements in a positive and constructive way. Computer literate.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Bilingual in Spanish and English preferred.
Ability to analyze facts, data and evidence to arrive at a logical conclusion.
Experience with investigating complaints and outbreak investigations that are received regarding regulated facilities.
Experience with assisting in developing classroom training materials to support learning needs of regulated communities, stakeholders and LPHA staff.
Ability to make recommendations on reporting improvements and / or program improvements based on submitted information.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT:
Must match approved PD

A pre-employment background check will be conducted as part of the selection process.
TRAVEL: Traveling 80% of the time, with up to 30% of that travel being overnights, required to accomplish job duties; it may also require out-of-state travel for training courses/meetings up to two times per year.
Operation of a fleet vehicle on a regular basis.

Appeal Rights

An applicant who has been removed from an employment list or removed from consideration during the selection process may request a review by the State Personnel Director.

As an applicant directly affected by the results of the selection or comparative analysis process, you may file a written appeal with the State Personnel Director.

Review of the completed, signed and submitted appeal will be timely on the basis of written material submitted by you, using the official appeal form signed by you or your representative. This form must be completed and delivered to the State Personnel Board by email at dpa_state.personnelboard@state.co.us within ten (10) calendar days from your receipt of notice or acknowledgment of the Department’s action.

For further information on the Board Rules, you can refer to 4 Colorado Code of Regulations (CCR) 801-1, State Personnel Board Rules and Personnel Director's

Administrative Procedures, Chapter 8, Resolution of Appeals and Disputes, at spb.colorado.gov/board-rules.

Supplemental Information

A Complete Application Packet Must Include

Completed State of Colorado application.
Cover Letter
If using education to qualify for this position a copy of your transcripts (unofficial acceptable) or diploma must be provided with application. Transcripts must be attached to your colorado.gov/jobs application.
If you are a veteran, a copy of your DD214 must be attached to your colorado.gov/jobs application.

The Selection Process:

All applications that are received by the closing of this announcement will be reviewed against the Minimum Qualifications in this announcement. Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications proceed to the next step.

Colorado Revised Statutes require that state employees are hired and promoted based on merit and fitness through a comparative analysis process.

Part of, or all of, the comparative analysis for this position may be a structured application review, which involves a review of the information you submit in your application materials by Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) against the preferred qualifications.

A top group, up to six candidates, will be invited to schedule an interview with the hiring manager.

E-Verify

CDPHE uses e-Verify, an Internet-based system, to confirm the eligibility of all newly hired employees to work in the United States. Learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities.

ADAAA Accommodations

The State of Colorado believes that equity, diversity, and inclusion drive our success, and we encourage candidates from all identities, backgrounds, and abilities to apply. The State of Colorado is an equal opportunity employer committed to building inclusive, innovative work environments with employees who reflect our communities and enthusiastically serve them. Therefore, in all aspects of the employment process, we provide employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, medical condition related to pregnancy, creed, ancestry, national origin, marital status, genetic information, or military status (with preference given to military veterans), or any other protected status in accordance with applicable law. jobs.title: Drone Pilot
jobs.description:
Role Description A Drone Pilot is responsible for operating, controlling, and maintaining unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to support aerial photography, surveying, inspection, monitoring, mapping, surveillance, or other approved operational activities. The role ensures safe and efficient drone operations in accordance with applicable aviation regulations, company procedures, operational requirements, and safety standards.
Key Responsibilities Operate drones and UAV systems safely and efficiently for assigned missions.
Conduct pre-flight, during-flight, and post-flight inspections of drones, payloads, batteries, controllers, and related equipment.
Plan and execute drone flight missions based on operational requirements and approved flight plans.
Monitor weather conditions, airspace restrictions, terrain, obstacles, and other potential flight hazards.
Operate drones using appropriate flight modes, navigation systems, cameras, sensors, and payloads.
Capture high-quality aerial photographs, videos, images, mapping data, or other required information.
Conduct aerial surveys, inspections, monitoring, mapping, and data-collection activities as assigned.
Maintain accurate flight logs, mission records, equipment records, and operational documentation.
Monitor drone systems, battery levels, GPS signals, communication links, and other critical flight parameters.
Identify and respond appropriately to equipment malfunctions, signal loss, weather changes, and other operational issues.
Perform basic troubleshooting and routine maintenance of drones and associated equipment.
Ensure batteries, propellers, sensors, cameras, controllers, and other equipment are properly maintained and stored.
Process, organize, and transfer captured aerial data in accordance with company procedures.
Coordinate with operations teams, technical staff, clients, surveyors, photographers, engineers, or other relevant personnel.

At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.

For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.

At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.

Bloom Energy
is the leading force in transforming the way energy is generated and delivered. We are driving toward the parallel goals of growing a dynamic and forward-thinking company while creating a positive impact on our environment. Our mission is to make clean, reliable energy affordable globally. Our company is filled with smart and innovative thinkers and doers, and we never stop striving to improve our technology, to expand and improve our company performance, and to develop and support the many talented employees that serve our mission!

We are looking for a Director/Senior Director, Environmental Law
to join our team in San Jose, California
in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This is a fully on-site, in office role
.

Reporting to the Vice President, Environmental and Regulatory Law,
this role will serve as a strategic legal advisor for environmental, land use, health and safety, sustainability, and regulatory matters that are critical to Bloom’s continued growth. The Director/Senior Director will provide practical, business-oriented counsel across project development, operations, manufacturing, service, policy, commercial, and compliance functions. This position will be expected to lead in complex and ambiguous regulatory environments, develop creative and compliant paths forward, manage outside counsel where appropriate, and interface with federal, state, and local agencies to advance Bloom projects and support scalable business execution. The ideal candidate will have deep environmental law experience, strong judgment, excellent leadership and communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally with business teams to solve complex problems.

Role and Responsibilities:

Provide strategic legal advice and practical business counseling on environmental, land use, health and safety, sustainability, and regulatory matters impacting Bloom’s operations, projects, products, and services.
Support project development strategy and execution, including environmental review, permitting, due diligence, entitlement, and dispute-resolution matters.
Advise internal stakeholders on compliance obligations under federal, state, local, and international environmental and related regulatory programs, including air, water, waste, hazardous materials, occupational safety, climate, and sustainability requirements.
Interface with and advocate before regulatory agencies, including environmental, energy, public utility, occupational safety, and local land use authorities, to advance company objectives and resolve compliance or permitting issues.
Partner closely with Sales, Finance, Engineering, Service, Operations, Quality, Policy, Commercial, and Legal teams to identify risk, develop practical mitigation strategies, and deliver compliant, workable business solutions.

Review, draft, and negotiate environmental, sustainability, compliance, and risk-allocation language in commercial agreements, customer contracts, project documents, real estate documents, and transaction materials.
Monitor and assess emerging environmental, climate, energy, ESG, and sustainability laws and regulations; translate developments into business risks, opportunities, and recommended actions for senior leadership.
Manage outside counsel and consultants efficiently, including developing matter strategy, budgets, workplans, and internal alignment.
Advise on corporate sustainability, environmental justice, ESG due diligence, climate strategy, disclosures, reporting, and customer-facing sustainability commitments.
Other duties as assigned.

Skills and Experience:

Juris Doctor from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing with at least one state bar; California bar admission preferred.
10+ years of relevant environmental, land use, regulatory, compliance, permitting, litigation, and/or project development experience; in-house experience preferred.
Deep knowledge of environmental and land use laws and regulatory programs, including CAA, CWA, RCRA, CERCLA, CEQA, NEPA, OSHA-related requirements, climate and air programs, hazardous materials, and state and local analogs.
Demonstrated experience counseling business teams in highly regulated operating environments, preferably involving manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, transportation, industrial facilities, service operations, or emerging technologies.
Experience interfacing with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies and developing successful permitting, compliance, enforcement-resolution, and advocacy strategies.
Ability to lead in ambiguity, exercise sound judgment, learn quickly, and design practical, compliant solutions in a dynamic and evolving regulatory environment.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to coordinate cross-functional teams, outside counsel, consultants, agency stakeholders, and business leaders to drive matters to resolution.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex legal and technical issues into clear business risks and recommendations for senior management.
Experience supporting sustainability, ESG, environmental justice, climate, corporate disclosure, and emerging environmental policy matters is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build credibility and effective working relationships across Legal, Operations, Service, Engineering, Sales, Finance, Policy, Quality, and executive leadership.

As a Geospatial Analyst with Stantec, you will provide technical support and applied GIS expertise for assigned projects, including mapping applications, spatial analysis, web mapping, data management, field data workflows, and map production. This full-time position supports our Mid-Atlantic Region Environmental Services group and offers opportunities to mentor junior staff, strengthen repeatable workflows, and contribute to consistent project delivery.

Compile, create, maintain, and QA/QC spatial and non-spatial data across Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and related project platforms, applying established data standards and recommending improvements when appropriate.

Develop and maintain web maps, dashboards, field data collection tools, and hosted data workflows using ArcGIS Online, Survey123, Field Maps, and related applications.
Support and help coordinate geospatial field data collection efforts, including preparation of mobile maps and forms, field data review, troubleshooting, and integration of field observations into project datasets.
Apply established cartographic standards and Quality Assurance / Quality Control processes while identifying opportunities to improve consistency, efficiency, and repeatability across common GIS deliverables.

Recognize when technical issues, data inconsistencies, or workflow risks are developing; initiate appropriate corrective actions and communicate options to project managers or senior technical staff.
Collaborate with GIS staff, environmental practitioners, project managers, and other disciplines across Stantec offices to support efficient delivery and shared technical standards.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
Organization

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)

Reference Code

EPA-OCSPP-2026-0008

How To Apply

To submit your application, scroll to the bottom of this opportunity and click APPLY.

A Complete Application Consists Of

All documents must be in English or include an official English translation.

Connect with ORISE...on the GO!
Download the new ORISE GO mobile app in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to help you stay engaged, connected, and informed during your ORISE experience and beyond!

Application Deadline

10/9/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time Zone

Description

Applications may be reviewed on a rolling-basis and this posting could close before the deadline.

EPA Office/Lab and Location:
A research opportunity is currently available at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Great Lakes Coastal Environmental Science Laboratory, located in Duluth, Minnesota.

The mission of EPA is to protect human health and the environment. EPA works to ensure that: Americans have clean air, land and water; national efforts to reduce environmental risks are based on the best available scientific information; federal laws protecting human health and the environment are administered and enforced fairly, effectively and as Congress intended; Environmental stewardship is integral to U.S. policies concerning natural resources, human health, economic growth, energy, transportation, agriculture, industry, and international trade, and these factors are similarly considered in establishing environmental policy; All parts of society have access to accurate information sufficient to effectively participate in managing human health and environmental risks; Contaminated lands and toxic sites are cleaned up; and chemicals in the marketplace are reviewed for safety.

Research Project:
The US EPA is mandated to address the endocrine disrupting potential of thousands of chemicals. For the majority of these chemicals there is a lack of information regarding whether they have the potential to cause adverse effects from impacts on thyroid hormone status. Understanding the important targets within the network of processes involved in maintaining normal functioning thyroid hormone levels, and what approaches to best assess activity at those targets are critical to developing a comprehensive approach to evaluating thyroid hormone disrupting potential of large numbers of chemicals.

Recently, a number of thyroid-related in vitro high-throughput screening (HTS) assays have been developed to broaden assay coverage for molecular targets potentially leading to thyroid disruption and were implemented to screen US EPA’s ToxCast Phase 1, 2 and E1K chemical libraries. This battery of thyroid-related in vitro HTS assays can be employed to rapidly assess potential interference with these targets. However, this screening approach leaves uncertainties regarding the meaning of in vitro activity data as it relates to in vivo adverse outcomes. Part of this research effort aims to develop a translational process that integrates relevant information, models, and data streams to provide richer context to interpret in vitro results related to thyroid disruption. As part of the translational process, this fellowship will focus on the development of a bio-assay to quantitative monitor thyroid hormone synthesis as a complimentary assay to existing in vitro thyroid-related assays. Assay development will be followed by the analysis of canonical and suspected thyroid disrupting chemicals to understand whether, or how, in vitro activity of chemicals translates to in vivo outcomes. Additionally, this research will employ existing computational tools such as the octanol-water partition coefficient (logKow) and quantitative structure-activity relationships (QSAR) models to provide deeper interpretation of in vitro data and further prioritize chemicals most likely to impact thyroid function in aquatic systems. The translational principles employed will have much broader applicability across ToxCast HTS assays and aquatic vertebrates.

With guidance from the mentor, you may be involved in any or all of the following training activities:

Learn how innovative in vitro to in vivo extrapolation and reverse toxicokinetic approaches are used to translate effect concentrations measured in laboratory assays to equivalent blood, tissue, or environmental media concentrations.
Help with designing workflows and applying data analysis pipelines that support automated and standardized analysis of large scientific data sets.
Gain experience contributing to the development and implementation of data archiving and storage systems for research data management.
Learn how statistical and performance-based measures are applied to assess assay and data quality through quality assurance and quality control practices.
Process and analyze large, high-content data sets using established and emerging computational analysis pipelines under mentor guidance.
Compile and synthesize scientific information from peer-reviewed literature and online data sources to support interpretation of test results within the Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) framework.
Apply statistical analysis approaches such as hypothesis testing, regression methods, multivariate statistics, and concordance analyses to support research objectives.
Develop familiarity with computational and quantitative methods used in toxicology, exposure science, and data-intensive research environments.
Build scientific communication skills through preparation and presentation of research findings at regional, national, and international conferences or workshops.
Contribute to the preparation of peer-reviewed publications and dissemination materials for research partners, collaborators, and stakeholders.
Gain professional development experience in interdisciplinary research, data analysis, scientific collaboration, and communication of complex scientific findings to diverse audiences.

Learning Objectives
: You will learn how to collaborate effectively within a transdisciplinary research team while gaining experience in project planning, scientific communication, research implementation, and data analysis activities. Through collaboration with researchers and staff, you will develop an understanding of how multidisciplinary scientific projects are designed, managed, and executed. You will also have opportunities to learn from and interact with internationally recognized scientific leaders within EPA and across external research organizations and institutions.

You will build knowledge of laboratory, analytical, and computational techniques that are broadly applicable across life sciences research fields. Through hands-on participation and mentorship, you will learn how to operate and use a variety of scientific instruments and equipment and gain familiarity with laboratory and research workflows. You will also learn approaches for evaluating data quality, troubleshooting research results, and applying statistical methods for scientific data analysis, interpretation, and communication. Opportunities may be available to contribute to original research efforts and support the development of scientific publications and related research products.

Mentor(s):
The mentor for this opportunity is Sigmund Degitz (degitz.sigmund@epa.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: Fall 2026.
All start dates are flexible and vary depending on numerous factors.

Appointment Length:
The appointment will initially be for one year and may be renewed three to four additional years upon EPA recommendation and subject to availability of funding.

Level of Participation:
The appointment is full time.

Participant Stipend:
The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience.

Citizenship Requirements:
This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) only.

EPA Security Clearance:
Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at EPA.

ORISE Information:
This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and EPA. Participants do not become employees of EPA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.

ORISE offers all ORISE EPA graduate students and Postdocs a free 5-year membership to the National Postdoctoral Association (NPA).

The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility.

Questions:
Please see the FAQ section of our website. If you have additional questions about the application process, please email ORISE.EPA.OCSPP@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.

Qualifications

The qualified candidate should have received a master's or bachelor's degree in one of the relevant fields (Computational Biology, Computational Toxicology, Mathematics, Biostatistics, Computer Science). Degree must have been received within the past five years.

Candidates with a bachelors may be considered if they can demonstrate strong experience.

Description

We are seeking an Applied Scientist to develop and optimize Visual Inertial Odometry (VIO) and sensor fusion systems for our intelligent robots. In this role, you will design, implement, and deploy state estimation and tracking algorithms that enable robots to understand their position and motion in real time, even in challenging and dynamic environments.

You will own the full pipeline from algorithm development through embedded deployment, ensuring that perception systems run efficiently on resource-constrained robotic hardware. You will also leverage modern machine learning approaches to push the boundaries of classical perception methods, combining learned representations with geometric techniques to achieve robust, real-time performance.

This is a deeply hands-on role. You will work directly with sensors, hardware, and real-world data, while prototyping, testing, and iterating in physical environments. The ideal candidate has strong foundations in VIO and sensor fusion, practical experience optimizing algorithms for embedded platforms, and familiarity with how modern deep learning is transforming perception.

Key job responsibilities

Design and implement Visual Inertial Odometry algorithms for robust real-time state estimation on robotic platforms like Sprout
Develop multi-sensor fusion pipelines integrating cameras, IMUs, and other sensing modalities for accurate pose tracking
Optimize perception and tracking algorithms for deployment on embedded hardware (e.g., ARM, GPU-accelerated edge devices) under strict latency and power constraints
Apply modern ML-based perception techniques (learned features, depth estimation, neural odometry) to complement and improve classical geometric approaches
Build and maintain calibration, evaluation, and benchmarking infrastructure for perception systems
Collaborate with hardware, controls, and navigation teams to integrate perception outputs into the robot’s autonomy stack
Lead technical projects from research prototyping through production deployment

Hands-on experience developing and deploying Visual Inertial Odometry or visual-inertial SLAM systems
Strong understanding of multi-sensor fusion (cameras, IMUs, odometry) and state estimation (EKF, factor graphs)
Experience optimizing perception algorithms for embedded or resource-constrained hardware
Demonstrated hands-on experience with real sensor data, calibration, and physical robot platforms

Publication record at major robotics or computer vision conferences (e.g., ICRA, IROS, RSS, CVPR, ECCV)
Experience with real-time systems programming and performance profiling on ARM/GPU platforms

Track record of shipping VIO or SLAM systems to production on physical robots at scale
Experience with NVIDIA Jetson, Qualcomm RB5, or similar embedded AI platforms

jobs.description:
Bring Clarity to Complexity

At Two Worlds Consulting, we help clients navigate complex social, environmental, and regulatory challenges by bringing together Indigenous Knowledge and Western science. Working collaboratively with First Nations, Métis, Inuit, industry, and the public sector, we support informed decision-making through practical, culturally grounded, and technically sound solutions.

We are seeking an Associate Principal, Portfolio Project Management
to provide project management leadership across our portfolio of small to medium-sized projects. The role balances direct management of individual projects with oversight of portfolio performance, resourcing, risk, and delivery outcomes.

The successful candidate will lead multidisciplinary teams in the delivery of human environment, archaeology, environmental, and related consulting services for a wide range of clients. Working closely with other Project Managers, Project Coordinators, Principals, and Associate Principals, they will monitor portfolio performance, identify and address emerging risks and resourcing needs, and help ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to a high standard of quality.

This position is well-suited to individuals who are confident Project Managers, thrive in collaborative and relationship-focused environments, and can balance hands-on project delivery with responsibility for the health and performance of a portfolio of work.

Compensation

$120,000 - $140,000 per year. Compensation is based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated expertise, with flexibility for exceptional candidates.

Location

Remote within Canada (home-based, with occasional travel). Hybrid or office-based options available for candidates located in Victoria or Vancouver, BC.

What You'll Do

Portfolio Management
Provide leadership and oversight for our portfolio of small to medium sized consulting projects, supporting successful delivery, effective resource utilization, financial performance, and a consistently high standard of client service.
Monitor portfolio performance and business-level portfolio health, including scope, schedule, budget, quality, capacity, utilization, backlog, revenue, margin, delivery risk, client relationship health, and alignment between current work, upcoming opportunities, and available resources.
Collaborate with Project Managers, Principals, and Directors to support prioritization, resource planning, workload management, and consistent delivery practices across the portfolio.
Develop and promote efficient project management practices, processes, reporting, and delivery standards across portfolio projects.
Support and mentor Project Managers, Principals, and other team members by sharing project management expertise and contributing to professional growth and development.
Foster a positive, collaborative team environment that supports engagement, accountability, learning, and recognition.

Project Management
Build and maintain positive client relationships focused on delivering high-quality services and fostering long-term partnerships across TWC service areas.
Develop proposals and support business development activities, including scope development, budgeting, resourcing, project planning, execution, and communication of project status and outcomes.
Manage project scope, budget, schedule, and quality.
Work with the Principals in Charge to lead project teams and provide direction and oversight of project activities to support successful project outcomes.
Maintain a strong understanding of TWC's service areas, project delivery approaches, relevant legislation, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
Ensure projects are delivered in alignment with client requirements, contractual obligations, corporate values, health and safety policies, and applicable regulatory standards.
Support timely invoicing, financial tracking, and client payment processes across assigned projects

What We're Looking For

We welcome applications from candidates who may not meet every qualification but bring relevant consulting experience, lived or professional insight, and a strong alignment with our work.

Required Qualifications
10+ years of progressively responsible project management experience in a consulting, professional services, or related environment, including responsibility for multiple concurrent projects or a portfolio of work with accountability for scope, budgets, schedules, resources, client relationships, and delivery outcomes.
Project management training, certification, or designation (e.g., PMP).
Experience delivering consulting services for Indigenous Nations, government, industry, or other clients in areas such as engagement, human environment, planning, stewardship, advisory services, environmental management, or related fields. 
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and working collaboratively with technical specialists, Project Managers, clients, and other stakeholders to deliver successful project outcomes.
Strong leadership, relationship-building, and communication skills, including experience mentoring team members, resolving challenges, and delivering exceptional client service.
Strong project and business management skills, including proposal development, budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, financial management, and risk mitigation.
Strong understanding of reconciliation and the diverse rights, priorities, perspectives, and governance structures of Indigenous Peoples in Canada.
Degree or diploma from an accredited post-secondary institution in a relevant discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and project management tools.
Alignment with TWC's values and principles, with the ability to thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced, and dynamic consulting environment.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience managing significant annual revenue portfolios and supporting resource planning and delivery oversight.
Experience working with geographically distributed or remote teams.
Indigenous lived experience that contributes to team-based, multi-lens project delivery and helps inform how Indigenous perspectives are collectively understood, represented, and integrated into consulting work.

About Two Worlds Consulting

Founded in 2016, Two Worlds Consulting supports clients across Canada through a multi-lens approach that respectfully brings together Indigenous Knowledge and Western scientific methods. Guided by respect, reciprocity, trust, and integrity, we are known for building strong relationships, delivering technical excellence, and helping clients and communities navigate complex decisions with confidence.

Our team works across sectors including mining, energy, infrastructure, transportation, government, and Indigenous community initiatives.

Learn more at twoworldsconsulting.com.

Key Areas

Environmental Consulting, Social Consulting, Project Management, Portfolio Management, Community and Culture, Human Environment, Engagement, Rights and Interests Assessment, Indigenous Knowledge, Socio-economic Services, Impact Assessment, Environmental Assessment, Policy, Planning, and Regulatory Processes.

jobs.description:
Take Your Environmental Career to the Next Level

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step into Your New Role

We are seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist / Ecologist
to join our EP&P team in our Sewickley, PA office.

Job Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will lead field teams in wetland delineations, prepare technical reports, prepare permitting applications to federal, state, and local entities, manage the environmental task in project schedules, and coordinate with internal and external groups to complete project tasks and goals. This is a client facing role, the candidate will be required to convey project related information to a variety of clients. The work will involve primarily technical writing for permitting, environmental task management, and leading field efforts including wetland delineations, site assessments, environmental inspections, endangered species surveys, habitat assessments, and other studies.

Position Requirements:

7-15 years of consulting experience.
Experience conducting wetland delineations in accordance with the USACE 1987 Wetland Delineation Manual and supporting Regional Supplements.
Excellent technical writing and verbal communication skills.
Comprehensive understanding and experience preparing of Section 404, 10, and 401WQC.
Knowledge of environmental laws and regulations, specifically pertaining to wetlands and listed wildlife species.
Ability to work flexible work schedules and availability to meet priority deadlines outside of normal working hours.
A valid driver's license.

Education & Certifications:

BS in an Environmental, Biological or Ecological Science, or Environmental Policy; Masters in a relevant field of study is a plus.
40-hour USACE wetland training.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

Plant and wildlife identification skills and survey and permitting protocols.
Excellent planning and organizational skills with strong problem-solving abilities and analytical skills.
Experience operating GPS units under ArcGIS or Terrasync programs.
Experience in ArcGIS or AutoCAD.
Ability to conduct work year-round in adverse climate and field conditions.
Ability to prioritize effort and effectively be engaged on multiple projects at one time.
Experience developing and completing Threatened and endangered species surveys, and coordination with the USFWS

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

Move Forward with Kleinfelder:
 Kleinfelder and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, has been connecting great people to the best work since 1961. We are engineers, scientists, and construction professionals providing solutions that improve our clients’ transportation, water, energy, and other private infrastructure. As a responsive, cross-disciplinary team of bright, curious, and innovative problem-solvers, we are dedicated to doing the right thing, every day, on every project from over 110 offices in the US, Canada, and Australia. Connecting great people to the best work is our purpose – together, we deliver. 

Progress with an Employer that Values You

Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, is an inclusive organization free from discrimination. We are a stronger organization when we are a diverse workforce and believe that through diversity, equity, and inclusion comes creativity, innovation, and unity. We are proud to offer the following: 

Benefits:
Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, offers an excellent compensation and benefits package, including: medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid holidays.

Career Development:
We are committed to investing in the professional development of our staff, offering each employee every opportunity to grow, develop, and take control of their career paths. We support these efforts through reimbursements for continuing education as well as many of the expenses associated with trainings and certifications, and opportunities for career development through our internal Mentoring Program.

Equal Opportunity:
Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Minorities/Women/Disabled/Veterans. (Compliant with the new VEVRAA and Section 503 rules) 

NOTICE TO THIRD PARTY AGENCIES

Please note that Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Recruitment Fee Agreement, Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, will not consider or agree to payment for any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without a previously signed agreement, Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resume, including those submitted to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of Kleinfelder.

jobs.title: Environmental Advisor
jobs.description:
Equans Data Centers are seeking to appoint an Environmental Advisor to support the growth in our data center sector.

Our commitment is to provide cutting edge solutions for our clients Data Center facilities. We are recruiting an Environmental Advisor to work with our project team to provide support our aim towards decarbonisation.

Based on the construction sites, the successful candidate will be the main point of contact for all Environmental management within the Data Center sites. This role will include regular travel to sites across the South.

What you will deliver?

Organise and arrange all site level environmental monitoring, measurement and reporting for all regulatory, compliance and business purposes
Assist with the delivery of central carbon reduction targets for projects
Implement waste reduction plans involving circular economy and waste diversion resulting in waste prevention
Embed Sustainable practices on site delivering training and toolbox talks and support the identification and implementation of preventative measures
Assist the project teams to achieve BREEAM/LEED rating and certification when required
Provide guidance and ensure that Project Teams are effectively managing all relevant environmental aspects to reduce risk on site
Act as a site level advisor on business related local and national environmental regulatory requirements
Monitor and report on our environmental performance and regularly undertake site level inspections
Assist in the preparation and review of project environmental documents
Assist the Project Teams in the management and investigation of environmental incidents
Complete regular internal environmental reports highlighting site performance against current KPI’s
Collaborate with the central Environmental & Sustainability team in driving the environmental agenda by improving performance across the data center business area and companywide though written communications.
Upskill and support teams, acting as a facilitator when delivering site based environmental training
When required, act as an advisor to clients for any environmentally related issues or activities
Review and discuss internal environmental reports highlighting site performance against current KPI’s
Ensure that sites have all correct permits and licences for conducting any activities that have an environmental impact.

What we can offer you?

On offer is a competitive salary and benefits package, which includes;

25 days annual leave (+ public holidays)
Life Cover equivalent to 4 times annual salary
Company Stakeholder Pension Scheme
Private Medical Insurance
2 corporate social responsibility days per year
Broad range of learning opportunities, such as professional qualifications, collective/individual training, and personalised support programmes
Attractive Employee Referral Rewards Scheme
Access to our growing employee networks including AccessAbility (representing those with physical and mental disabilities), Encompass (representing the LGBTQ+ community), RISE (representing people from ethnic backgrounds), Veterans & Reservists, WOMEN TOGETHER (representing women in Equans), Working Parents, and Young Professionals.
24/7 Employee Assistance Program and access to mental wellbeing app

Who are we looking for?

Previous experience as an Environmental Advisor or similar role
Knowledge of the application of ISO14001
Technical familiarity with environmental processes and assessments e.g. BREEAM/LEED knowledge and Advisory Professional certification
Strong background in assessment of environmental hazards and understanding of the mechanisms of how to mitigate
Ability to work independently and be self-motivated
High level of personal drive and commitment with the desire to progress
Effective communication skills with the ability to build relationships across all levels of the organisation.
Competent report writing skills
Professional and pragmatic team player who can build and sustain effective working relationships
Degree qualification in a relevant discipline e.g. Environmental Management /Sciences or Sustainability, with professional body membership (IEMA, IES or CIEEM) preferred
Practitioner Membership with IEMA or similar professional membership, or working towards would be advantageous
Experience of the Construction or a related industry would be desirable
Willingness and ability to travel nationally across projects

Who are we?

Equans Data Centers is a strategic data centre partner. We deliver the whole data centre, providing full general contracting for hyperscaler and colocation data centre projects across Europe, through a single point of contact.

Leveraging Bouygues Energies & Services and Equans Group' experiences, we provide expertise in construction and engineering, global standardisation, precision localisation and total control of the supply chain. This enables us to deliver data centres with the best possible quality, speed to delivery and high repeatability and scalability – to realise client needs for cost transparency, low risk, continual availability, innovation and certainty of planning and outcomes.

With more than 1,200 highly skilled employees across 8 European countries, Equans Data Centres has delivered over 400,000m2 of data halls, exceeding 640MW of IT space for major data centres providers such as VIRTUS Data Centers, Digital Reality, Equinix, Vantage Data Centers, Stack Infrastructure, Data4 and many others.

What’s next?

If this role is of interest to you, please click below to register, apply, and track your progress! A member of our Resourcing Team will review your application and be in touch. 

As part our commitment to better reflect the markets within which we operate, we encourage applications from women, ethnically diverse individuals and people with disabilities, along with all candidates who identify with protected characteristic groups under the Equality Act 2010.

At Equans we’re committed to delivering a culture where everyone’s voice is heard and supported. We know the value a diverse workforce creates, delivering better results for our people, customers, and stakeholders. Diversity and inclusion is at the core of what we do, should you join Equans you’ll find a welcoming and open workplace where you’re supported and encouraged to be your true self at work.

You’ll also have access to our growing employee networks including AccessAbility (representing those with physical and mental disabilities), Encompass (representing the LGBTQ+ community), RISE (representing people from ethnic backgrounds), Veterans & Reservists, WOMEN Together (representing women in Equans), Working Parents, and Young Professionals.

For this role, you must have evidence of the right to work in the UK. Unfortunately, we are not able to offer a re-location package with this job role.  Certain roles may require applicants to undergo a Disclosure check, as noted in the role requirements.

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Our Environmental group is looking for an Environmental Scientist
to join their team! As a graduate with this group, you will be engaged with projects that involve wetland delineations/assessments & permitting, endangered species surveys, water quality assessments, and ecological & environmental studies. These projects support ecological risk assessments, site characterization and remedial action projects on contaminated sites.

Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Wetland delineation
Field surveys for rare, threatened or endangered flora and fauna and their habitats
Ecological assessments to classify and map habitat cover types and plant communities
Surface water quality monitoring and sampling
Sediment sampling
Macroinverterate surveys / sampling
Fish, reptile and amphibian surveys
Managing and evaluating chemical and biological data
Evaluating and understanding environmental regulations
Preparing work plans, reports and other written communications

Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Biology, Ecology or related field of study
0-2 years of experience conducting wetland delineations and ecological field studies
Proficiency with managing and evaluating chemical and biological data using spreadsheets or database software

: Geospatial Business Development Specialist - Southern California
Territory:
Irvine/Orange County, Inland Empire & San Diego

Build Your Career. Own Your Territory. Grow With Us.

AeroTech Mapping, Inc. is seeking a motivated, relationship-driven Geospatial Business Development Specialist to lead business development efforts throughout Los Angeles County and Southern California.

This is an opportunity for an ambitious sales professional who wants the freedom to manage their own territory, build lasting client relationships, and directly influence their income and career growth. We are not looking for someone who requires constant direction; we are looking for a self-starter who thrives in a flexible, remote work environment and takes ownership of their success.

·      Identify, pursue, and secure new business opportunities within assigned markets and territories
·      Build and maintain relationships with engineering firms, government agencies, utilities, developers, and other industry stakeholders
·      Promote AeroTech Mapping's aerial mapping, LiDAR, surveying, orthophotography, GIS, remote sensing, and geospatial solutions

·      Monitor market trends, industry developments, and competitor activity
·      Manage and grow existing client relationships while continually developing new opportunities
·      Serve as a trusted advisor to clients throughout the project lifecycle

What Makes This Opportunity Different

·      Remote and flexible work environment
·      High degree of autonomy and trust
·      Established reputation with over 20 years in the geospatial industry
·      Strong technical support team allowing you to focus on relationship building and sales
·      Opportunity to grow your territory and income
·      Long-term career path with leadership potential
·      Collaborative culture that values initiative and accountability over micromanagement

What We're Looking For

·      3+ years of business development, sales, account management, or client relationship experience
·      Proven ability to develop and maintain professional relationships
·      Strong communication, presentation, and networking skills
·      Self-starter with excellent time management and organizational skills
·      Ability to work independently while remaining connected to a remote team
·      Experience using CRM systems such as Salesforce or similar platforms
·      Willingness to travel throughout assigned territories as needed

·      Understanding of aerial mapping, LiDAR, GIS, surveying, remote sensing, or related technologies
·      Experience responding to proposals, RFQs, or public agency procurement processes
·      Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Geography, Engineering, GIS, Surveying, or a related field
·      Ability to travel throughout Southern California for client meetings, industry events, and conferences

The Ideal Candidate

·      Entrepreneurial and motivated by achieving goals
·      Comfortable working independently without constant supervision
·      Naturally curious and relationship-driven
·      Competitive, resilient, and energized by creating opportunities
·      Looking for a long-term career rather than a short-term job
·      Interested in becoming a recognized industry professional and trusted client advisor

·      Medical, dental, and vision insurance

·      Paid holidays and PTO
·      Professional development and industry training

·      Remote work flexibility

jobs.title: Environmental & Safety Professional
jobs.description:
Description

Leidos’ NISC IV Program (National Airspace System Integration Support Contract) is one of the largest and oldest programs supporting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and we have an exciting career opportunity for an Environmental & Safety Professional to support the FAA with the goal of providing outstanding customer service to the Environmental Occupational Safety and Health (EOSH) Program.

In general, this person will be a part of a larger team of EOSH professionals that supports the FAA’s Eastern Service Area. The candidate will responsible for supporting many multi-faceted EOSH programs, and will be required to maintain applicable training and certification requirements as necessary. These programs include (but are not limited to) Asbestos, Lead, Mold, Chemical Management, Emergency Response, Electrical Safety, Water, Fuel Storage Tanks, and Fall Protection. The candidate will provide direct support to multi-level customers.

Remote with up to 50% travel. Report to customer site as needed.

Must be located in the Fayetteville or Raleigh/Durham, NC areas.

Specifically, the chosen candidate will have experience in writing reports with strict reporting deadlines. This includes extensive experience sampling and interpreting analytical reports and being able to identify exceedances in those reports. The selected candidate will also have experience climbing towers and/or be capable of receiving and giving fall protection training as well as completing tower safety inspections. The selected candidate must be able to provide comprehensive technical EOSH training to employees as requested. The selected candidate must have excellent customer service skills necessary to interact with senior level management and internal and external customers, as well as foster an environment of cooperation between different departments and co-workers. The chosen applicant must be a self-starter, able to work independently and with minimum supervision. This is a full time position that requires up to 75 percent travel. Overnight travel will be required in many instances. This position will be at the customer site in Memphis as requested.

Primary Responsibilities

Provide environmental and safety support to the FAA’s EOSH Programs. The primary programs are Indoor Air Quality (IAQ); Asbestos Management; Lead Management (paint); Polychlorinated Biphenyls Management; Chemical/Hazardous Waste Management; Pesticide Management; Drinking Water Management; Fuel Storage Tank Management; Fall Protection Program; Hearing Safety Program; Electrical Safety Program; Confined Space Program; and Radiation Program. Additionally, the candidate will be required to employ and be familiar with a wide variety of sampling instrumentation, sampling techniques.
Conduct site inspections and surveys, and submit proper technical reports conveying findings and sound guidance to resolve/mitigate any EOSH issues.
Manage inspections using electronic data; utilize on-line data storage locations; and be able to use all Microsoft programs.
Research and interpret Federal, State, Local, and FAA rules and regulations that are applicable to EOSH Programs.
Provide excellent problem-solving and customer service skills.

Basic Qualifications/Experience

Requires Bachelors degree and 2+ years of prior relevant experience or Masters degree and relevant experience.
Environmental, health and safety experience.
Proven experience with various types of EOSH field equipment (ex. PID, XRF, Dosimeter, etc.).
Proficient in obtaining and developing Asbestos samples & reports.
Experience in conducting and developing indoor air quality (IAQ) samples & reports.
Technical competence in surveying and developing Fall Protection issues & reports as well as Electrical Safety issues and reports.
Proficient in obtaining and developing Drinking Water samples and reports.
Must be strong in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and Microsoft Project.
Must be able to work, manage and maintain information stored in a Knowledge Sharing Network (KSN)/SharePoint site(s).
Candidate must also have a reliable vehicle.
Ability to obtain and maintain Public Trust Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Undergraduate Degree in Environmental Science, Occupational Safety & Health, or similar degree.
Master Degree in Occupational Safety & Health, Environmental Science or Environmental Engineering
Certified Safety Professional.
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager.
